Ich sehne mich sehr, dich zu sehen und gedenke deiner Tränen, damit ich voll Freude sei; Ich erinnere mich an den ungeheuchelten Glauben, der in dir ist und zuerst in deiner Großmutter Loïs und deiner Mutter Eunike wohnte; und ich bin überzeugt, dass er auch in dir ist. Darum ermahne ich dich, das Gnadengeschenk Gottes anzufachen, das in dir ist durch die Auflegung meiner Hände. Denn Gott hat uns nicht gegeben den Geist der Furcht, sondern der Kraft und der Liebe und der Besonnenheit – 2. Timotheus 1:4-7.

„O Gott, gib uns Mütter wie Eunike und Großmütter wie Loïs. Gib uns Frauen, die Frauen des Glaubens sind. Gib uns Frauen, die wissen, wie sie für die Wahrheit einstehen gegen die Flut menschlicher Rationalisierung, die das Leben so vieler gutmeinender Menschen zerstört. Gib uns Frauen, die in ihrer Treue zu Jesus Christus, zu ihren Ehemännern und zu ihrer Berufung, den Geist Jesu im ganzen Leben darzustellen, unerschütterlich sind. Amen.“

Die Geschichte hat gezeigt, dass Frauen ebenso einflussreich sind wie Männer bei der Gestaltung des Gefüges der Gesellschaft und der christlichen Gemeinschaft. Man könnte argumentieren, dass ihr Einfluss noch größer ist, wenn man bedenkt, dass sie eine bedeutende Rolle bei der Prägung der Werte kleiner Kinder spielen und, ob sie sich nun züchtig kleiden und verhalten oder nicht, sie die Moral großer Massen von Männern um sie herum beeinflussen können.

Daher der Ruf an Frauen, Frauen des Glaubens zu sein. Nicht nur beeinflusst der Glaube einer Frau die Menschen um sie herum, sondern jede Frau hat ihren eigenen persönlichen Weg. Ihr Weg ist die Suche nach Identität, Sicherheit und Sinn für ihr Leben.

Die Frauen von heute werden von Stimmen überflutet, die behaupten, die Erfüllung anzubieten, die ihr Herz begehrt. Wie bei ihrer Mutter Eva sprechen viele dieser Stimmen ihren weiblichen Geist an, aber wie ihre Mutter Eva entdeckte, führt es, wenn es nicht die Stimme Gottes ist, zu Tod und Zerstörung.

Die Bibel ist reich an Berichten über Frauen, die aus Glauben lebten. Denken wir an die Hure Raab. Bibelwissenschaftler sind sich nicht einig, ob sie diesen Titel verdiente, aber so ist sie uns überliefert. Sie hörte die Geschichten vom Gott Israels. Als sie auf die Spione traf und deren düstere Vorhersage für ihre Stadt hörte, entschied sie sich zu glauben.

Sie stammte aus Jericho. Jericho war ihre Heimat. Jericho hatte hohe Steinmauern und tapfere Verteidiger. Sie hätte viele Gründe gehabt, ihren Glauben auf das zu setzen, was ihr vertraut war und was sie in der Vergangenheit erhalten hatte.

Sie entschied sich, ihren Glauben auf den Gott Israels zu setzen. Die Männer Israels sagten ihr, wenn sie einen scharlachroten Faden aus ihrem Fenster an der Mauer hängen würde, würden ihr Haus und ihr Leben verschont bleiben. Ein scharlachroter Faden. Nicht viel an Identität oder Sicherheit, aber Raab hängte ihren Glauben an einen scharlachroten Faden. Dieser scharlachrote Faden stellte die Macht des Gottes Israels dar und, wie wir heute wissen, ist er ein schönes Symbol des Blutes Jesu.

Der Ruf, eine Frau des Glaubens zu sein, ist ein Ruf, sich von der Ideologie der Welt abzuwenden und das anzunehmen, was in den Augen der Welt ein vergebliches Heilmittel ist—einen scharlachroten Faden. Raabs Glaube wurzelte in ihrer Kenntnis des Gottes Israels und seines Plans, ihr Volk zu richten. Der scharlachrote Faden war ihre Hoffnung auf Rettung.

Ich möchte, dass wir betrachten, wie der Glaube an Gott die primären Sehnsüchte des weiblichen Herzens beeinflusst. Jede Frau sehnt sich nach Identität, Sicherheit und Sinn. Jesus ist gekommen, um diese Sehnsucht des Herzens zu erfüllen.

Identität – „Wer bin ich?“

Dies ist eine Frage, die jeder irgendwann im Leben zu stellen gezwungen ist—oft in der Adoleszenz. Junge Männer neigen dazu, ihre Identität auf der Grundlage dessen zu formen, wen sie bewundern und auf ihre beruflichen Neigungen. Junge Frauen, besonders in unseren täuferischen Gemeinden, sind weitgehend den prominenten Männern in ihrem Leben ausgeliefert, wenn es darum geht, ihre Identität zu definieren.

Das ist nicht rein kulturell. Als Gott zu Eva sagte: …dein Verlangen wird sich auf deinen Mann richten, und er wird über dich herrschen – 1. Mose 3:16, verkündete er, dass sie und ihre weiblichen Nachkommen sich an den Mann wenden würden, um einen wesentlichen Teil ihrer Natur zu definieren.

Väter spielen eine Schlüsselrolle in der frühen Entwicklung der Identität eines kleinen Mädchens. Missbrauchende Väter, abwesende Väter und gleichgültige Väter hinterlassen kleine Mädchen, die unsicher sind, wer sie sind oder welchen Wert sie als Person haben. Ein Vater, der die gottgegebene Weiblichkeit seiner Tochter bestätigt, schenkt ihr ein unschätzbares Gut. Damit meine ich, ihre Eigenschaften weiblicher Tugend zu loben, sie für Bemühungen um Keuschheit und Bescheidenheit zu segnen und ja, ihr zu sagen, dass sie schön ist.

Das Herz einer Frau wird sich letztlich einem Ehemann zuwenden. Gott sagte: „Dein Verlangen wird sich auf deinen Mann richten“, nicht auf deinen Vater. Die meisten Frauen heiraten in der Erwartung, endlich ihren „Retter“ gefunden zu haben, und das ist berechtigt. Hat Paulus in Epheser 5 nicht gesagt, dass der Ehemann „der Retter des Leibes“ sei? Sollte eine Frau nicht erwarten, von ihrem Mann Liebe, Bestätigung, Schutz und Versorgung zu erhalten? Dies steht ihr kraft göttlichen Gebots zu. Ein gottesfürchtiger Ehemann wird alles in seiner Macht Stehende tun, ihr dies in dieser Weise zu gewähren.

„Dein Verlangen wird sich auf deinen Mann richten“ steht im Kontext des Falls. Es war eine der Folgen des Falls. Es ist eine Aussage ohne die Zusicherung der Erfüllung. Das lässt uns glauben, dass, obwohl durch Verlangen getrieben, dieses Verlangen unerfüllt bleiben kann.

Was soll eine Frau tun, wenn ihr Mann nicht bereit oder nicht imstande ist, die Sehnsucht ihres Herzens zu befriedigen? Was, wenn eine Frau keinen Mann hat? Sie muss eine Frau des Glaubens werden. Solange eine Frau ihre Identität nicht in Jesus gefunden hat, wird kein Mann in der Lage sein, die tiefsten Sehnsüchte ihres Herzens zu erfüllen.

Viele Ehen leiden, weil die Frau erwartet, dass ihr Mann die tiefen Sehnsüchte ihres Herzens erfüllt, die nur Jesus erfüllen kann. Viele Männer fühlen sich unzulänglich und ziehen sich zurück, wenn von ihnen erwartet wird, für ihre Frau das zu sein und zu tun, was nur Jesus tun kann.

Aufruf an alle Frauen, Frauen des Glaubens zu sein

Frauen des Glaubens sind Frauen, die wissen, wer sie in Christus Jesus sind. Sie haben die tiefsten Sehnsüchte ihres weiblichen Herzens in ihm erfüllt gefunden. Weil ihre Herzenssehnsüchte befriedigt sind, sind sie zu einer Quelle des Lebens für ihren Mann, für ihre Kinder und für andere geworden.

Sicherheit – „Wer wird mich beschützen?“

Frau zu sein war schon immer riskant. Frauen sind sehr verletzlich. Neben der Tatsache, dass sie körperlich zarter sind, sind Frauen anfälliger für emotionale Schwankungen, und ich glaube, basierend auf dem, was die Bibel zur Täuschung Evas sagt, dass Frauen eher anfällig für geistliche Täuschung sind (siehe 1. Timotheus 2:14).

Das macht sie nicht den Männern unterlegen. Ihre emotionale Sensibilität macht sie empfänglicher für die vielen Realitäten zwischenmenschlicher Probleme als viele Männer. Darin kann ihre Einsicht etwas Positives sein und dazu beitragen, uns Männer in einigen unserer natürlichen Schwächen auszugleichen. Welche Vergleiche wir auch immer anstellen mögen, ich denke, wir können uns alle einig sein, dass Frauen den Schutz brauchen, den Männer bieten.

Was ist, wenn der Mann, der dich schützen sollte, ein Feigling ist? Wir haben ein Beispiel für eine solche Situation in der Bibel. Der Mann heißt Abraham—ja… der Vater des Glaubens. Selbst starke Männer treffen manchmal feige Entscheidungen.

Abraham und Sarah reisten nach Ägypten. Als sie Ägypten näher kamen, wurde Abraham um sein Leben fürchtend. Seine Frau Sarah war eine schöne Frau und Abraham wusste, dass Ägypten eine heidnische Nation mit sehr laschen Sitten war. Er fürchtete, dass die Ägypter ihn töten würden, um seine Frau zu nehmen. Abraham sprach zu Sarah: Sage doch, du bist meine Schwester, damit es mir um deinetwillen wohl ergehe und mir mein Leben durch dich erhalten bleibe – 1. Mose 12:13.

Sarah war in der Tat Abrahams Halbschwester. Sie hatten denselben Vater, aber nicht dieselbe Mutter. Abrahams Notfallplan brachte Sarah in eine sehr schwierige Lage. Wir lesen nichts über Sarahs Reaktion auf Abrahams Plan. Alles, was wir wissen, ist, dass …Sara gehorsam war Abraham und nannte ihn „Herr“: ihr seid seine Töchter, solange ihr Gutes tut und euch nicht von Furcht einschüchtern lasst – 1. Petrus 3:6.

Es scheint, dass Sarah keine Furcht hatte. Ihr Glaube hing nicht von Abrahams Schutz ab. Sie vertraute auf eine höhere Macht. Sarahs Glaube brachte ihr einen Platz in der Glaubenshalle in Hebräer 11 und machte sie zu Petrus’ Beispiel dafür, wie Ehefrauen zu ihren Ehemännern in Beziehung stehen sollen.

Der Kern dieser Geschichte liegt im Ausgang. Wegen Sarahs Glauben wurde sie aus der Hand des Pharao gerettet, des mächtigsten Herrschers der damaligen Welt. Es war Sarahs Glaube, nicht Abrahams, der sie beschützte.

Frauen wenden sich wegen Sicherheit an Männer, und das ist richtig so. Männer schützen ihre Frauen so gut sie können. Ich glaube, wenn Männer und Frauen in ihren gottgegebenen Rollen leben, gibt es viel Schutz und Sicherheit; doch wir leben in einer gefallenen Welt. Wir erfüllen unsere Rollen nicht immer ehrenhaft und manchmal lässt Gott auch das Böse über die Frommsten kommen.

Aufruf an alle Frauen, Frauen des Glaubens zu sein, wie Sarah

Hast du den Glauben zu glauben, dass Gott größer ist als dein Ehemann oder dein Vater? Bist du bereit, Gott zu vertrauen, dass er eingreift, wo dein Mann schwach ist oder sogar gegen Gott oder die Gemeinde rebellisch ist?

Eine Frau des Glaubens ist eine Frau, die wählt, Gott auch dann zu vertrauen, wenn kein vernünftiger Weg nach vorn erkennbar ist. Eine Frau des Glaubens tut weiterhin das Richtige, obwohl es vielleicht kein Weg garantierter Sicherheit ist, denn …der Herr ist mein Helfer, ich will mich nicht fürchten; was kann mir ein Mensch tun? – Hebräer 13:6.

Sinn – „Warum bin ich hier?“

Das ist eine Frage, die jeder irgendwann im Leben stellt. Wir wollen, dass unser Leben Sinn und Zweck hat. Die Sinnlosigkeit eines bedeutungslosen Lebens treibt Männer und Frauen in Depression und Verzweiflung. Zielgerichtet zu leben segnet uns und andere und bringt Ehre unserem Schöpfer.

Wenn Männer daran denken, zielgerichtet zu leben, stellen sie sich vor… einen Kampf zu führen, einen Berg zu bezwingen, ein edles Ziel anzustreben. Wir Männer tendieren dazu, visionsorientiert und zielgerichtet zu sein.

Was bedeutet es für eine Frau, zielgerichtet zu leben?

Lukas gibt uns dazu Einsicht im Bericht von Jesu Besuch im Haus von Maria und Martha. (Siehe Lukas 10:38-42) Jesus hielt sich häufig in diesem Haus auf, wenn er durch Bethanien zog. Hier wusste er, dass er große Gastfreundschaft und anregende Gespräche finden würde. Heute war keine Ausnahme.

Als er sich in ihrem Gemach ausruhte, saß Maria zu seinen Füßen, stellte Fragen und lauschte aufmerksam, während er ihr den Sinn seines Lebens und sein zukünftiges Schicksal offenbarte. Maria verstand Dinge über Jesus, die selbst seine Jünger nicht begriffen hatten.

Matthäus berichtet, dass als Jesus im Hause Simons speiste, eine Frau, von der man annahm, sie sei Maria von Bethanien, eintrat, sich niederkniete und Jesus’ Füße mit teurem Öl salbte. Als die Jünger sich über „diese Verschwendung“ beschwerten, sagte Jesus zu ihnen: Denn sie hat diesen Duft auf meinen Leib ausgegossen, damit er begraben werde – Matthäus 26:12.

Woher hatte Maria dieses Verständnis? War es nicht, als sie „zu Jesu Füßen saß“?

Martha hingegen war „sehr mit dem Dienst beschäftigt“. Nun musste Jesus essen. Jemand musste das Essen zubereiten, und ich bin sicher, dass Jesus Marthas köstliche Zubereitungen genoss. Aber Jesus tadelte sie mit „Martha, Martha“. Beachte den familiären Ton in seiner Stimme.

Er verurteilte sie nicht. Er forderte sie heraus, Zeit für die wichtigen Dinge im Leben zu nehmen. Er rühmte Maria, denn sie …hat den guten Anteil erwählt, der ihr nicht genommen werden wird – Lukas 10:42.

Ich möchte vorschlagen, dass die meisten unserer Ängste selbstgemacht sind. Wir setzen Ziele für unser Leben, die Jesus nie verlangt hat. Wir legen uns Erwartungen auf, die keinen ewigen Wert haben. Wie Martha sorgen wir uns um Belangloses und zerstören Beziehungen über triviale Dinge. Ja, das Abendessen muss serviert werden, und Maria sollte helfen, aber nicht so, dass sie den „besseren Teil“ vernachlässigt.

Aufruf an alle Frauen, Frauen des Glaubens zu sein wie Maria, die liebte, bei Jesu Füßen zu verweilen

Das Leben für eine Ehefrau und Mutter ist voll drängender Anforderungen. Entschärfe dein Leben von Stress und Angst, indem du Zeit damit verbringst, auf die Stimme Jesu zu hören—diese „leise, sanfte Stimme“, die Elija schließlich hörte.

Stress und Angst schmelzen in der Gegenwart Jesu dahin. Gott spricht zu uns durch seinen Heiligen Geist durch sein Wort. Wenn es für dich eine Herausforderung ist, Zeit zu finden, um dich mit deiner Bibel hinzusetzen, dann kannst du deinen Geist beruhigen mit den Händen im Spülwasser, oder beim Wäschefalten, oder während du erneut eine Mahlzeit für deine Familie zubereitest. In solchen Zeiten kannst du Gemeinschaft mit Gott haben. Du kannst zu deinem Vater im Himmel beten. Du kannst Dinge sagen wie: „Ich liebe dich, Herr Jesus, sprich zu mir durch dein Wort, bring Frieden in meine Seele; beruhige die Kämpfe meines Denkens; hilf mir, in deine Ruhe einzutreten; gib mir deinen Frieden.“ Dann kannst du lauschen, wie sein Geist deinen Geist mit Wahrheiten aus der Schrift anstößt, die in deinem Herzen verborgen sind.

Zusammenfassung – Aufruf an alle Frauen, Frauen des Glaubens zu sein

Für dein eigenes Wohlbefinden:

Frauen werden heute von Selbsthilferessourcen in Form von Büchern, Podcasts, sozialen Medien und Seminaren bombardiert. Vieles davon ist gut und kann hilfreich sein, aber nichts ersetzt eine persönliche Beziehung und ein tägliches Wandeln mit Jesus.

Für das Wohl deiner Kinder:

Heute mehr denn je brauchen wir Mütter, die Frauen des Glaubens sind und ihren Kindern vermitteln können, dass das Wandeln mit Gott real und erfüllend ist. Der junge Timotheus wurde durch den ungeheuchelten Glauben seiner Mutter und seiner Großmutter beeinflusst. Unterschätze niemals die Wirkung deines Lebens auf die Leben derer, die dir folgen.

Für die Stärke deines Mannes:

Männer brauchen heute die Unterstützung treuer Frauen, besonders ihrer Ehefrau. Das tägliche Wandeln eines Mannes kann durch die Frau in seinem Leben gestärkt oder geschwächt werden. Es heißt: „Hinter jedem erfolgreichen Mann steht eine Frau.“ Ein Mann wird in hohem Maße zum Guten oder zum Schlechten von den Frauen in seinem Leben beeinflusst.

Zum Wohle der Gemeinde:

Frau des Glaubens, die Gemeinde braucht dich. Frauen bringen eine Gnade in die Gemeinde, die dringend nötig ist. Deine Gebete werden gebraucht. Dein Zeugnis ermutigt. Dein Lied bewegt unsere Herzen. Dein Lächeln gibt Hoffnung. Dein friedliches, freudiges Antlitz einer Seele, die in Jesus Ruhe gefunden hat, ist ein Einfluss, den in dieser Welt nur wenig übertrifft.

As sisters in the Lord and born-again believers, I am sure we would all agree that memorizing scripture is important to our spiritual health. I have memorized many, many Scripture verses during my childhood years. Most of the verses that I memorized were taught during a vacation Bible School which I attended each summer.

During the first evening of Bible School, the teachers handed out memory work assignments, often many pages worth. These were not all required but the rewards were appealing. Most years I memorized everything that was assigned. I give these teachers and this Bible School the credit for the wealth of verses I memorized during those years.

Now I am married and have children of my own. The Bible School from my childhood is long past. I realized that if my children were going to memorize Scripture, I would need to make it happen. As moms, many of us know the importance of memorizing God’s Word and hiding it, not only in our hearts, but also in our children’s hearts.

Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments. Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee –Psalm 119:9-11.

We need God’s Word in our hearts to help us with our daily battles with sin. Our children need this as well. Most of our children are not going to memorize scripture without some help from us.

My husband and I did not enter marriage with dreams of memorizing with our children. For our family, it happened almost accidentally. Our oldest children were three and four when my husband suggested that we work with them on memorizing the Christmas story found in Luke 2:1-19. I didn’t think they would be able to do it. I thought young children memorized short verses like, “Be ye kind one to another.” We started reciting it together every evening during our family devotions. I was quite surprised when they memorized this passage quickly and easily.

I was intrigued. Should we try again? Easter was approaching so I started working with them on the crucifixion account found in John 19:1-19. Again, they memorized this without much effort. This encouraged me to continue with other passages.

When it came time to homeschool the children, I wanted memorization to be a part of our daily routine. I bought a binder and inserted the printed passages we had memorized as well as the passages I wanted them to memorize. This started a routine that we still do today.

Every day we recite the current passage as well as one we have previously memorized. We also recite it together as a family during our devotion time. I have found that doing it this way results in the family having the passage memorized in about three to four weeks.

At the beginning of a new passage, I read the scripture out loud. As the days go by the children start chiming in more and more. Eventually, I just get them started and only help as they need help. When I think they know the passage I have them recite it to me one by one. If they know it well, they start reciting it to their dad during our family devotions. If they don’t know it, we keep on practicing till they do know it. Sometimes I will give the struggling child just a few verses to recite. However, most of them would rather recite the whole thing.

We memorize as a family instead of individually. I don’t move on to a new passage until everyone has it memorized or at least memorized to their ability. (Not all children can memorize 19 verses at age three.) Some of our children were barely talking at three years old so verbal Bible memory was hardly possible. Some children will stumble through a passage and need lots of clue words, which is okay if they are doing their best. Sometimes we go over the same passage again in a few years and they learn it better the second time.

This may sound time-consuming and stressful, but it is not so for us. I spend about five minutes a day working on memory work. We have no time constraints on our memorization so there is no pressure to know it by a certain time. The children have been doing this since they were barely talking, so they are used to it and rarely complain. Since we memorize as a family, it also helps the child who can’t memorize as well as another. As a family, we encourage and cheer on the struggling child. He feels a sense of accomplishment even if he struggles through the whole passage.

I give a small reward for each passage memorized. I have a prize box that they can choose from. This does not need to cost much! I often do not spend much more than a dollar. Yard sales and thrift stores are places to purchase items cheaply. Back-to-school sales are nice as well since most children like to have a new pack of crayons or a cute eraser.

As time went by, I found myself becoming discouraged at how quickly the children would forget a memorized passage. I discovered that several years later they often could hardly recite a previously learned passage. I wondered why I was putting in the effort if they were simply going to forget it in a few years. My husband encouraged me to continue. He said that the concepts were still in their hearts even if they could no longer recite the passage. So I continued, but I still hoped for a solution to this problem.

One day I read an article written by another mom who also worked on memorization with her children. In the article she said that it is important to get the memory work out of the short-term memory and into the long-term memory. The solution is actually quite simple. Every day in addition to reciting our new passage, we also recite a previously learned passage. My binder comes in handy for this! All the passages we have learned are in this binder. I use a paper clip to help me remember the passage we just reviewed. Each day the paper clip moves to the next passage. When we reach the end, we start over. This helps to keep the passages fresh in our minds as well as move them to our long-term memory.

I also like to have a theme for each school year. One year my theme was, “Memorize 100 Verses.” The children enjoyed watching the number rise as the year progressed. This year we are working on, “The Sermon on the Mount.” I divided it into 10 sections. The goal is to complete it in a year, but if we don’t reach that goal it doesn’t matter. It is better to go slow and memorize something well than to go fast and not retain what you have learned.

These are the methods I have found helpful for our family. Pray and ask God for ideas that will work well for your family without comparing yourself to other families! Don’t underestimate what your children can do. Don’t assume that because they are young, they can only memorize a verse or two. Children often do only as well as we expect them to, even the younger ones.

After we have God’s Word memorized, we need to use it daily. A blanket that is kept stored away in a closet does no good on a cold, winter night. The writer of Deuteronomy sums this up well—And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up –Deuteronomy 6:5-7.

First, we love God. Then we put His Word into our hearts. Finally, we should teach these truths to our children as we go about our daily activities. This passage encompasses it all—sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up. After a passage is memorized, my husband will explain the verses to us during our devotion time. This helps us to understand what we are memorizing.

We do many things by habit because we realize their importance. We brush our teeth, comb our hair, eat breakfast, and do many other things. We do these things daily. They are a regular part of our lives. Because we value them, we make them happen. This is how it should be with scripture memorization. It is too valuable to skip.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper –Psalm 1:1-3.

When we delight in God’s Word, we will be glad to take time to memorize scripture, and the memorized Word will then bear fruit in its season.

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not –Galatians 6:9.

As susters in die Here en wedergebore gelowiges, is ek seker ons sal almal saamstem dat die memorisering van Skrif belangrik is vir ons geestelike gesondheid. Ek het baie, baie Skrifverse in my kinderjare uit die hooft geleer. Die meeste van die verse wat ek gememoriseer het, is tydens ’n vakansiebybelkool aangeleer wat ek elke somer bygewoon het.

Tydens die eerste aand van Bybelkool het die onderwysers geheuewerk-opdragte uitgedeel, dikwels bladsye vol. Dit was nie alles verpligtend nie, maar die belonings was aantreklik. Meestal het ek al die toegewese werk memoriseer. Ek gee hierdie onderwysers en die Bybelkool krediet vir die rykdom van verse wat ek in daardie jare memoriseer het.

Nou is ek getroud en het my eie kinders. Die Bybelkool van my kinderjare is lank verby. Ek het besef dat as my kinders Skrif sou memoriseer, ek dit sal moet laat gebeur. As moeders weet baie van ons die belangrikheid daarvan om God se Woord te memoriseer en dit nie net in ons eie harte weg te steek nie, maar ook in ons kinders se harte.

Hoe sal ’n jongman sy weg suiwer? Deur dit na te vors volgens u woord. Met my hele hart het ek U gesoek; laat my nie van u gebooie afdwale nie. U woord het ek in my hart verberg, sodat ek nie teen U sal oortree nie –Psalm 119:9-11.

Ons het God se Woord in ons harte nodig om ons te help met ons daaglikse stryde teen sonde. Ons kinders het dit ook nodig. Die meeste van ons kinders gaan nie Skrif memoriseer sonder ’n mate van hulp van ons nie.

My man en ek het nie met die droom getrou om saam met ons kinders te memoriseer nie. Vir ons familie het dit byna per ongeluk gebeur. Ons oudste kinders was drie en vier toe my man voorgestel het dat ons met hulle werk aan die Kersverhaal in Lukas 2:1-19. Ek het nie gedink hulle sou daartoe in staat wees nie. Ek het gedink jong kinders memoriseer kort verse soos: “Wees vriendelik teenoor mekaar.” Ons het dit elke aand saam tydens ons gesinsgebed gereciteer. Ek was nogal verras toe hulle hierdie gedeelte vinnig en maklik memoriseer het.

Ek was nuuskierig. Moes ons dit weer probeer? Paasnaweek het aangebreek en ek het begin om met hulle te werk aan die kruisigingsrekening in Johannes 19:1-19. Weer het hulle dit sonder veel moeite memoriseer. Dit het my aangespoor om met ander gedeeltes voort te gaan.

Toe dit tyd was om die kinders tuis te onderrig, wou ek hê memorisering moet deel wees van ons daaglikse roetine. Ek het ’n banderole gekoop en die gedrukte gedeeltes wat ons memoriseer het en ook die gedeeltes wat ek wou hê hulle moes memoriseer, ingevoer. Dit het ’n roetine begin wat ons steeds vandag doen.

Elke dag reciteer ons die huidige gedeelte sowel as een wat ons vroeër memoriseer het. Ons reciteer dit ook saam as ’n gesin tydens ons aanbiddingsuur. Ek het gevind dat deur dit so te doen die gesin die gedeelte binne ongeveer drie tot vier weke memoriseer.

Aan die begin van ’n nuwe gedeelte lees ek die Skrif hardop voor. Namate die dae aangaan begin die kinders meer en meer byspring. Uiteindelik kry ek hulle net aan die gang en help net soos hulle hulp nodig het. Wanneer ek dink hulle ken die gedeelte, laat ek hulle dit een vir een aan my reciteer. As hulle dit goed ken, begin hulle dit tydens ons gesinsaanbidding aan hul pa reciteer. As hulle dit nie ken nie, bly ons oefen totdat hulle dit ken. Soms gee ek die sukkelende kind net ’n paar verse om op te sê. Die meeste sal egter liewer die hele gedeelte reciteer.

Ons memoriseer as ’n gesin in plaas van individueel. Ek gaan nie na ’n nuwe gedeelte oor totdat almal dit memoriseer het of ten minste volgens hul vermoë nie. (Nie alle kinders kan met drie jaar 19 verse memoriseer nie.) Sommige van ons kinders het by drie jaar skaars gepraat, so mondelinge Bybelgeheue was byna onmoontlik. Sommige kinders struikel deur ’n gedeelte en het baie leidrade nodig, wat finaal aanvaarbaar is as hulle hul bes doen. Soms oorloop ons dieselfde gedeelte weer oor ’n paar jaar en hulle leer dit die tweede keer beter.

Dit mag tydrowend en stresvol klink, maar dit is nie so vir ons nie. Ek spandeer ongeveer vyf minute per dag aan geheuewerk. Ons het geen tydsdruk op ons memorisering nie, so daar is geen spanning om dit teen ’n sekere tyd te ken nie. Die kinders doen dit sedert hulle skaars praat, dus is hulle daaraan gewoond en kla hulle selde. Omdat ons as ’n gesin memoriseer, help dit ook die kind wat nie so goed kan memoriseer as ’n ander nie. As ’n gesin moedig ons en juig ons die sukkelende kind aan. Hy ervaar ’n gevoel van prestasie selfs as hy deur die hele gedeelte moet worstel.

Ek gee ’n klein beloning vir elke gememoriseerde gedeelte. Ek het ’n prysblikkie waarvan hulle kan kies. Dit hoef nie veel te kos nie! Ek spandeer dikwels nie meer as ’n dollar nie. Skoonheidsverkopings en tweedehandswinkels is plekke om items goedkoop te koop. Terugskool-aanbiedings is ook lekker omdat meeste kinders daarvan hou om ’n nuwe stel krasters of ’n oulike uitveër te hê.

Met verloop van tyd het ek myself moedeloos gevind oor hoe vinnig die kinders ’n gememoriseerde gedeelte vergeet. Ek het ontdek dat hulle enkele jare later dikwels skaars ’n vroeër geleerde gedeelte kon reciteer. Ek het wonder waarom ek die moeite ingesit het as hulle dit oor ’n paar jaar tog gaan vergeet. My man het my aangemoedig om aan te hou. Hy het gesê dat die konsepte steeds in hul harte was, selfs al kon hulle die gedeelte nie meer reciteer nie. So ek het aangehou, maar ek het steeds na ’n oplossing vir hierdie probleem gesoek.

Een dag het ek ’n artikel gelees wat deur ’n ander ma geskryf is wat ook met haar kinders op memorisering gewerk het. In die artikel het sy gesê dat dit belangrik is om die geheuewerk uit die korttermyngeheue in die langtermyngeheue te kry. Die oplossing is eintlik redelik eenvoudig. Elke dag benewens ons nuwe gedeelte reciteer ons ook ’n vroeër geleerde gedeelte. My banderole kom handig te pas hiervoor! Al die gedeeltes wat ons geleer het, is in hierdie banderole. Ek gebruik ’n paperclip om my te help onthou watter gedeelte ons pas hersien het. Elke dag skuif die paperclip na die volgende gedeelte. Wanneer ons by die einde aankom, begin ons weer van vooraf. Dit help om die gedeeltes vars in ons gedagtes te hou en dit te verskuif na ons langtermyngeheue.

Ek hou ook daarvan om ’n tema vir elke skooljaar te hê. Een jaar was my tema: “Memoriseer 100 Verse.” Die kinders het daarvan gehou om te sien hoe die getal met verloop van die jaar styg. Vanjaar werk ons aan “Die Bergrede.” Ek het dit in 10 afdelings verdeel. Die doel is om dit in ’n jaar klaar te kry, maar as ons daardie doel nie bereik nie, maak dit nie saak nie. Dit is beter om stadig te gaan en iets goed te memoriseer as om vinnig te gaan en nie te behou wat jy geleer het nie.

Dit is die metodes wat ek nuttig gevind het vir ons familie. Bid en vra God vir idees wat goed vir jou familie sal werk sonder om jouself met ander families te vergelyk! Onderskat nie wat jou kinders kan doen nie. Moet nie aanvaar dat omdat hulle jonk is, hulle slegs ’n of twee verse kan memoriseer nie. Kinders presteer dikwels net so goed as wat ons van hulle verwag, selfs die jonger een.

Nadat ons God se Woord memoriseer het, moet ons dit daagliks gebruik. ’n Kombers wat in ’n kas weggesteek word, doen niks goed op ’n koue wintersnag nie. Die skrywer van Deuteronomium vat dit goed saam—En jy sal die HERE jou God liefhê uit al jou hart, en uit al jou siel, en uit al jou krag. En hierdie woorde, wat ek jou vandag beveel, sal in jou hart wees: En jy sal dit jou kinders deeglik leer, en sal daarvan praat as jy sit in jou huis, en as jy wandel langs die pad, en as jy lê neer, en as jy opstaan –Deuteronomium 6:5-7.

Eerstens, ons het God lief. Dan sit ons Sy Woord in ons harte. Laastens behoort ons hierdie waarhede aan ons kinders te leer terwyl ons ons daaglikse aktiwiteite doen. Hierdie gedeelte omvat dit alles—sit, wandel, neerle, en opstaan. Nadat ’n gedeelte memoriseer is, sal my man die verse tydens ons aanbiddingsuur aan ons verduidelik. Dit help ons om te verstaan wat ons memoriseer.

Ons doen baie dinge uit gewoonte omdat ons hul belangrikheid besef. Ons borsel ons tande, kam ons hare, eet ontbyt, en doen baie ander dinge. Ons doen hierdie dinge daagliks. Dit is ’n gereelde deel van ons lewens. Omdat ons dit waardeer, laat ons dit gebeur. Dit behoort so te wees met Skrifmemorisasie. Dit is te waardevol om oor te slaan.

Geseënd is die man wat nie wandel in die raad van die goddelose, en nie staan in die pad van die sondares, en nie sit in die saamkoms van spotters nie. Maar sy behae is in die wet van die HERE; en in sy wet dink hy dag en nag. En hy sal wees soos ’n boom geplant by die strome van waters, wat sy vrug gee in sy seisoen; sy blare sal ook nie verwelk nie; en al wat hy doen sal slaag –Psalm 1:1-3.

Wanneer ons ons behae in God se Woord vind, sal ons graag tyd neem om Skrif te memoriseer, en die gememoriseerde Woord sal dan in sy tyd vrug dra.

En laat ons nie moeg word om goed te doen nie: want in die regte tyd sal ons oes, as ons nie afmat nie –Galasiërs 6:9.

I watched as a man attempted to cut a large sheet of plywood in half. He was talking with a few other men while he was cutting, and it seemed that he wasn’t too concerned about making the cut straight. I noticed that he continued to cut further and further from the line that he had scratched into the piece of plywood with a nail. After he was several inches off, one of his friends tried to point it out but he pretended to ignore him. He tried to casually guide the old handsaw back towards the line, while continuing to talk with the men, not making a big deal of it. Finally, after he was more than a foot off, he stopped. He knew now that he had a problem, a problem he could not fix.

I had to think, “Is this what we are doing as the church, the bride of Christ?” We are not too serious about drifting off the straight and narrow way; we allow things to come into our midst. We say, “It’s not a big deal, let’s not be critical.” But the longer we wait, the harder it will be to straighten out. At first it shocks us; later it becomes the new normal. How do we tell if we have drifted? It should be as easy as considering where we used to be, and comparing it that with where we are now, then evaluating the change with what the Bible teaches.

Since fighting against drift is not popular, men in the church don’t want to do it. Some people in our churches who are drifting towards the world have perfected a feel-good gospel. They go on and on about how close they are getting to Jesus, and how blessed they are, but their direction is clearly not in line with the teachings of Scripture. They’re headed towards the world.

There are others who don’t want the church to drift, yet they have their own problems—the love of money, covetousness, and a love of pleasure. No one says anything because it seems that nobody wants to hear. A popular response is, “Yes, I know it’s not good, but what can we do?” “All churches have problems.” Or “Yes, I would never allow that, but I don’t feel it’s in my place to speak up about it.” “It’s not for my family, but if others want to do that, its fine.”

We live in a “me” age. Everything is about me. The conservative, Anabaptist people are getting tangled up in social media, selfies, tweeting, Facebook, and you name it. We love ourselves to the extent that we talk, act, and dress in ways that draw attention to ourselves—we promote ourselves. We talk about looking good, feeling good, and living good. What happened to promoting Jesus? Remember, Jesus said: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it –Matthew 16:25.

Why does it seem so hard to tell which direction we are going? If we are all about ourselves, then we are not all about Jesus. If we are into the latest fashions and the nicest cars, trucks, and houses, then we are not all about Jesus. We cannot indulge ourselves in pleasing the flesh, and still say we are Christians.

I was recently asked why some pastors lose their children to the world. In most cases, I believe it’s the same reason that many Anabaptists are losing their children to the kingdom of darkness—the fathers have lost a godly vision for their homes. They live a powerless life and allow the world to come in. Maybe they do not have television, but what about the internet? This still allows the influence of the world to come in. Also, Dad spends more time with his business and more time enjoying life than he does seeking the face of God.

Many Americans go on short-term missions. Many times, it seems that the youth who go want to hit the beach or some other pleasure and relaxation as soon as they get off the plane. Why? Because that’s what they are either taught or allowed to do back home—seek pleasure. They haven’t been taught to deny the flesh; they haven’t seen their parents deny the flesh. Some of us might be so far off the mark that we need to do like the carpenter at the beginning of this article—Humble ourselves and start over.

Husbands are pulling their unwilling wives into the world, wives are pushing their husbands into the world, and children are dragging their parents into the world. And unfortunately, since the modern church has thrown off all forms of discipline and structure, everyone can stay in the church and pollute it with their worldly ideas (at least as long as you smile and say you love Jesus.) Remember the Scriptures: If ye love me, keep my commandments –John 14:15. And, He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him –1 John 2:4.

Here are some areas of drift in the church.

Brotherly love

By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another –John 13:35.

People have visited our church and asked if we practice the holy kiss. I reply that we do; however, understanding the need to love one another comes first. Many churches are doing away with the holy kiss, which is clearly instructed in the Word. And it seems appropriate because they have stopped loving one another. I don’t believe we understand the importance of this topic—having love one for another. When our love causes us to suffer for one another, the world sees it. Often, the reason a brotherhood stops loving each other is because they are not in the fight “together” anymore. They have become independent.

Some of the greatest acts of showing love for one another have happened on the battlefield. Men have jumped on grenades, and they have jumped in front of bullets to save their comrades. Because they have fought together, they look out for each other. What if a soldier marching out to battle would notice a fellow soldier’s ammunition clip fall from his gun? What would he do? Would he remain quiet because his comrade might get mad? Or would he remain quiet because he knew that he had his own problems? No. He would help his brother. If ungodly men on the battlefield can practice this, why can’t God’s people do so in the church? Before I was converted, I was in the military. I chose to suffer for my country. Now that I’m a Christian, I now choose to suffer for my Lord.

Dress

This is the most obvious, but also the most overlooked. The worldly church says, “It’s the heart that counts, so how we appear on the outside doesn’t matter”. Are the Anabaptists falling for this? The world used to dress modestly, but television and Hollywood began to promote a focus on the human body. Surely the church wouldn’t follow Hollywood. But what is the difference—a woman of the world who is obviously dressed immodestly, or a woman of the church dressed with a cape dress that is form-fitting, and with a little covering hanging skimpily on the back of her head? There is little difference, except the one claims to be a Christian and the other one doesn’t. Dear ones, the world is laughing at us.

So how does it all start? Subtly. First remove a pleat here or a gather there, then start using a little less material, finally, start buying brighter bolder colors. The men untuck the shirt, switch to jeans, then skinny jeans, undo a few buttons, grow out the hair a little. Buy a pair of the “cool” name brand shoes, and a cowboy hat. The devil is no fool. If you drop a frog into boiling water, it will jump out quickly. If you boil the water that contains the frog, he will slowly cook to death. Is it too late for us to jump out? With God all things are possible. Brothers and sisters, it is the heart that counts; and if we desire to look like the world, our heart is worldly and needs to be cleaned—cleaned by the ever so powerful blood of Jesus.

Pleasure

Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter. Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you –James 5:5-6.

And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection –Luke 8:14.

This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away –2 Timothy 3:1-5.

When we are given to pleasure, we separate ourselves from the sufferings we have been called to, therefore separating us from the reward received from suffering.

Remember, when we give in a little on any issue during our generation, our children will go farther with it. When our children enjoy going to church only because of the volleyball game that’s scheduled afterward, it’s not good. When they want to go on a mission trip because of the pleasures of the ocean, it’s not good. I’m not saying those things are bad, but when they become the focal point, we have a serious problem. Do we enjoy doing the things that God enjoys? Do we enjoy hymn sings anymore? Do we enjoy helping the poor? What about visiting the widows? I believe if the fathers have their priorities right, and they truly love doing the things of God even if the flesh suffers, then so will our children, (the next generation) for which WE are responsible. I often tell people that they don’t need to follow Jesus. They can love the world, and the pleasures of this life, but they cannot continue sitting in our church and pretend they are Christians. People might say that’s too harsh, but I believe Jesus said the same thing. I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth –Revelation 3:15-16.

This is not a complete list as there are many other ways that the church is drifting towards the world. My prayer is that, first, we could see the problem, and second, we could deal with it. Remember a little leaven leavens the lump. (1 Corinthians 5)

There is a battle that’s raging; the kingdom of darkness is pressing in. The devil truly knows he has but a short time. Let us make a stand, put down our white flags, and pick up our swords. Let us remove the traitors, the world, and the sin that has come into the church. Let us purify the church and fight the good fight of faith.

How do we stop the drift? How do we leave behind a faithful generation? First, the fathers need to teach their children, and the leaders in the church need to teach them all. The early Anabaptists met as many times as they could, and that was usually out in the weather, in some woods somewhere. Our church here meets five times a week. Meeting on Sundays only, I believe, shows where our priorities are.

And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ: – Ephesians 4:11-13.

It seems that God would give us teachers, pastors, evangelists, prophets, and apostles if we would use them.

Let’s make this personal—there could be areas of drift in my life. We need to help each other before we all drift into ruin. Maybe we can maintain, but we also need to be concerned about our children. If we could get together and be honest with ourselves and with one another about what the scriptures clearly teach, then we would be more careful. If we could study God’s Word together, with open hearts and minds, I believe we could strengthen that which remains. I believe if we would fall on our faces before God, He would heal our churches. May God bless us all in a deeper walk with Him.

Nilikuwa nikitazama mtu anajaribu kukata karatasi kubwa ya plywood katikati. Alikuwa akizungumza na baadhi ya wanaume wengine wakati alipokuwa akikata, na ilionekana kwamba hakuwa na wasiwasi mkubwa kuhusu kukata kwa mstari. Niligundua kwamba aliendelea kukata umbali mrefu zaidi kutoka kwenye mstari aliozikia kwenye karatasi kwa msumari. Baada ya kuwa mbali kwa inchi kadhaa, mmoja wa marafiki zake alijaribu kuonyesha hilo lakini alitajwa kuanza kuwasahau. Alijaribu kwa kimya kumwelekeza tena mswaki wa mikono kuelekea mstari, huku akiendelea kuzungumza na wanaume hao, bila kurudisha suala hilo kuwa jambo kubwa. Hatimaye, baada ya kuwa mbali zaidi ya futi moja, alikuja kusimama. Sasa alijua kwamba alikuwa na tatizo, tatizo ambalo hakuwa na uwezo wa kulitatua.

Nilihitaji kufikiri, “Je, hili ndilo tunalofanya kama kanisa, mchumba wa Kristo?” Hatuwe na mzaha mkubwa kuhusu kuongoka kutoka njia nyembamba na iliyo sawa; tunaruhusu mambo kuingia katikati yetu. Tunasema, “Si jambo mkubwa, tusiwe na ukosoaji.” Lakini kadri tunavyosubiri, ndivyo itakavyokuwa vigumu kurudisha. Mwanzoni inatushangaza; baadaye inakuwa kawaida mpya. Tujue vipi kama tumepotoka? Inapaswa kuwa rahisi kama kuzingatia tulikokuwa, na kulilinganisha na tulipo sasa, kisha kutathmini mabadiliko na mafundisho ya Biblia.

Kwa kuwa kupigana dhidi ya kupotoka si maarufu, wanaume ndani ya kanisa hawataki kufanya hivyo. Watu wengine katika makanisa yetu ambao wanapotoka kuelekea dunia wameshakuza injili ya kujihisi vizuri. Wanaendelea kuzungumza kuhusu jinsi wanavyokaribia Yesu, na jinsi walivyoibarikiwa, lakini mwelekeo wao hauendani wazi na mafundisho ya Maandiko. Wako wakielekea dunia.

Kuna wengine ambao hawataki kanisa lipoteze njia, lakini wao wenyewe wana matatizo yao—upendo wa pesa, tamaa, na upendo wa starehe. Hakuna anayesema jambo lolote kwa sababu inaonekana hakuna anayependa kusikia. Jibu maarufu ni, “Ndiyo, najua sio nzuri, lakini tunaweza kufanya nini?” “Makanisa yote yana matatizo.” Au “Ndiyo, ningekataa hilo kamwe, lakini sijihisi ni nafasi yangu kuzungumza juu yake.” “Sio kwa familia yangu, lakini kama wengine wanataka kufanya hivyo, sawa.”

Tunaishi katika enzi ya “mimi”. Kila kitu ni kuhusu mimi. Watu wa Kikomavu, watu wa Anabaptisti wanajikuta wamechanganyikiwa kwenye mitandao ya kijamii, selfies, tweeting, Facebook, na neno lolote utakaloita. Tunajipenda kiasi kwamba tunazungumza, kutenda, na kuvaa kwa njia zinazoruhusu kupendeza kwa sisi—tunajitangaza wenyewe. Tunazungumzia kuonekana nzuri, kuhisi vizuri, na kuishi vizuri. Nini kilitokea kwa kueneza Yesu? Kumbuka, Yesu alisema: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it –Matthew 16:25.

Kwa nini inaonekana kuwa ngumu kusema ni wapi tunakwenda? Ikiwa sisi ni kuhusu sisi wenyewe tu, basi hatuwezi kuwa kuhusu Yesu. Ikiwa tuko kwenye mitindo ya hivi punde na magari mazuri, malori, na nyumba nzuri, basi hatuwezi kuwa kuhusu Yesu. Hatuwezi kujiruhusu kufurahisha mwili, na bado tuseme sisi ni Wakristo.

Hivi karibuni niliulizwa kwa nini baadhi ya wachungaji hupoteza watoto wao kwa dunia. Katika kesi nyingi, naamini ni kwa sababu ile ile ambayo wengi wa Anabaptisti wanapoteza watoto wao kwa ufalme wa giza—baba wamepoteza maono ya Mungu kwa nyumba zao. Huwa wana maisha bila nguvu na waruhusu dunia kuingia. Labda hawana televisheni, lakini vipi kuhusu intaneti? Hii bado inaruhusu ushawishi wa dunia kuingia. Pia, Baba hutumia muda mwingi na biashara yake na kufurahia maisha kuliko kutafuta uso wa Mungu.

Wengi wa Wamarekani hufanya misheni za muda mfupi. Mara nyingi, inaonekana vijana wanaoenda wanataka kwenda ufukweni au starehe nyingine mara tu wanapotua. Kwa nini? Kwa sababu ndio wanavyofundishwa au kuruhusiwa kufanya nyumbani—kutafuta starehe. Hawajafundishwa kukataa tamaa ya mwili; hawajawaona wazazi wao wakikataa tamaa ya mwili. Wengine wetu tunaweza kuwa mbali sana kwamba tunahitaji kufanya kama mkarani aliyekuwa mwanzoni mwa makala hii—kujinyenyekea na kuanza upya.

Waume wanavuta wake zao wasiotaka ndani ya dunia, wake wanasukuma waume zao ndani ya dunia, na watoto wanavuta wazazi wao ndani ya dunia. Na kwa bahati mbaya, tangu kanisa la kisasa limetupa aina zote za nidhamu na muundo, kila mtu anaweza kubaki ndani ya kanisa na kuichafua na mawazo yao ya kidunia (angalau mradi unacheka na kusema unapompenda Yesu.) Kumbuka Maandiko: If ye love me, keep my commandments –John 14:15. And, He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him –1 John 2:4.

Hapa kuna baadhi ya maeneo ya kupotoka ndani ya kanisa.

Upendo wa kirafiki

By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another –John 13:35.

Watu wamekutembelea kanisa yetu na kukuuliza kama tunafanya busu mtakatifu. Ninajibu kwamba tunafanya; hata hivyo, kuelewa hitaji la kupendana kwanza ni muhimu. Makanisa mengi yameacha busu mtakatifu, ambalo linaelekezwa wazi katika Neno. Na inaonekana inafaa kwa sababu wametoa upendo miongoni mwao. Sidhani kwamba tunaelewa umuhimu wa mada hii—kuwa na upendo wa kila mmoja. Wakati upendo wetu unatusababisha kuathirika kwa ajili ya kila mmoja, dunia inaona. Mara nyingi, sababu kwa nini ndugu huacha kupendana ni kwa sababu hawako katika vita “pamoja” tena. Wamekuwa huru.

Baadhi ya matendo makubwa ya kuonyesha upendo kwa mmoja kwa mwingine yamefanyika uwanjani. Watu wamejiweka juu ya granadi, na wamejiweka mbele ya risasi kuokoa wenzake. Kwa sababu wamepigana pamoja, wanajali kila mmoja. Je, ikiwa mwanajeshi anayetoka kuingia vita angemwona karanga ya risasi ya mwenzake ikiondoka kutoka kwenye bunduki yake? Angefanya nini? Angebaki kimya kwa sababu mwenzake angekasirika? Au angebaki kimya kwa sababu yeye mwenyewe alikuwa na matatizo yake? Hapana. Angeweza kumsaidia ndugu yake. Ikiwa watu wasio wa Mungu uwanjani wanaweza kufanya hivi, kwa nini watu wa Mungu wasifanane ndani ya kanisa? Kabla sijabadilika, nilikuwa kwenye jeshi. Nilichagua kuvumilia kwa ajili ya nchi yangu. Sasa mimi ni Mkristo, sasa ninachagua kuumia kwa Bwana wangu.

Mavazi

Hili ndilo dhahiri zaidi, lakini pia linalopuuzwa zaidi. Kanisa la kidunia linasema, “Ni moyo unaohesabiwa, hivyo jinsi tunavyoonekana nje haijali”. Je, Anabaptisti wanapigwa na hili? Dunia zamani ilikuwa ikivaa kwa adabu, lakini televisheni na Hollywood ilianza kukuza mtazamo kuhusu mwili wa binadamu. Bila shaka kanisa halingefuata Hollywood. Lakini ni tofauti gani—mwanamke wa dunia aliye wazi kuwa amevaa vibaya, au mwanamke wa kanisa amevaa gauni lenye cape linaloweza kuonyesha mwili, na na kifuniko kidogo kinachotawanyika nyuma ya kichwa chake? Kuna tofauti ndogo, isipokuwa mmoja anadai kuwa Mkristo na mwingine hapadai. Wapendwa, dunia inatusema vicheko.

Basi yote huanza vipi? Kwa taratibu. Kwanza ondoa pleati hapa au kukusanya pale, kisha anza kutumia kitengo kidogo cha kitambaa, hatimaye, anza kununua rangi ang’avu na kali. Wanaume wanatupa shati ndani, kubadilisha kuwa jeans, kisha skinny jeans, kufungua vitufe vichache, kukuza nywele kidogo. Nunua jozi ya viatu vya chapa maarufu, na kofia ya cowboy. Ibilisi sio mjinga. Ukimwaga chura ndani ya maji moto, ataruka nje kwa haraka. Ukapika maji ambayo yanamnyonyesha chura, ataungua polepole hadi kufa. Je, bado ni kuchelewa kwetu kuruka nje? Kwa Mungu yote inawezekana. Ndugu na dada, moyo ndio unaoheshimiwa; na ikiwa tunataka kuonekana kama dunia, mioyo yetu ni ya kidunia na inahitaji kusafishwa—kusafishwa kwa damu yenye nguvu ya Yesu.

Starehe

Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter. Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you –James 5:5-6.

And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection –Luke 8:14.

This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away –2 Timothy 3:1-5.

Wakati tunajitumikia kwa starehe, tunajitenga kutoka kwa mateso tulioitwa kuyashuhudia, na hivyo kututenganisha na zawadi inayopatikana kwa kupitia mateso.

Kumbuka, tunapoteremsha kidogo jambo lolote katika kizazi chetu, watoto wetu watakwenda zaidi nalo. Wakati watoto wetu wanapenda kwenda kanisani kwa sababu tu ya mchezo wa voliboli uliopangwa baadaye, sio nzuri. Wakati wanataka kwenda kwenye safari ya misheni kwa sababu ya furaha za bahari, sio nzuri. Sizungumzii kwamba mambo hayo ni mabaya, lakini wakati yanakuwa kitovu cha mambo, tuna tatizo kubwa. Je, tunafurahia kufanya mambo ambayo Mungu anafurahia? Je, tunafurahia nyimbo za kanisa tena? Je, tunafurahia kusaidia maskini? Vipi kuhusu kutembelea mzaziwa? Ninaamini ikiwa baba wanaweka vipaumbele vyake vizuri, na kwa kweli wanapenda kufanya mambo ya Mungu hata kama mwili unateseka, basi vivyo hivyo watoto wetu (kizazi kijacho) watafanya, kwa ajili yao SISI tumejibu. Mara nyingi nampa watu neno kwamba hawahitaji kumfuata Yesu. Wanaweza kumpenda dunia, na starehe za maisha haya, lakini hawawezi kuendelea kukaa katika kanisa letu wakidai kuwa Wakristo. Watu wanaweza kusema hilo ni kali sana, lakini naamini Yesu alisema kitu kama hicho. I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth –Revelation 3:15-16.

Hii sio orodha kamili kwani kuna njia nyingi nyingine ambazo kanisa linapotoka kuelekea dunia. Sala yangu ni kwamba, kwanza, tunaweza kuona tatizo, na pili, tunaweza kulitatua. Kumbuka chachu kidogo huchafua unga mzima. (1 Corinthians 5)

Kuna vita inayochoma; ufalme wa giza unakuza shinikizo. Yule mwizi, Ibilisi, anajua ana muda mfupi tu. Tuchukue msimamo, tuchome bendera zetu nyeupe, na kuchukua upanga wetu. Tuondoe wasaliti, dunia, na dhambi ambayo imeingia ndani ya kanisa. Tufsafishe kanisa na tupigane vita nzuri ya imani.

This hymn is universally thought to be one of the greatest hymns ever authored by a woman. It can be found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. This hymn writer was a woman of great ambition and enjoyment; a person full of life, vivacious, beautiful, talented, and a person who’s “exalted character always made a deep impression upon all who knew her”. Although she had a full and productive life, it was short, hastened on by her delicate and frail constitution. This hymn story has touched many lives in times of distress and hardship, including death. It has been used of God to draw the hearts of men from their present distresses, heavenward, to the immortal realities beyond this life.

Sarah Flower Adam was born at Harlow, England on February 22, 1805, to Benjamin and Eliza Flower. When she was five years old, her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis. Sarah and her older sister Eliza also inherited the same physical weakness. Speaking of the hymn writer I quote from 101 Hymn Stories: “She was also widely known for her many literary accomplishments, though her delicate health was always a handicap for her many ambitions.”

In the year 1834, at the age of 29, Sarah married a prominent inventor and civil engineer, John Brydges. This distinguished couple made their home in London, England for the duration of their marriage, until the hymn writer’s death fourteen years later in 1848, at the early age of 43.

Sarah and her older sister Eliza made an outstanding team in the realm of music—writing and composing new songs. The elder sister being an accomplished musician, and the younger the hymn writer. One day their pastor, the Rev. William Johnson Fox, asked these two exceptional sisters if they would help him with the compilation for a new hymnal for his congregation. They committed to the project, and soon were busily occupied in helping him complete the song book. “Together, they contributed thirteen texts and sixty-two new tunes.”

One day as the two sisters were pressing into the task at hand, the pastor remarked that he wished he could have a hymn written to conclude a sermon he was preparing to preach on the account of Jacob and Esau. Eliza interrupted enthusiastically, “Sarah, now there’s an excellent idea for a new hymn for our hymnal. Why don’t you write your own hymn about Jacob’s dream?”

“Splendid!” replied the pastor. Later that day, after spending much time studying the Genesis account, absorbing the atmosphere, and feeling the dramatic movement of this Old Testament narrative, Sarah began to write. Soon she had versified the complete Biblical story into these five stanzas of the immortal hymn still in use today.

Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song would be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven:
All that Thou send’st to me
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with Thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Or if on joyful wing
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upwards I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

This great hymn was written in 1840 and published the next year in the hymn book Hymns and Anthems prepared by Rev. Fox, the hymn writer’s pastor. The hymn’s original tune was a composition of Eliza, Sarah’s older sister. In 1844, Rev. James Freeman Clarke introduced the hymn in America, but it did not become well known for another 12 years. At that point the hymn was wedded with the present-day tune “Bethany” composed especially for the text by Lowell Mason, who is sometimes referred to as the father of American church and school music. Other hymns by Mason include “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains”, “When I Survey the Wondrous Cross”, “A Charge to Keep I Have”, “Joy to the World”, “My Faith Looks Up to Thee”, and “O Day of Rest and Gladness”.

Many very interesting accounts have been recorded in conjunction with the use of this hymn, and its effect on those who sang it or heard it sung. In the Boston Peace Jubilee of 1872, which commemorated the end of the civil war, this hymn, “Nearer, My God to Thee”, was sung by 50,000 voices. In 1871, three renowned theologians, Professors Hitchcock, Smith, and Park, were traveling in Palestine, when they heard the faint strains of “Bethany” reach their ears. Regarding this incident, I quote from A Treasury of Hymn Stories, “Drawing near, to their amazement, they saw fifty Syrian students standing under some trees in a circle, and singing in Arabic ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee,’ Professor Hitchcock, speaking afterward of the event, said that the singing of that Christian hymn by those Syrian youths moved him to tears, and affected him more than any singing he had ever heard before”.

During the Johnstown City Flood of May 31, 1889 (a tragic disaster that killed over 2,000 people), an unfortunate railroad train rushed into the swirling flood waters. A young woman, prepared to be a missionary, and on her way to the far east, became one of those trapped in a railroad car which was turned up on end. Beyond the hope of rescue, she spoke calmly to the awe-struck crowd as they gazed helplessly at the unfolding tragedy as the car sank beneath the muddy waters. She ended up with prayer and by singing “Nearer, my God, to Thee,” in which she was joined by the grieving and sympathizing throng. As she sang, she passed away, coming indeed nearer to her God whom she loved and desired to serve.

Last, but not least, in the wee hours of April 15th, 1912, the story of the sinking of the proud and ill-fated ship, the Titanic, brings this song to our memory yet again. Many survivors that witnessed this great tragedy have testified that the hymn “Nearer, my God to Thee” was the final song played before the cold waves of the Atlantic Ocean silenced her forever—as the band played, the great ship sank, plunging into the depths, sending over 1,500 souls into eternity.

In conclusion, it is incredible how much music and singing affect us. As we have seen from some of these accounts, from praise to peril, from thanksgiving to tragedy, from worship to the worst disasters that man may experience, God has given us this priceless gift in the timeless possession of the old-time hymns. May they never lose their luster in our lives or in the lives of our posterity, until that final day when time shall cease to exist.

يُعتبر هذا الترتيل على نطاق واسع واحدًا من أعظم التراتيل التي كتبتها امرأة على الإطلاق. يوجد في كل مزمور تقريبًا أو كتاب تراتيل نُشر اليوم تقريبًا. كانت كاتبة هذا الترتيل امرأة ذات طموح واستمتاع كبيرين؛ شخصية نابضة بالحياة، حيوية، جميلة، موهوبة، وشخصية «كان طابعها المتميز دائمًا يترك انطباعًا عميقًا على كل من عرفها». ومع أن حياتها كانت مليئة ومنتجة، فقد كانت قصيرة، مُسرَّعة بسبب بنيتها الجسدية الرقيقة والضعيفة. لقد لمست قصة هذا الترتيل العديد من القلوب في أوقات الضيق والشدة، بما في ذلك الموت. وقد استعملها الله لجذب قلوب البشر من ضيقاتهم الحاضرة، نحو السماء، نحو الحقائق الخالدة وراء هذه الحياة.

ولدت سارة فلاور آدامز في هارلو، إنجلترا في 22 فبراير 1805، لِـبنيامين وإليزا فلاور. عندما كانت في الخامسة من عمرها، ماتت والدتها بسبب الدرن، المعروف اليوم باسم السلّ. وورثت سارة وأختها الكبرى إليزا نفس الضعف الجسدي أيضًا. وفيما يخص كاتبة التراتيل أقتبس من كتاب 101 Hymn Stories: «كانت معروفة على نطاق واسع أيضًا لإنجازاتها الأدبية العديدة، على الرغم من أن صحتها الرقيقة كانت دائمًا عقبة أمام طموحاتها العديدة.»

في عام 1834، عن عمر يناهز 29 عامًا، تزوجت سارة مخترعًا ومهندسًا مدنيًا بارزًا، جون بريدجز. أقام هذا الزوج المرموق في لندن، إنجلترا طوال مدة زواجهما، حتى وفاة كاتبة التراتيل بعد أربعة عشر عامًا في 1848، عن عمرٍ مبكرٍ هو 43 عامًا.

شكلت سارة وأختها الكبرى إليزا فريقًا متميزًا في مجال الموسيقى—كتابة وتأليف أناشيد جديدة. فقد كانت الأخت الكبرى موسيقية بارعة، والأصغر منها كاتبة التراتيل. ذات يوم طلب منهما قسُّهما، القس ويليام جونسون فوكس، أن تساعداه في تجميع كتاب ترانيم جديد لجماعته. التزمتا بالمشروع، وسرعان ما انغمستا في مساعدته على إكمال كتاب الأغاني. «معًا، ساهمتا بثلاث عشرة نصًا وستين لحنًا جديدًا.»

ذات يوم، بينما كانتا الأختان مشغولتين بالمهمة، قال القس إنه يتمنى لو وُجد ترتيل ليُختم به موعظة كان يستعد لإلقائها حول قصة يعقوب وعيسو. قاطعت إليزا بحماس: «سارة، هذه فكرة ممتازة لترتيل جديد في كتاب ترانيمنا. لماذا لا تكتبي ترتيلك الخاص عن حلم يعقوب؟»

«عظيم!» أجاب القس. وفي وقت لاحق من ذلك اليوم، وبعد قضاء وقت طويل في دراسة سرد سفر التكوين، واستيعاب الجو العام، والشعور بالحركة الدرامية لهذه الرواية العهدية، بدأت سارة في الكتابة. وسرعان ما صاغت العرض الكامل للقصة التوراتية في هذه الأبيات الخمسة من الترتيل الخالد الذي لا يزال يُستخدم اليوم.

أقرب إليك يا إلهي،
أقرب إليك!
حتى لو كان ذلك صليبًا
يرفعني؛
فستظل كل ترنيمي،
أقرب إليك يا إلهي،
أقرب إليك!

حتى لو كنت كالتائه،
وقد غربت الشمس،
فالظلمة فوقي،
راحتي حجر؛
ومع ذلك في أحلامي سأكون
أقرب إليك يا إلهي،
أقرب إليك!

هناك ليظهر الطريق،
خطوات إلى السماء:
كل ما ترسله إليّ
معطى برحمتك؛
ملائكة لتلوح لي
أقرب إليك يا إلهي،
أقرب إليك!

ثم، مع أفكاري اليقظة
المتألقة بمجدك،
من أحزاني الحجرية
سأقيم بيت إيل؛
هكذا عبر مصائبي أكون
أقرب إليك يا إلهي،
أقرب إليك!

أو إن حلّقت مبتهجًا
متمزقًا في السماء،
وقد نُسيت الشمس والقمر والنجوم،
لأعلى أحلّق،
فستظل كل ترنيمي،
أقرب إليك يا إلهي،
أقرب إليك!

كُتب هذا الترتيل العظيم في عام 1840 ونُشر في العام التالي في كتاب الترانيم Hymns and Anthems الذي أعده القس فوكس، قس كاتبة التراتيل. كان اللحن الأصلي للترتيل من تأليف إليزا، أخت سارة الكبرى. في عام 1844 قدّم القس جيمس فريمان كلارك الترتيل في أمريكا، لكنه لم يَكْنْ معروفًا جيدًا إلا بعد اثني عشر عامًا أخرى. في تلك المرحلة تزوَّج النص باللحن الحالي "بِيثَانِي" الذي ألّفه لويل ميسون خصيصًا للنص، والذي يُشار إليه أحيانًا بأب الموسيقى الكنسية والمدرسية الأمريكية. ومن تراتيله الأخرى "From Greenland’s Icy Mountains" و"When I Survey the Wondrous Cross" و"A Charge to Keep I Have" و"Joy to the World" و"My Faith Looks Up to Thee" و"O Day of Rest and Gladness".

سُجلت العديد من الحوادث المثيرة للاهتمام المتعلقة باستخدام هذا الترتيل وتأثيره على الذين غنّوه أو سمعوه يُغنّى. ففي مهرجان بوسطن للسلام عام 1872، الذي احتفل بنهاية الحرب الأهلية، غناه 50,000 صوتًا. في عام 1871 كان ثلاثة لاهوتيين مرموقين، الأساتذة هيتشكوك، سميث، وبارك، يسافرون في فلسطين، عندما بلغتهم نسمات خفيفة من لحن "بيثاني". وفيما يتعلق بهذا الحادث أقتبس من A Treasury of Hymn Stories: «وعندما اقتربوا، لدهشتهم، رأوا خمسين طالبًا سوريًا واقفين تحت بعض الأشجار في دائرة، ويغنون بالعربية "أقرب إليك يا إلهي". قال الأستاذ هيتشكوك، متحدثًا بعد الحدث، إن غناء ذلك الترتيل المسيحي بتلك الأصوات السورية قد دفعه إلى البكاء، وأثر فيه أكثر من أي غناء سمعه من قبل.»

أثناء فيضان مدينة جونزتاون في 31 مايو 1889 (كارثة مأساوية قتلت أكثر من 2,000 شخص)، اندفعت سيارة قطار تعيسة إلى مياه الفيضان الدوّارة. كانت شابة مُعدة لتكون مبشِّرة، وفي طريقها إلى الشرق الأقصى، فأصبحت واحدة من المحاصَرين في عربة قطار انقلبت على جانبها. وبعد أن فقدت أمل النجاة، خاطبت الحشد المذهول بهدوء وهم يحدقون بلا حول ولا قوة في المأساة الجارية بينما غرقت العربة تحت المياه الموحلة. أنهت صلاتها بالغناء "أقرب إليك يا إلهي"، فانضم إليها الجمع الحزين المتأثر والمتعاطف. وبينما كانت تغني، فارقت الحياة، مقتربة بالفعل من إلهها الذي أحبّت وخدمت رغبةً فيه.

وأخيرًا، ولكن ليس آخِرًا، في ساعة الفجر الباكرة من 15 أبريل 1912، تعيدنا قصة غرق السفينة المتكبّرة وحزينة المصير، Titanic, إلى هذه الأغنية مرة أخرى. شهد العديد من الناجين من تلك المأساة أن الترتيل "أقرب إليك يا إلهي" كان آخر أغنية عُزفت قبل أن تسكت موجات المحيط الأطلسي الباردة السفينة إلى الأبد—فبينما كانت الفرقة تعزف غرقت السفينة العظيمة، متهاوية إلى الأعماق، مرسلةً أكثر من 1,500 نفس إلى الأبدية.

خاتمةً، من المذهل مدى تأثير الموسيقى والغناء علينا. كما رأينا من بعض هذه الحوادث، من المديح إلى الخطر، من الشكر إلى المأساة، من العبادة إلى أسوأ الكوارث التي قد يختبرها الإنسان، أعطانا الله هذه الهدية الثمينة في الملكية الخالدة للأناشيد القديمة. فليحفظها الله من أن يفقد نورها في حياتنا أو في حياة ذُرّيتنا، إلى ذلك اليوم الأخير حينما يتوقف الزمن عن الوجود.

As sisters in the Lord and born-again believers, I am sure we would all agree that memorizing scripture is important to our spiritual health. I have memorized many, many Scripture verses during my childhood years. Most of the verses that I memorized were taught during a vacation Bible School which I attended each summer.

During the first evening of Bible School, the teachers handed out memory work assignments, often many pages worth. These were not all required but the rewards were appealing. Most years I memorized everything that was assigned. I give these teachers and this Bible School the credit for the wealth of verses I memorized during those years.

Now I am married and have children of my own. The Bible School from my childhood is long past. I realized that if my children were going to memorize Scripture, I would need to make it happen. As moms, many of us know the importance of memorizing God’s Word and hiding it, not only in our hearts, but also in our children’s hearts.

Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments. Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee –Psalm 119:9-11.

We need God’s Word in our hearts to help us with our daily battles with sin. Our children need this as well. Most of our children are not going to memorize scripture without some help from us.

My husband and I did not enter marriage with dreams of memorizing with our children. For our family, it happened almost accidentally. Our oldest children were three and four when my husband suggested that we work with them on memorizing the Christmas story found in Luke 2:1-19. I didn’t think they would be able to do it. I thought young children memorized short verses like, “Be ye kind one to another.” We started reciting it together every evening during our family devotions. I was quite surprised when they memorized this passage quickly and easily.

I was intrigued. Should we try again? Easter was approaching so I started working with them on the crucifixion account found in John 19:1-19. Again, they memorized this without much effort. This encouraged me to continue with other passages.

When it came time to homeschool the children, I wanted memorization to be a part of our daily routine. I bought a binder and inserted the printed passages we had memorized as well as the passages I wanted them to memorize. This started a routine that we still do today.

Every day we recite the current passage as well as one we have previously memorized. We also recite it together as a family during our devotion time. I have found that doing it this way results in the family having the passage memorized in about three to four weeks.

At the beginning of a new passage, I read the scripture out loud. As the days go by the children start chiming in more and more. Eventually, I just get them started and only help as they need help. When I think they know the passage I have them recite it to me one by one. If they know it well, they start reciting it to their dad during our family devotions. If they don’t know it, we keep on practicing till they do know it. Sometimes I will give the struggling child just a few verses to recite. However, most of them would rather recite the whole thing.

We memorize as a family instead of individually. I don’t move on to a new passage until everyone has it memorized or at least memorized to their ability. (Not all children can memorize 19 verses at age three.) Some of our children were barely talking at three years old so verbal Bible memory was hardly possible. Some children will stumble through a passage and need lots of clue words, which is okay if they are doing their best. Sometimes we go over the same passage again in a few years and they learn it better the second time.

This may sound time-consuming and stressful, but it is not so for us. I spend about five minutes a day working on memory work. We have no time constraints on our memorization so there is no pressure to know it by a certain time. The children have been doing this since they were barely talking, so they are used to it and rarely complain. Since we memorize as a family, it also helps the child who can’t memorize as well as another. As a family, we encourage and cheer on the struggling child. He feels a sense of accomplishment even if he struggles through the whole passage.

I give a small reward for each passage memorized. I have a prize box that they can choose from. This does not need to cost much! I often do not spend much more than a dollar. Yard sales and thrift stores are places to purchase items cheaply. Back-to-school sales are nice as well since most children like to have a new pack of crayons or a cute eraser.

As time went by, I found myself becoming discouraged at how quickly the children would forget a memorized passage. I discovered that several years later they often could hardly recite a previously learned passage. I wondered why I was putting in the effort if they were simply going to forget it in a few years. My husband encouraged me to continue. He said that the concepts were still in their hearts even if they could no longer recite the passage. So I continued, but I still hoped for a solution to this problem.

One day I read an article written by another mom who also worked on memorization with her children. In the article she said that it is important to get the memory work out of the short-term memory and into the long-term memory. The solution is actually quite simple. Every day in addition to reciting our new passage, we also recite a previously learned passage. My binder comes in handy for this! All the passages we have learned are in this binder. I use a paper clip to help me remember the passage we just reviewed. Each day the paper clip moves to the next passage. When we reach the end, we start over. This helps to keep the passages fresh in our minds as well as move them to our long-term memory.

I also like to have a theme for each school year. One year my theme was, “Memorize 100 Verses.” The children enjoyed watching the number rise as the year progressed. This year we are working on, “The Sermon on the Mount.” I divided it into 10 sections. The goal is to complete it in a year, but if we don’t reach that goal it doesn’t matter. It is better to go slow and memorize something well than to go fast and not retain what you have learned.

These are the methods I have found helpful for our family. Pray and ask God for ideas that will work well for your family without comparing yourself to other families! Don’t underestimate what your children can do. Don’t assume that because they are young, they can only memorize a verse or two. Children often do only as well as we expect them to, even the younger ones.

After we have God’s Word memorized, we need to use it daily. A blanket that is kept stored away in a closet does no good on a cold, winter night. The writer of Deuteronomy sums this up well—And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up –Deuteronomy 6:5-7.

First, we love God. Then we put His Word into our hearts. Finally, we should teach these truths to our children as we go about our daily activities. This passage encompasses it all—sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up. After a passage is memorized, my husband will explain the verses to us during our devotion time. This helps us to understand what we are memorizing.

We do many things by habit because we realize their importance. We brush our teeth, comb our hair, eat breakfast, and do many other things. We do these things daily. They are a regular part of our lives. Because we value them, we make them happen. This is how it should be with scripture memorization. It is too valuable to skip.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper –Psalm 1:1-3.

When we delight in God’s Word, we will be glad to take time to memorize scripture, and the memorized Word will then bear fruit in its season.

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not –Galatians 6:9.
