Jag såg på när en man försökte såga en stor plywoodskiva i två delar. Han pratade med några andra män medan han sågade, och det verkade som att han inte var så noga med att göra snittet rakt. Jag lade märke till att han fortsatte att såga allt längre bort från linjen som han hade ristat in i plywoodskivan med en spik. Efter att han hade kommit flera centimeter utanför försökte en av hans vänner påpeka det, men han låtsades ignorera honom. Han försökte nonchalant styra tillbaks den gamla handsågen mot linjen, medan han fortsatte att prata med männen och inte gjorde någon stor sak av det. Slutligen, efter att han var mer än trettio centimeter fel, stannade han. Han visste nu att han hade ett problem, ett problem han inte kunde laga.

Jag fick tänka: "Är detta vad vi gör som kyrka, Kristi brud?" Vi tar inte driftande från den smala och rätta vägen på allvar; vi tillåter att saker kommer in bland oss. Vi säger: "Det är ingen stor sak, låt oss inte vara kritiska." Men ju längre vi väntar, desto svårare blir det att räta upp. Först chockar det oss; senare blir det det nya normala. Hur ser vi om vi har drivit bort? Det borde vara lika enkelt som att fundera över var vi brukade vara, jämföra det med var vi är nu och sedan utvärdera förändringen med vad Bibeln lär.

Eftersom kampen mot avdrift inte är populär vill män i kyrkan inte göra det. Vissa människor i våra kyrkor som driver mot världen har förfinat ett feel-good-evangelium. De pratar om och om igen om hur nära de kommer Jesus och hur välsignade de är, men deras riktning stämmer tydligt inte med Skriftens undervisning. De är på väg mot världen.

Det finns andra som inte vill att kyrkan ska driva, ändå har de sina egna problem—kärlek till pengar, girighet och en kärlek till nöjen. Ingen säger något eftersom det verkar som att ingen vill höra. Ett vanligt svar är: "Ja, jag vet att det inte är bra, men vad kan vi göra?" "Alla kyrkor har problem." Eller "Ja, jag skulle aldrig tillåta det, men jag känner inte att det är min plats att säga något." "Det är inte för min familj, men om andra vill göra det går det bra."

Vi lever i en "jag"-tid. Allt handlar om mig. De konservativa anabaptistiska människorna blir intrasslade i sociala medier, selfies, tweeting, Facebook och vad du än kan tänka dig. Vi älskar oss själva så till den grad att vi talar, handlar och klär oss på sätt som drar uppmärksamhet till oss själva—vi marknadsför oss själva. Vi talar om att se bra ut, må bra och leva bra. Vad hände med att främja Jesus? Kom ihåg att Jesus sade: Ty den som vill spara sitt liv skall förlora det; och den som förlorar sitt liv för min skull skall vinna det – Matt 16:25.

Varför verkar det så svårt att se i vilken riktning vi går? Om allt handlar om oss själva, då handlar det inte om Jesus. Om vi är förtjusta i de senaste modefläckarna och de finaste bilarna, lastbilarna och husen, då handlar det inte om Jesus. Vi kan inte unna oss att behaga köttet och ändå säga att vi är kristna.

Jag blev nyligen tillfrågad varför vissa pastorer förlorar sina barn till världen. I de flesta fall tror jag att det är samma anledning som många anabaptister förlorar sina barn till mörkrets rike—fäderna har förlorat en gudfruktig vision för sina hem. De lever ett maktlöst liv och låter världen komma in. Kanske har de ingen TV, men vad sägs om internet? Det tillåter ändå världens inflytande att komma in. Dessutom tillbringar pappa mer tid med sitt företag och mer tid med att njuta av livet än att söka Guds ansikte.

Många amerikaner åker på korttidsmission. Ofta verkar det som att ungdomarna som åker vill slå sig ner på stranden eller söka andra nöjen och avkoppling så fort planet landat. Varför? För det är vad de lärs eller tillåts göra hemma—söka nöjen. De har inte fått lära sig att förneka köttet; de har inte sett sina föräldrar förneka köttet. Några av oss kan vara så långt från målet att vi behöver göra som snickaren i början av denna artikel—ödmjuka oss och börja om.

Män drar sina ovilliga hustrur in i världen, hustrur puttar sina män in i världen, och barn drar sina föräldrar in i världen. Och tyvärr, eftersom den moderna kyrkan har kastat av sig alla former av disciplin och struktur, kan alla stanna i kyrkan och förgifta den med sina världsliga idéer (åtminstone så länge du ler och säger att du älskar Jesus). Kom ihåg Skrifterna: Om ni älskar mig, håller ni mina bud – Joh 14:15. Och: Den som säger: Jag känner honom, och inte håller hans bud, han är en lögnare, och sanningen är icke i honom – 1 Joh 2:4.

Här är några områden där kyrkan driver.

Broderlig kärlek

På detta skall alla känna att ni är mina lärjungar, om ni älska varandra – Joh 13:35.

Människor har besökt vår kyrka och frågat om vi praktiserar den heliga kyssen. Jag svarar att det gör vi; dock kommer förståelsen av behovet att älska varandra först. Många kyrkor avskaffar den heliga kyssen, vilket klart är föreskrivet i Ordet. Och det verkar lämpligt eftersom de har slutat att älska varandra. Jag tror inte vi förstår hur viktig denna fråga är—att ha kärlek till varandra. När vår kärlek får oss att lida för varandra ser världen det. Ofta är anledningen till att ett broderskap slutar att älska varandra att de inte längre kämpar "tillsammans." De har blivit oberoende.

Några av de största akterna av att visa kärlek till varandra har skett på slagfältet. Män har hoppat på granater och stått framför kulor för att rädda sina kamrater. Eftersom de har kämpat tillsammans ser de efter varandra. Tänk om en soldat som marscherar ut i strid skulle se en kamrats magasin falla ur vapnet? Vad skulle han göra? Skulle han förbli tyst för att hans kamrat kanske blir arg? Eller skulle han förbli tyst för att han visste att han själv hade egna problem? Nej. Han skulle hjälpa sin bror. Om ogudaktiga män på slagfältet kan göra detta, varför kan inte Guds folk göra det i kyrkan? Före min omvändelse var jag i militären. Jag valde att lida för mitt land. Nu när jag är kristen väljer jag att lida för min Herre.

Klädsel

Detta är det mest uppenbara, men också det mest förbisedda. Den världsliga kyrkan säger: "Det är hjärtat som räknas, så hur vi ser ut på utsidan spelar ingen roll." Faller anabaptisterna för detta? Världen brukade klä sig blygsamt, men television och Hollywood började framhäva fokus på människokroppen. Säkert skulle inte kyrkan följa Hollywood. Men vad är skillnaden—en kvinna i världen som uppenbart är klädd oanstämt, eller en kvinna i kyrkan klädd i en cape-klänning som är figurnära, med en liten huvudduk som hänger tunt på bakhuvudet? Det är liten skillnad, förutom att den ena påstår sig vara kristen och den andra gör det inte. Kära vänner, världen skrattar åt oss.

Så hur börjar det? Subtilt. Först tar man bort en veckning här eller en rynkning där, sedan börjar man använda lite mindre tyg, slutligen börjar man köpa ljusare, starkare färger. Männen skjortan stoppas ut, man byter till jeans, sedan tighta jeans, knäpper upp ett par knappar, sparar ut håret lite. Köp ett par av de "coola" märkeskorna och en cowboyhatt. Djävulen är ingen dåre. Om du släpper en groda i kokande vatten hoppar den snabbt ut. Om du kokar vattnet som innehåller grodan kommer den långsamt att tillagas till döds. Är det för sent för oss att hoppa ut? Med Gud är allt möjligt. Bröder och systrar, det är hjärtat som räknas; och om vi önskar se ut som världen, är vårt hjärta världsligt och behöver bli rent—rent genom Jesu så kraftfulla blod.

Nöje

Ni har levat i nöje på jorden och varit frossare; ni har uppfyllt era hjärtan liksom på en slaktens dag. Ni har fördömt och dödat den rättfärdige, och han motsätter sig er icke – Jak 5:5-6.

Och det som föll ibland törnena, det är de som, när de hört, går fram och kvävs av livets bekymmer och rikedomar och nöjen och inte bär fram någon frukt till fullhet – Luk 8:14.

Men detta vet du också, att i de sista dagarna skall svåra tider komma. Ty människor skall då vara själviska, giriga, skrytsamma, stolta, hädare, olydiga mot föräldrar, otacksamma, ogudaktiga, utan naturlig kärlek, fredsbrottare, falska anklagare, otuktiga, hårda, förakta dem som är goda, förrädare, våghalsiga, högmodiga, älskare av nöjen mer än älskare av Gud; som äro med sken av gudfruktighet, men förneka dess kraft; sådana vänd dig ifrån – 2 Tim 3:1-5.

När vi ger oss åt nöjen skiljer vi oss från de lidanden vi blivit kallade till, och därigenom skiljer vi oss från den lön som mottages genom lidandet.

Kom ihåg, när vi ger vika lite i någon fråga under vår generation, kommer våra barn att gå längre med det. När våra barn tycker det är roligt att gå i kyrkan endast på grund av volleybollmatchen som är planerad efteråt, är det inte bra. När de vill åka på en missionsresa på grund av nöjena vid havet, är det inte bra. Jag säger inte att dessa ting är onda, men när de blir fokuspunkt har vi ett allvarligt problem. Tycker vi om att göra de saker Gud gläds åt? Tycker vi om psalmsång längre? Tycker vi om att hjälpa de fattiga? Hur är det med att besöka änkorna? Jag tror att om fäderna har sina prioriteringar rätt, och verkligen älskar att göra Guds saker även om köttet lider, då kommer så också våra barn (nästa generation) att göra, för vilka VI är ansvariga. Jag säger ofta till människor att de inte behöver följa Jesus. De kan älska världen och livets nöjen, men de kan inte fortsätta sitta i vår kyrka och låtsas vara kristna. Folk kanske säger att det är för hårt, men jag tror att Jesus sade samma sak. Jag vet dina gärningar, att du varken är kall eller het; ville du vore kall eller het. Eftersom du nu är ljummen, och varken kall eller het, skall jag spotta ut dig ur min mun – Upp 3:15-16.

Detta är inte en uttömmande lista eftersom det finns många andra sätt som kyrkan driver mot världen. Min bön är att, för det första, vi skulle se problemet, och för det andra, vi skulle ta itu med det. Kom ihåg att en liten jäst jäser hela degen. (1 Kor 5)

Det rasar en strid; mörkrets rike tränger sig på. Djävulen vet verkligen att han endast har en kort tid. Låt oss göra motstånd, lägga ner våra vita flaggor och lyfta våra svärd. Låt oss avlägsna förrädarna, världen och synden som har kommit in i kyrkan. Låt oss rena kyrkan och kämpa den goda troskampen.

Hur stoppar vi avdriften? Hur lämnar vi efter oss en trogen generation? Först behöver fäderna lära sina barn, och ledarna i kyrkan behöver undervisa dem alla. De tidiga anabaptisterna samlades så ofta de kunde, och det var vanligtvis ute i vädret, någonstans i skogen. Vår kyrka här samlas fem gånger i veckan. Att bara samlas på söndagar, tror jag, visar var våra prioriteringar ligger.

Och han gav några till apostlar, och några till profeter, och några till evangelister, och några till herdar och lärare, till utrustning för de heliga, till tjänstens verk, till uppbyggelse av Kristi kropp, till dess att vi alla nå fram till enhet i tron och kunskapen om Guds Son, till en fullkomlig man, till måttet av Kristi fullhet – Ef 4:11-13.

Det verkar som om Gud skulle ge oss lärare, pastorer, evangelister, profeter och apostlar om vi bara skulle använda dem.

Låt oss göra detta personligt—det kan finnas områden av avdrift i mitt liv. Vi måste hjälpa varandra innan vi alla driver in i undergång. Kanske kan vi hålla oss, men vi måste också vara oroade för våra barn. Om vi kunde samlas och vara ärliga mot oss själva och mot varandra om vad Skrifterna klart lär, då skulle vi vara mer försiktiga. Om vi kunde studera Guds Ord tillsammans, med öppna hjärtan och sinnen, tror jag vi kunde stärka det som återstår. Jag tror att om vi skulle falla ner på våra ansikten inför Gud, skulle Han hela våra kyrkor. Må Gud välsigna oss alla i en djupare vandring med Honom.

As we discussed in the first part of this two-part series, cancer is not a single entity. Various cancers have general similarities in that they develop from normal cells which mutate to make them grow in an uncontrolled, unnatural fashion, yet each type of cancer behaves in its specific, unique way.

Some cancers are aggressive, and some are much slower growing. Some tend to be localized and are quite slow to spread to other parts of the body, whereas others are likely to show up in locations far from where they began.

It is not possible to make blanket statements about cancers, but in this section, I will discuss some general things about prevention and treatment, then I’ll finish with some thoughts about us as Christians relating to someone who is dealing with cancer.

Lifestyle Changes to Prevent Cancers

Many of the things that increase the risk of cancer are things that (hopefully) we, as Christian people, are already avoiding.

Tobacco is one such thing. Tobacco, when smoked, increases the risk of lung cancer. It also increases the risk of head cancer, neck cancers, esophageal cancer, stomach cancer, and cancers of the liver and bladder.

Alcohol is another substance that raises the risk of cancer. Liver, voice box, and esophagus cancers are all related to alcohol consumption. Some people claim to drink alcohol for “health benefits,” but there is no safe level of alcohol consumption. Even people who drink moderately have an increased risk of death related to their alcohol usage.i

Another thing that should be limited is exposure to ultraviolet radiation. We know that UV radiation increases the risk of skin cancers, so wearing clothing that protects, such as hats and long-sleeved garments, and using sunblock can reduce this risk.

On the positive side of things, healthy eating habits, such as consuming lots of fruits and vegetables and avoiding highly processed foods, will reduce the risk of colon cancer.ii Fiber seems to be a key here and higher levels of dietary fiber are helpful. Additionally, fruits and vegetables are rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals and are supportive of a healthy immune system. It is recommended to eat at least two servings of fruit and five servings of vegetables per day.

It is interesting that while people who eat healthy diets have a decreased risk of cancer, there is little evidence that there are specific vitamins that will prevent cancer. That is, there is little benefit if you eat a very unhealthy diet and then take vitamins in an effort to compensate for your unwise choices.

Prior to doing a controlled test it is always hard to know whether or not a certain supplement will help. Vitamin E is an antioxidant and so it was thought to be helpful in the prevention of cancer. However, it turns out that studies have not shown this to be true. Actually, in high doses, it seems to increase the risk of certain cancers and heart disease.iii

Rather than trying to find the right supplements, it is more important to make certain that we are eating healthy diets.

Chemotherapy

Now, let us move to a brief discussion about different types of treatment for cancer. Chemotherapy is probably what most people think of first. It was first used in the 1940s when doctors used a derivative of nitrogen mustard to treat lymphoma.

Since that time, hundreds of different medications have been developed as chemotherapy, designed to attack the cancer cells. It is hard to generalize about chemotherapy because there are so many different medications designed to treat different cancers and because they have different side effects.

Due to the fact that they attack cells that are rapidly multiplying, many of these drugs tend to make a person’s hair fall out since hair cells are of the rapidly multiplying type. Nausea, vomiting, and blood count alterations (low white cell counts) are other common side effects.

If a cancer has spread from its initial location, chances are good that it will require more than just one type of medication in order to achieve remission.

Even if a cancer hasn’t spread, surgeons will often recommend doing some chemotherapy ahead of surgery to shrink the tumor and to make surgical removal easier.

While chemotherapy sounds scary, it actually works quite well for certain types of cancers, such as blood cancers (like leukemias), lymphoma, and breast cancer.

These days, cancer doctors test the biopsied cancer cells for genetic markers. As a family doctor, I see these reports but, since I am not a specialist in this field, I find them somewhat confusing. The important thing to remember is that these markers help to predict what the best drugs are to use on a specific type of cancer.

Surgery

For many years, surgery was the cornerstone of cancer treatment. Cancers that have not spread can be removed entirely, allowing a person to move forward without any further treatment.

Often, by the time that a person’s cancer is discovered, it is too late to completely remove it. Surgery can still be helpful. For one thing, it gives a sample of the cancer for testing to help identify the best treatment. More than that, even if a cancer has spread, there are times that a tumor needs to be removed, simply because of the organs that it is putting pressure on.

I have heard some people claim that it is dangerous for a cancer to be exposed to oxygen. They believe that cancer cells spread faster after the tissues are opened up and exposed to the air during surgery. There is no documented evidence to support this idea. Many people do seem to get sicker after having an exploratory surgery when their cancer is being diagnosed. But the issue isn’t really the air getting into the cancer cells, rather the cancer was most certainly at the point of beginning to exhibit serious symptoms, and the surgery simply brought things to a head. Also, any surgery will be stressful for any person’s body, which will only increase the wearing down of a person’s already taxed strength and vitality—their ability to stay on top of a debilitating illness.

Typically, when a tumor is removed, nearby lymph glands will be sampled to see if they contain cancer cells. This presence, or absence, of cells helps with the “staging” of the cancer (such as “stage 3” or “stage 4”) and will provide insight for further treatment to prevent a chance of recurrence.

Immunotherapy

One of the newest treatments of cancer is called immunotherapy. These are medications that rev up a patient’s immune system to clear their body of cancer cells.

This sounds great and you would think the side effects should be minimal. Unfortunately, it doesn’t always work according to plan. Some cancers don’t respond to these sorts of treatments. And as far as side effects go, these medications can result in autoimmune diseases. When a medication is prescribed that makes the immune system extra active (or over-active), sometimes it begins to attack the patient’s own organs. While some of these side effects get better with the cessation of treatment, not all of them go away.

As an example, I had a patient who took immunotherapy for melanoma that had spread to his lymph glands. He was cured of the cancer, but the immunotherapy damaged his saliva glands enough that he has ongoing issues with a dry mouth. At this point, it seems unlikely that he will regain that moisture in his mouth.

Future Treatments

There will probably be more treatments in the future, targeting specific types of cancers. Something that is currently under investigation are vaccines that would target specific types of cancers. Currently none of these are available except in clinical trials.

Choosing Wisely

Oncologists (cancer specialists) do not know the future. They talk in terms of percentages. One protocol has an 86 percent chance of achieving a two-year remission from cancer, another only 56 percent. The same thing is true for side effects. While a doctor can tell you that 26 percent of patients get nauseated with a treatment, that doesn’t tell you if you will be one of that 26 percent and whether that nausea will be controllable with anti-nausea medication.

In deciding what course of treatment to choose, you will find no Bible passage to indicate one direction or another. Having a good oncologist who will explain things carefully—both the chance of success and risk of side effects—is key. There are times that you may need to change to a different cancer doctor, simply because the one you have does not take the time that you need to feel comfortable with your treatment.

If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –James 1:5. We need wisdom in many areas of our lives, but certainly choosing how to navigate medical decisions is one of those areas. It is a wonderful thing that God has promised to give us the wisdom that we need—if we just ask.

Prayer—both personal prayer and by your church community—is very important. Prayers can be for healing. It can also be for caring, Christian, medical caregivers, and for wisdom in choosing the best treatments.

Sometimes God cures through doctors and medications. Sometimes, He heals in spite of them. Sometimes He decides it is time for us to go home to be with Him, thereby providing us with a new body that is not sick and broken.

Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases –Psalm 103:2-3. With all of the medical technology available to us, it is easy to forget that healing comes from God. All the chemotherapy in the world will not avail if God does not work an act of healing. At the same time, there are many times that God works in miraculous ways to heal despite the dire predictions made by the medical professionals or other well-meaning individuals.

Often the best that a patient can do is to choose (according to their best judgment) the best treatment course (based on success rate and side effects) and then see how things go. If the side effects are too severe or the treatment doesn’t seem to be working, there is always the option to change.

Ultimately, when healing comes, regardless of how it comes, it is God that provides that healing. Let us never forget that.

Cancer Takes Energy

Relating to someone with cancer is not much different from relating to a person with any other chronic illness. There are differences though.

Both having cancer and receiving treatment for the cancer takes a lot of energy out of a person. While it is important not to ignore someone who has cancer, it is just as important to remember that they do not have endless energy supplies. A ten- or fifteen-minute visit may be all that they can handle. It is best to let them decide the length of visits that they have energy for.

Hesitate to Give Advice

Your “cousin” may have had cancer and may have gotten better after taking a particular supplement or visiting a particular clinic. Sharing that information with a person who is dealing with cancer is just one more piece of information for them to process out of a “thousand” others they may have received. It seems as though someone with cancer is often bombarded with advice and recommendations from well-meaning friends and family.

It is hard to figure out what the best thing is to do when a person is already low on energy. Sometimes, cancer patients simply have prayed that God would bless their choices and then have left the outcome in His hands.

If the cancer patient asks for your input, you can give it, but if not, it is probably best to hold off on the temptation to give unsought advice.

Listen

There is never a situation where listening isn’t beneficial. It is through listening that we allow others to unburden themselves from fears and frustrations. Listening can help the person to put their thoughts into words. More than that, we may hear ways in which we can help.

Maybe it is someone telling you the (too long) story of how their doctor missed their cancer. Or perhaps, it is them telling you about their fears regarding either their cancer or their treatments.

Pray

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16. This verse comes in the midst of James talking about anointing with oil, confession of sins, and physical healing.

We can certainly pray for, and with, someone who is dealing with cancer. Listening helps us to know how best we can pray for them. It lets us know what their particular struggle is on a given day and how we can best lift them up to the throne.

The passage in James makes it clear that healing does not come from the oil that is poured over someone, but rather from God’s work in their life. The prayer, the faith, and the obedient action is more important than the anointing oil, although all demonstrate a dependence on a God who is always faithful.

Do Small Chores

If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? –James 2:15-16.

If it is not enough to pray for someone who is dealing with a serious illness, it is certainly not enough to tell them, “God bless you.”

Figuring out what things someone with cancer needs help with may not be easy, but often even little tasks are difficult for them. It could be that they need transportation to a chemotherapy appointment. Maybe they need help with making a meal, with childcare, or with cleaning their house. Helping in whatever ways we can makes a huge difference for those who are dealing with the fatigue and stress of cancer.

More than that, the important thing is that we make the effort to demonstrate our love to those in our church body who are suffering. Paul told the Corinthians that when …one member suffer[s], all the members suffer with it… –1 Corinthians 12:26. Whenever there is a need, the rest of the local church body has an obligation and should have a deep desire to help in whatever way they can.

Be Willing to Keep Your Distance

Chemotherapy can cause a cancer patient to have an extremely weak immune system. A normal white cell count is between 4,000 and 10,000. but during cancer treatments I have seen patient’s white cell count drop down to 200. In this scenario, if they catch any type of infection, they will be unable to fight off that infection and will end up in the hospital.

It is important to understand that someone in this condition who chooses to keep their distance is not necessarily trying to avoid fellowship. Rather, they are trying to avoid an unneeded hospital stay for what cancer doctors call a “neutropenic fever” (a febrile illness with a really low white cell count).

In these sorts of situations, phone calls or even text messages go a long way toward helping a brother or sister feel that they are not alone, even when they cannot physically be around other people.

Conclusion

I wish I could give a complete run down of every type of cancer out there and the best treatment for each one. That would be beyond my capability and further, it would be outdated within six months’ time.

What I can say is that prayer is key. Prayer for the Holy Spirit’s leading (see John 16:13), for energy for each day, for healing, and for God’s will to be done. Most of all, we need to pray that God would be glorified in and through us. (See 1 Peter 4:11) There have been so many people who were able to speak to their nurses and doctors about their Lord, even as they dealt with side effects and cancer symptoms.

It is easy to read all the instructions about giving up worrying that is found in Scripture and think that it should be easy to cast our cares on Him (see 1 Peter 5:7). However, it is much harder to put into practice. We may feel one day as though we have conquered fear and wake up the next morning with every bit as much anxiety as we ever had.

It is in this that we desperately need a church community. We are not alone, but we will feel alone unless we have brothers and sisters around us who help us as they are able and who pray for us in our valleys and rejoice with us in our times of victory.

It is only then, that we can come to the place that the Apostle Paul did when he said, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. Of course, he was talking about a possible execution, but his resignation to God’s will was total. I pray that we too might reach that place, even as we deal with something as difficult as cancer.

Kama tulivyojadili katika sehemu ya kwanza ya mfululizo huu wa sehemu mbili, kansa si kitu kimoja tu. Aina mbalimbali za kansa zinafanana kwa ujumla kwa kuwa hutokea kutoka kwa seli za kawaida ambazo hubadilika na kuzifanya zikue kwa njia isiyo ya kawaida na isiyodhibitiwa, lakini kila aina ya kansa huenda inapenda kujiendeleza kwa njia yake maalum na ya kipekee.

Kuna kansa ambazo ni kali, na kuna nyingine zinazokua kwa taratibu. Baadhi zinapendelea kukaa eneo moja na huwa polepole kuenea sehemu nyingine za mwili, wakati nyingine zina uwezekano mkubwa wa kuonekana kwenye maeneo mbali na pale zilipoanza.

Haiwezekani kutoa matamko ya jumla kuhusu kansa, lakini katika sehemu hii, nitajadili mambo ya jumla kuhusu utokomezaji na matibabu, kisha nitaisha kwa mawazo kuhusu sisi kama Wakristo tukihusiana na mtu ambaye anashughulika na kansa.

Mabadiliko ya Maisha Kuzuia Kansa

Mengi kati ya vitu vinavyoongeza hatari ya kansa ni vitu ambavyo (kwa matumaini) sisi, kama watu wa Kikristo, tayari tunaziepuka.

Tumbaku ni mojawapo ya vitu hivyo. Tumbaku, wakati unavyovutwa, huongeza hatari ya kansa ya mapafu. Pia huongeza hatari ya kansa za kichwa, shingo, koo, tumbo, na za ini na kibofu cha mkojo.

Pombe ni dutu nyingine inayoongeza hatari ya kansa. Kansa za ini, sanduku la sauti (kipafu cha sauti), na koo yote yanahusishwa na matumizi ya pombe. Watu wengine hujieleza kunywa pombe kwa ajili ya “faida za kiafya,” lakini hakuna kiwango salama cha matumizi ya pombe. Hata watu wanaonywa kwa kiasi cha wastani wana hatari iliyoongezeka ya kifo inayohusiana na matumizi yao ya pombe.i

Jambo jingine linalopaswa kupunguzwa ni kuwekwa chini ya mionzi ya ultraviolet. Tunajua kuwa mionzi ya UV huongeza hatari ya kansa ya ngozi, hivyo kuvaa nguo zinazolinda, kama vile kofia na nguo zenye mikono mirefu, pamoja na kutumia krimu ya kujikinga na jua kunaweza kupunguza hatari hii.

Katika upande mzuri wa mambo, tabia za kula kiafya, kama kutumia matunda na mboga kwa wingi na kuepuka vyakula vilivyochakatwa sana, zitapunguza hatari ya kansa ya utumbo mkubwa (colon).ii Wiani wa nyuzinyuzi (fiber) unaonekana kuwa muhimu hapa na viwango vya juu vya nyuzinyuzi vya lishe vinasaidia. Zaidi ya hayo, matunda na mboga ni tajiri kwa antioxidants, vitamini, na madini na vinasaidia mfumo wa kinga kuwa mzuri. Inashauriwa kula angalau sehemu mbili za matunda na sehemu tano za mboga kwa siku.

Inavutia kuwa wakati watu wanaokula mlo mzuri wana hatari ndogo ya kansa, kuna ushahidi mdogo kwamba kuna vitamini maalum zitakazozuia kansa. Yaani, kuna faida kidogo ikiwa utakula mlo mbaya sana kisha unywe vitamini kama jitihada ya kukosa ulivyochagua kihisia.

Kabla ya kufanya jaribio lililodhibitiwa mara zote ni vigumu kujua kama nyongeza fulani itasaidia. Vitamini E ni antioxidant na hivyo ilidhaniwa itasaidia katika kuzuia kansa. Hata hivyo, imekuwa wazi kuwa tafiti hazijaonyesha hili kuwa kweli. Kwa kweli, kwa dozi kubwa, inaonekana kuongeza hatari ya aina fulani za kansa na magonjwa ya moyo.iii

Badala ya kujaribu kutafuta nyongeza sahihi, ni muhimu zaidi kuhakikisha kwamba tunakula milo yenye afya.

Chemotherapia

Sasa, tuende kwenye mjadala mfupi kuhusu aina tofauti za matibabu ya kansa. Chemotherapia labda ndiyo mtu wengi wanafikiria kwanza. Ilitumika mara ya kwanza katika miaka ya 1940 pale madaktari walipotumia dume la nitrojeni (derivative of nitrogen mustard) kutibu lymphoma.

Tangu wakati huo, dawa mia kadhaa zimeundwa kama chemotherapia, zikiwa zimetengenezwa kushambulia seli za kansa. Ni vigumu kufanya jumla kuhusu chemotherapia kwa sababu kuna dawa nyingi tofauti zilizoundwa kutibu aina tofauti za kansa na kwa sababu zina athari mbaya tofauti.

Kutokana na ukweli kwamba zinashambulia seli zinazojidondosha kwa kasi, dawa nyingi za aina hii hupelekea mtu kupoteza nywele kwa kuwa seli za nywele ni aina inayojidondosha kwa kasi. Kutapika, kutapika kwa mkongo, na mabadiliko ya hesabu za damu (hesabu za seli nyepesi chini) ni athari nyingine za kawaida.

Kama kansa imeenea kutoka eneo lililokuwa mwanzo, kuna uwezekano mkubwa itahitaji zaidi ya aina moja ya dawa ili kufikia ukimya wa dalili (remission).

Hata kama kansa haijaenea, madaktari wa upasuaji mara nyingi watapendekeza kufanya chemotherapia kabla ya upasuaji ili kupunguza uvimbe na kufanya uondoaji wa upasuaji kuwa rahisi.

Wakati chemotherapia inasikika kutisha, kweli hufanya kazi vizuri kwa aina fulani za kansa, kama vile kansa za damu (kama leukaemia), lymphoma, na kansa ya matiti.

Sasa hivi, madaktari wa kansa huchunguza seli za kansa zilizochukuliwa kwa biopsi kwa alama za kijeni. Kama daktari wa familia, ninaona ripoti hizi lakini, kwa kuwa mimi si mtaalamu wa fani hii, zinanivuruga kidogo. Jambo muhimu kukumbuka ni kwamba alama hizi husaidia kutabiri ni dawa gani bora kutumia kwa aina maalum ya kansa.

Upasuaji

Kwa miaka mingi, upasuaji ulikuwa nguzo ya matibabu ya kansa. Kansa ambazo hazijaenea zinaweza kuondolewa kabisa, na kumruhusu mtu kuendelea bila matibabu zaidi.

Mara nyingi, wakati kansa ya mtu inagunduliwa, ni kuchelewa kuizuia kabisa. Upasuaji bado unaweza kuwa na msaada. Kwa jambo moja, unatoa sampuli ya kansa kwa ajili ya vipimo kusaidia kutambua matibabu bora. Zaidi ya hapo, hata kama kansa imeenea, kuna nyakati ambapo uvimbe unahitaji kuondolewa, kwa sababu tu waingilia ndani ya viungo vinavyoweka shinikizo.

Nimesikia baadhi ya watu wakidai kuwa ni hatari kwa kansa kufichuliwa kwa oksijeni. Wanaamini kuwa seli za kansa zinaenea kwa kasi zaidi baada ya tishu kufunguliwa na kufichuliwa katika hewa wakati wa upasuaji. Hakuna ushahidi uliowekwa kuunga mkono wazo hili. Watu wengi wanaonekana kuwa wagonjwa zaidi baada ya upasuaji wa uchunguzi wakati kansa yao inatambuliwa. Lakini suala si kweli hewa kuingia kwenye seli za kansa, bali kansa ilikuwa kwa hakika imekuwa ikianza kuonyesha dalili kali, na upasuaji ulileta mambo wazi. Pia, upasuaji wowote utakuwa mzigo kwa mwili wa mtu, jambo litakaloongeza tu kupoteza nguvu na uhai wa mtu aliyeshindwa—uwezo wao wa kukabiliana na ugonjwa unaochosha.

Mara nyingi, uvimbe ukiondolewa, vitu vya limfu zenye karibu vitachukuliwa sampuli kuona kama vina seli za kansa. Uwepo au kutokuwepo kwa seli hizi husaidia katika “kustaiaji” (kama “sikio la 3” au “sikio la 4”) na itatoa mwanga kwa matibabu zaidi ili kuzuia nafasi ya kurudi kwa kansa.

Immunotherapia

Mojawapo ya matibabu mapya ya kansa huitwa immunotherapia. Hizi ni dawa zinazochochea mfumo wa kinga wa mgonjwa ili kuondoa seli za kansa mwilini mwao.

Hii inasikika nzuri na mtu angeweza kufikiria kuwa athari zake za pembeni zinapaswa kuwa ndogo. Kwa bahati mbaya, si mara zote zinakwenda kama ilivyopangwa. Baadhi ya kansa hazitoki kwa matibabu ya aina hizi. Na kuhusu athari za pembeni, dawa hizi zinaweza kusababisha magonjwa ya kinga mwilini (autoimmune diseases). Wakati dawa inapotolewa ambayo inafanya mfumo wa kinga kuwa na shughuli nyingi (au kupitiliza), wakati mwingine huanza kushambulia viungo vya mgonjwa mwenyewe. Ingawa baadhi ya athari hizi za pembeni huwa bora baada ya kuacha matibabu, si zote zinaondoka.

Kama mfano, nilikuwa na mgonjwa aliyechukuliwa immunotherapia kwa melanoma ambayo ilikuwa imeenea hadi kwa vifundo vya limfu. Alipona kutoka kwa kansa, lakini immunotherapia iliharibu tezi za mate kwa kiasi kwamba ana matatizo ya kudumu ya kavu ya kinywa. Hivi sasa, inaonekana hawezi kupata tena unyevu huo katika kinywa chake.

Matibabu ya Baadaye

Huenda kutakuwa na matibabu zaidi kwa siku zijazo, zikilenga aina maalum za kansa. Kitu ambacho kwa sasa kinachunguzwa ni chanjo zitakazolenga aina maalum za kansa. Hivi sasa hakuna kati yao zinapatikana isipokuwa katika majaribio ya kliniki.

Kuchagua Kwa Busara

Onkolojisti (mataalamu wa kansa) hawajui siku za usoni. Wanaongea kwa istilahi za asilimia. Mchakato mmoja una nafasi ya asilimia 86 ya kufikia ukimya wa dalili kwa miaka miwili, mwingine ni asilimia 56 tu. Hali ile ile ni kweli kwa athari za pembeni. Wakati daktari anaweza kukuambia kuwa asilimia 26 ya wagonjwa wanahisi kichefuchefu kwa matibabu, hilo halikuambii kama utakuwa miongoni mwa asilimia 26 hiyo na kama kichefuchefu hicho kitatibika kwa dawa za kupunguza kichefuchefu.

Kutokana na uamuzi wa njia gani ya matibabu kuchagua, hautapati kifungu cha Biblia kinachoonyesha upande mmoja au mwingine. Kuwa na onkologisti mzuri atakayeeleza mambo kwa uwazi—pamoja na nafasi ya mafanikio na hatari za athari za pembeni—ni muhimu. Kuna nyakati ambapo unaweza kuhitaji kubadilisha daktari wa kansa, kwa sababu tu yule uliyenayo hatochukua muda unaohitaji ili ujihisi uko katika hali ya kuaminika na matibabu yako.

Kama mmoja kati yenu anakosa busara, na aombe kwa Mungu, ambaye hutoa kwa wote kwa wingi, wala hamtakisi; naye atampa –Yakobo 1:5. Tunahitaji busara katika nyanja nyingi za maisha yetu, lakini bila shaka kuchagua jinsi ya kuendesha maamuzi ya matibabu ni mojawapo ya nyanja hizo. Ni jambo zuri kwamba Mungu ameahidi kutupa busara tunayohitaji—ikiwa tu tunaomba.

Mwomba waumini—sala binafsi pamoja na ile ya jamii ya kanisa lako—ni muhimu sana. Maombi yanaweza kuwa kwa ajili ya uponyaji. Pia yanaweza kuwa kwa ajili ya watoa huduma za afya wanaomtendea mtu kimawazo ya Kikristo, na kwa ajili ya busara katika kuchagua matibabu bora.

Mara nyingine Mungu anaponya kupitia kwa madaktari na dawa. Wakati mwingine Huponya licha yao. Wakati mwingine Huamua kwamba ni wakati wetu kurudi nyumbani kwa Yeye, na hivyo kutupatia mwili mpya usio mgonjwa na usiovunjika.

Bariki, Ee BWANA, roho yangu, wala usisahau yote faida zake: Yeye anayekusamehe hata dhambi zako zote; Yeye anayaponya magonjwa yako yote –Zaburi 103:2-3. Kwa teknolojia yote ya matibabu iliyo mbele yetu, ni rahisi kusahau kwamba uponyaji unatoka kwa Mungu. Chemotherapia yote ya dunia haitakuwa na maana ikiwa Mungu hatatenda tendo la uponyaji. Wakati huo huo, mara nyingi Mungu hutenda kwa njia za muujiza kuponya licha ya utabiri mbaya uliotolewa na wataalamu wa matibabu au watu wengine wenye nia njema.

Mara nyingi bora kwa mgonjwa ni kuchagua (kulingana na hukumu yao bora) mkondo bora wa matibabu (kulingana na kiwango cha mafanikio na athari za pembeni) na kisha kuona jinsi mambo yatakavyoenda. Ikiwa athari za pembeni ni kali sana au matibabu hayaonekani kufanya kazi, daima kuna nafasi ya kubadilisha.

Kwa mwisho, pale uponyaji unapokuja, bila kujali jinsi ulivyojengwa, ni Mungu ndiye anayetoa uponyaji huo. Tusisahau hilo kamwe.

Kansa Hutumia Nguvu

Kuhusiana na mtu mwenye kansa si tofauti kubwa sana na kuhusiana na mtu mwenye ugonjwa mwingine sugu. Hata hivyo kuna tofauti.

Kuwa na kansa na kupokea matibabu ya kansa kunachukua nguvu nyingi kutoka kwa mtu. Wakati ni muhimu kutoeza mtu mwenye kansa, ni muhimu pia kukumbuka kwamba hawana akiba ya nguvu isiyo na kikomo. Ziara ya dakika kumi au kumi na tano inaweza kuwa ni yote wanaweza kuvumilia. Ni bora kuwaacha wao waamua urefu wa ziara wanayo kuwa nayo kwa nguvu zao.

Tikisika Kutoa Ushauri

“Binamu” wako anaweza kuwa amepitia kansa na akapona baada ya kutumia virutubisho fulani au kutembelea kliniki fulani. Kushiriki habari hiyo na mtu anayeishi na kansa ni kipande kingine tu cha habari kwao kuchanganua miongoni mwa “elfu” nyingine walizopokea. Inaonekana mtu mwenye kansa mara nyingi anapalaumiwa kwa ushauri na mapendekezo kutoka kwa marafiki na familia wenye nia njema.

Ni vigumu kubaini nini cha kufanya wakati mtu tayari hana nguvu nyingi. Wakati mwingine, wagonjwa wa kansa huomba tu kwamba Mungu ambariki chaguo zao na kisha wauache matokeo mikononi Mwake.

Kama mgonjwa wa kansa akikuomba maoni yako, unaweza kuyatoa, lakini ikiwa hapofuati, labda ni bora kujizuia kutaka kutoa ushauri usioulizwa.

Sikiliza

Hakuna hali ambapo kusikiliza hakutakuwa na faida. Kupitia kusikiliza tunamruhusu mwingine kuachilia hofu na hasira zao. Kusikiliza kunaweza kumsaidia mtu kuweka mawazo yao kwa maneno. Zaidi ya hayo, tunaweza kusikia njia ambazo tunaweza kusaidia.

Labda ni mtu anayekuambia hadithi ndefu jinsi daktari wao alivyokosa kansa yao. Au labda ni wanakulia kuhusu hofu zao zinazohusiana na kansa yao au matibabu yao.

Tafakari

…Sala yenye nguvu ya mwaminifu ina faida tele –Yakobo 5:16. Aya hii inakuja katikati ya Yakobo anayezungumzia kupaka mafuta kwa mafuta, kukiri dhambi, na uponyaji wa kimwili.

Tunaweza bila shaka kuomba, na kuomba pamoja na, mtu anayeshughulika na kansa. Kusikiliza kunatusaidia kujua ni jinsi gani tunapaswa kuwaombea. Kunatuambia ni mapambano yao maalum siku fulani na jinsi tunavyoweza kuwaweka juu ya kiti cha enzi kwa sala zetu.

Sehemu katika Yakobo inaonyesha wazi kuwa uponyaji haukatoki kwa mafuta yaliyomwagwa juu ya mtu, bali kutoka kwa kazi ya Mungu maishani mwao. Sala, imani, na tendo la utii ni muhimu zaidi kuliko mafuta ya kupaka, ingawa zote zinaonyesha utegemezi kwa Mungu ambaye ni mwaminifu daima.

Fanya Kazi Ndogo za Nyumbani

Ikiwa ndugu au dada wako wako uchi, na hawana chakula cha kila siku, na mmoja wenu akawaambia, Nenda kwa amani, msimizeni na msongwe; na hamwatolei vitu vya mwili; je, itawafaidishaje? –Yakobo 2:15-16.

Ikiwa si vya kutosha kumuombea mtu anayeishi na ugonjwa mzito, hakika si vya kutosha kumwambia, “Mungu akubariki.”

Kubaini mambo ambayo mtu mwenye kansa anahitaji msaada nayo inaweza kuwa si rahisi, lakini mara nyingi hata kazi ndogo ni ngumu kwao. Inaweza kuwa wanahitaji usafiri kwenda miadi ya chemotherapia. Labda wanahitaji msaada kuandaa chakula, kwa malezi ya watoto, au kwa kusafisha nyumba yao. Kusaidia kwa wayo te tunazoweza kunafanya tofauti kubwa kwa wale wanaokabiliana na uchovu na msongo wa kansa.

Zaidi ya hayo, jambo muhimu ni kwamba tuchukue juhudi kuonyesha upendo wetu kwa wale walioko ndani ya mwili wa kanisa letu wanaoteseka. Paulo aliwaambia Wakorintho kwamba …wakati mmoja anateseka, wanashiriki wote pamoja naye… –1 Wakorintho 12:26. Kila wakati kuna hitaji, sehemu nyingine ya kanisa la mahali ina wajibu na inapaswa kuwa na tamaa kubwa ya kusaidia kwa njia yoyote wanayoweza.

Kua Tayari Kuhifadhi Umbali Wako

Chemotherapia inaweza kusababisha mfumo wa kinga wa mgonjwa wa kansa kuwa dhaifu sana. Hesabu ya kawaida ya seli nyeupe ni kati ya 4,000 na 10,000, lakini wakati wa matibabu ya kansa nimeona hesabu za seli nyeupe za mgonjwa zipungua hadi 200. Katika hali hii, kama watapata aina yoyote ya maambukizi, hawataweza kupambana na maambukizi hayo na watamalizika hospitalini.

Ni muhimu kuelewa kwamba mtu katika hali hii anayechagua kuzuia kukaribia si lazima anajaribu kuepuka ushirika. Badala yake, wanajaribu kuepuka kujazwa hospitalini kwa kile madaktari wa kansa wanaita “homa ya neutropenia” (ugonjwa wenye homa na hesabu ya chini sana ya seli nyeupe).

Katika aina hizi za hali, simu za simu au hata ujumbe wa maandishi hufanya mengi kuwahisisha ndugu au dada kwamba hawako peke yao, hata wanapoweza kukaribia kimwili watu wengine.

Hitimisho

Ningependa niweze kutoa orodha kamili ya kila aina ya kansa iliyopo na matibabu bora kwa kila moja. Hilo lingekuwa nje ya uwezo wangu na zaidi ya hayo, lingeisha ndani ya miezi sita.

Ni ninachoweza kusema ni kwamba sala ni muhimu. Sala kwa ajili ya uongozi wa Roho Mtakatifu (tazama Yoh 16:13), kwa nguvu za kila siku, kwa uponyaji, na kwa kutimizwa kwa mapenzi ya Mungu. Zaidi ya yote, tunahitaji kuomba kwamba Mungu atukamatishe katika na kupitia sisi. (Tazama 1 Petro 4:11) Kumekuwa na watu wengi walioweza kuongea na wauguzi na madaktari wao kuhusu Bwana wao, hata walipokuwa wakikabiliana na athari za pembeni na dalili za kansa.

Ni rahisi kusoma maagizo yote kuhusu kuacha kuwa na wasiwasi yanayopatikana katika Maandiko na kufikiri kwamba kutakuwa rahisi kuwarejesha mawazo yetu kwake (tazama 1 Petro 5:7). Hata hivyo, ni ngumu zaidi kutekeleza. Tunaweza kujihisi siku moja kwamba tumeushinda hofu na kuamka asubuhi iliyofuata tukiwa na wasiwasi mwingi kama tulivyokuwa hapo awali.

Ni katika hili ambapo tunahitaji jamii ya kanisa kwa uamuzi. Hatuwezi kuwa peke yetu, lakini tutahisi peke ikiwa hatuna ndugu na dada karibu nasi ambao hutusaidia kadri wanavyoweza na ambao hutuombea katika mabonde yetu na kufurahi nasi wakati wa ushindi wetu.

Ni tu kisha, tunaweza kufika mahali ambapo Mtume Paulo alifika alipotamka, Kwangu kuishi ni Kristo, na kufa ni faida –Wafilipi 1:21. Bila shaka, alikuwa akizungumza kuhusu adhabu ya kifo inayoweza kutokea, lakini kukubali kwake mapenzi ya Mungu kulikuwa kamili. Ninaomba pia sisi tufikie mahali hapo, hata tunapokabiliana na kitu kigumu kama kansa.

This hymn is universally thought to be one of the greatest hymns ever authored by a woman. It can be found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. This hymn writer was a woman of great ambition and enjoyment; a person full of life, vivacious, beautiful, talented, and a person who’s “exalted character always made a deep impression upon all who knew her”. Although she had a full and productive life, it was short, hastened on by her delicate and frail constitution. This hymn story has touched many lives in times of distress and hardship, including death. It has been used of God to draw the hearts of men from their present distresses, heavenward, to the immortal realities beyond this life.

Sarah Flower Adam was born at Harlow, England on February 22, 1805, to Benjamin and Eliza Flower. When she was five years old, her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis. Sarah and her older sister Eliza also inherited the same physical weakness. Speaking of the hymn writer I quote from 101 Hymn Stories: “She was also widely known for her many literary accomplishments, though her delicate health was always a handicap for her many ambitions.”

In the year 1834, at the age of 29, Sarah married a prominent inventor and civil engineer, John Brydges. This distinguished couple made their home in London, England for the duration of their marriage, until the hymn writer’s death fourteen years later in 1848, at the early age of 43.

Sarah and her older sister Eliza made an outstanding team in the realm of music—writing and composing new songs. The elder sister being an accomplished musician, and the younger the hymn writer. One day their pastor, the Rev. William Johnson Fox, asked these two exceptional sisters if they would help him with the compilation for a new hymnal for his congregation. They committed to the project, and soon were busily occupied in helping him complete the song book. “Together, they contributed thirteen texts and sixty-two new tunes.”

One day as the two sisters were pressing into the task at hand, the pastor remarked that he wished he could have a hymn written to conclude a sermon he was preparing to preach on the account of Jacob and Esau. Eliza interrupted enthusiastically, “Sarah, now there’s an excellent idea for a new hymn for our hymnal. Why don’t you write your own hymn about Jacob’s dream?”

“Splendid!” replied the pastor. Later that day, after spending much time studying the Genesis account, absorbing the atmosphere, and feeling the dramatic movement of this Old Testament narrative, Sarah began to write. Soon she had versified the complete Biblical story into these five stanzas of the immortal hymn still in use today.

Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song would be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven:
All that Thou send’st to me
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with Thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Or if on joyful wing
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upwards I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

This great hymn was written in 1840 and published the next year in the hymn book Hymns and Anthems prepared by Rev. Fox, the hymn writer’s pastor. The hymn’s original tune was a composition of Eliza, Sarah’s older sister. In 1844, Rev. James Freeman Clarke introduced the hymn in America, but it did not become well known for another 12 years. At that point the hymn was wedded with the present-day tune “Bethany” composed especially for the text by Lowell Mason, who is sometimes referred to as the father of American church and school music. Other hymns by Mason include “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains”, “When I Survey the Wondrous Cross”, “A Charge to Keep I Have”, “Joy to the World”, “My Faith Looks Up to Thee”, and “O Day of Rest and Gladness”.

Many very interesting accounts have been recorded in conjunction with the use of this hymn, and its effect on those who sang it or heard it sung. In the Boston Peace Jubilee of 1872, which commemorated the end of the civil war, this hymn, “Nearer, My God to Thee”, was sung by 50,000 voices. In 1871, three renowned theologians, Professors Hitchcock, Smith, and Park, were traveling in Palestine, when they heard the faint strains of “Bethany” reach their ears. Regarding this incident, I quote from A Treasury of Hymn Stories, “Drawing near, to their amazement, they saw fifty Syrian students standing under some trees in a circle, and singing in Arabic ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee,’ Professor Hitchcock, speaking afterward of the event, said that the singing of that Christian hymn by those Syrian youths moved him to tears, and affected him more than any singing he had ever heard before”.

During the Johnstown City Flood of May 31, 1889 (a tragic disaster that killed over 2,000 people), an unfortunate railroad train rushed into the swirling flood waters. A young woman, prepared to be a missionary, and on her way to the far east, became one of those trapped in a railroad car which was turned up on end. Beyond the hope of rescue, she spoke calmly to the awe-struck crowd as they gazed helplessly at the unfolding tragedy as the car sank beneath the muddy waters. As she sang, she passed away, coming indeed nearer to her God whom she loved and desired to serve.

Last, but not least, in the wee hours of April 15th, 1912, the story of the sinking of the proud and ill-fated ship, the Titanic, brings this song to our memory yet again. As we have seen from some of these accounts, from praise to peril, from thanksgiving to tragedy, from worship to the worst disasters that man may experience, God has given us this priceless gift in the timeless possession of the old-time hymns. Questo inno è universalmente considerato uno dei più grandi inni mai scritti da una donna. Si trova in quasi ogni innoario o raccolta di inni pubblicata oggi. L'autrice di questo inno era una donna di grande ambizione e brio; una persona piena di vita, vivace, bella, dotata, e il cui "carattere nobile faceva sempre una profonda impressione su tutti coloro che la conoscevano". Sebbene avesse una vita piena e produttiva, fu breve, accelerata dalla sua costituzione delicata e fragile. La storia di questo inno ha toccato molte vite in tempi di angoscia e difficoltà, perfino di fronte alla morte. È stata usata da Dio per volgere i cuori degli uomini dalle angosce presenti verso l'alto, alle realtà immortali oltre questa vita.

Sarah Flower Adam nacque a Harlow, Inghilterra, il 22 febbraio 1805, da Benjamin ed Eliza Flower. Quando aveva cinque anni, sua madre morì di tisi, nota oggi come tubercolosi. Sarah e la sua sorella maggiore Eliza ereditarono la stessa debolezza fisica. Parlando dell'autrice dell'inno cito da 101 Hymn Stories: "Era anche ampiamente conosciuta per i suoi molti risultati letterari, sebbene la sua salute delicata fosse sempre un ostacolo per le sue molte ambizioni."

Nell'anno 1834, all'età di 29 anni, Sarah sposò un noto inventore e ingegnere civile, John Brydges. Questa distinta coppia stabilì la propria casa a Londra, Inghilterra, per tutta la durata del loro matrimonio, fino alla morte dell'autrice dell'inno quattordici anni dopo, nel 1848, alla giovane età di 43 anni.

Sarah e la sua sorella maggiore Eliza formarono una squadra eccezionale nel campo della musica—scrivendo e componendo nuove canzoni. La sorella maggiore era una musicista affermata, e la minore l'autrice degli inni. Un giorno il loro pastore, il Reverendo William Johnson Fox, chiese a queste due sorelle eccezionali se lo avrebbero aiutato nella compilazione di un nuovo innoario per la sua congregazione. Si impegnarono nel progetto e presto furono occupate ad aiutarlo a completare il libro di canti. "Insieme, contribuirono con tredici testi e sessantadue nuove melodie."

Un giorno, mentre le due sorelle si dedicavano al compito, il pastore osservò che avrebbe voluto avere un inno per concludere un sermone che stava preparando su Giacobbe ed Esaù. Eliza interruppe con entusiasmo: "Sarah, ecco un'ottima idea per un nuovo inno per il nostro innoario. Perché non scrivi tu un inno sul sogno di Giacobbe?"

"Splendido!" rispose il pastore. Più tardi quel giorno, dopo aver speso molto tempo a studiare il racconto della Genesi, assorbendone l'atmosfera e percependone il movimento drammatico, Sarah cominciò a scrivere. Presto versificò l'intera storia biblica in queste cinque strofe dell'inno immortale tuttora in uso.

Più vicino a Te, mio Dio,
Più vicino a Te!
Anche se fosse una croce
Che mi innalza;
Ancora tutto il mio canto sarebbe,
Più vicino a Te, mio Dio,
Più vicino a Te!

Come il vagabondo,
Il sole calato,
Oscurità su me,
Il mio riposo una pietra;
Eppure nei miei sogni sarei
Più vicino a Te, mio Dio,
Più vicino a Te!

Là lasci che appaia la via,
Gradini al cielo:
Tutto ciò che Tu m'invii
È donato in misericordia;
Angeli a chiamarmi
Più vicino a Te, mio Dio,
Più vicino a Te!

Allora, coi miei pensieri risvegliati
Luminosi della Tua lode,
Dalle mie ferree afflizioni
Betel innalzerò;
Così, per mezzo delle mie pene
Più vicino a Te, mio Dio,
Più vicino a Te!

O se con ali di gioia
Fendendo il cielo,
Sole, luna e stelle dimenticate,
Verso l'alto volo,
Ancora tutto il mio canto sarà,
Più vicino a Te, mio Dio,
Più vicino a Te!

Questo grande inno fu scritto nel 1840 e pubblicato l'anno successivo nell'innoario Hymns and Anthems preparato dal Reverendo Fox, il pastore dell'autrice dell'inno. La melodia originale dell'inno era una composizione di Eliza, la sorella maggiore di Sarah. Nel 1844, il Reverendo James Freeman Clarke introdusse l'inno in America, ma non divenne ben noto che dopo altri 12 anni. A quel punto l'inno fu unito alla melodia tuttora usata, "Bethany", composta appositamente per il testo da Lowell Mason, che a volte è definito il padre della musica ecclesiastica e scolastica americana. Altri inni di Mason includono "From Greenland's Icy Mountains", "When I Survey the Wondrous Cross", "A Charge to Keep I Have", "Joy to the World", "My Faith Looks Up to Thee", e "O Day of Rest and Gladness".

Molti resoconti molto interessanti sono stati registrati in relazione all'uso di questo inno e al suo effetto su coloro che lo cantavano o lo udivano cantare. Al Boston Peace Jubilee del 1872, che commemorava la fine della guerra civile, questo inno, "Nearer, My God to Thee", fu cantato da 50.000 voci. Nel 1871, tre rinomati teologi, i professori Hitchcock, Smith e Park, stavano viaggiando in Palestina, quando udirono flebili frammenti di "Bethany" giungere alle loro orecchie. Riguardo a questo episodio, cito da A Treasury of Hymn Stories, "Avvicinandosi, con loro stupore videro cinquanta studenti siriani in piedi sotto alcuni alberi in cerchio, che cantavano in arabo 'Nearer, my God to Thee'. Il professor Hitchcock, parlando in seguito dell'evento, disse che il canto di quell'inno cristiano da parte di quei giovani siriani lo commosse alle lacrime, e lo colpì più di qualsiasi canto avesse mai udito prima."

Durante l'alluvione della città di Johnstown del 31 maggio 1889 (una tragica catastrofe che uccise oltre 2.000 persone), un sfortunato treno ferroviario fu travolto dalle acque vorticosamente in movimento. Una giovane donna, preparata per essere missionaria e diretta all'estremo oriente, divenne una di quelle intrappolate in un carro ferroviario che si capovolse. Senza speranza di salvataggio, parlò con calma alla folla attonita mentre osservava impotente la tragedia in atto mentre il vagone affondava nelle acque fangose. Finì con una preghiera e cantando "Nearer, my God to Thee", in cui fu raggiunta dalla folla addolorata e solidale. Mentre cantava, morì, giungendo davvero più vicino al suo Dio che amava e desiderava servire.

Ultimo, ma non meno importante, nelle prime ore del 15 aprile 1912, la storia dell'affondamento del fiero e sventurato transatlantico, il Titanic, riporta alla nostra memoria ancora una volta questo canto. Molti superstiti che assistettero a questa grande tragedia hanno testimoniato che l'inno "Nearer, my God to Thee" fu l'ultimo canto eseguito prima che le fredde onde dell'Oceano Atlantico lo zittissero per sempre—mentre la banda suonava, il grande transatlantico affondò, precipitò nelle profondità, mandando oltre 1.500 anime nell'eternità.

In conclusione, è incredibile quanto la musica e il canto ci influenzino. Come abbiamo visto da alcuni di questi resoconti, dal lode al pericolo, dal ringraziamento alla tragedia, dal culto ai peggiori disastri che l'uomo possa sperimentare, Dio ci ha dato questo dono inestimabile nel possesso senza tempo dei vecchi inni. Possano essi non perdere mai il loro splendore nelle nostre vite o nelle vite della nostra posterità, fino a quel giorno finale in cui il tempo cesserà di esistere.

This hymn is universally thought to be one of the greatest hymns ever authored by a woman. It can be found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. This hymn writer was a woman of great ambition and enjoyment; a person full of life, vivacious, beautiful, talented, and a person who’s “exalted character always made a deep impression upon all who knew her”. Although she had a full and productive life, it was short, hastened on by her delicate and frail constitution. This hymn story has touched many lives in times of distress and hardship, including death. It has been used of God to draw the hearts of men from their present distresses, heavenward, to the immortal realities beyond this life.

Sarah Flower Adam was born at Harlow, England on February 22, 1805, to Benjamin and Eliza Flower. When she was five years old, her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis. Sarah and her older sister Eliza also inherited the same physical weakness. Speaking of the hymn writer I quote from 101 Hymn Stories: “She was also widely known for her many literary accomplishments, though her delicate health was always a handicap for her many ambitions.”

In the year 1834, at the age of 29, Sarah married a prominent inventor and civil engineer, John Brydges. This distinguished couple made their home in London, England for the duration of their marriage, until the hymn writer’s death fourteen years later in 1848, at the early age of 43.

Sarah and her older sister Eliza made an outstanding team in the realm of music—writing and composing new songs. The elder sister being an accomplished musician, and the younger the hymn writer. One day their pastor, the Rev. William Johnson Fox, asked these two exceptional sisters if they would help him with the compilation for a new hymnal for his congregation. They committed to the project, and soon were busily occupied in helping him complete the song book. “Together, they contributed thirteen texts and sixty-two new tunes.”

One day as the two sisters were pressing into the task at hand, the pastor remarked that he wished he could have a hymn written to conclude a sermon he was preparing to preach on the account of Jacob and Esau. Eliza interrupted enthusiastically, “Sarah, now there’s an excellent idea for a new hymn for our hymnal. Why don’t you write your own hymn about Jacob’s dream?”

“Splendid!” replied the pastor. Later that day, after spending much time studying the Genesis account, absorbing the atmosphere, and feeling the dramatic movement of this Old Testament narrative, Sarah began to write. Soon she had versified the complete Biblical story into these five stanzas of the immortal hymn still in use today.

Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song would be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven:
All that Thou send’st to me
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with Thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Or if on joyful wing
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upwards I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

As she sang, she passed away, coming indeed nearer to her God whom she loved and desired to serve.

这首圣诗被普遍认为是女性所作的最伟大圣诗之一。它几乎出现在当今出版的每一本圣诗集或圣歌中。这位圣诗作者是一个充满抱负与享受生活的人；充满生机、活泼、美丽、有才华，并且其“高贵的品格总是给所有认识她的人留下深刻印象”。尽管她拥有充实而富有成效的生活，但因体质羸弱而英年早逝。这个圣诗的故事在困苦与艰难、乃至面对死亡的时刻触动了许多生命。上帝曾借此把人的心从眼前的苦境引向天堂，指向这生命之外的不朽现实。

莎拉·弗劳尔·亚当（Sarah Flower Adam）于1805年2月22日出生在英格兰哈洛，父母为本杰明与伊丽莎·弗劳尔。她五岁时，母亲死于当时称为肺痨的消耗症，今称结核病。莎拉与她的姐姐伊丽莎也遗传了相同的身体虚弱。论及这位圣诗作者，我引用自《101首圣诗的故事》的一段话：“她也因众多的文学成就而广为人知，尽管她纤弱的健康总是妨碍她实现许多抱负。”

1834年，29岁时，莎拉嫁给了一位著名的发明家兼土木工程师约翰·布里奇斯（John Brydges）。这对杰出的夫妇在婚后的岁月里一直住在伦敦，直到十四年后——1848年，这位圣诗作者以43岁英年早逝。

莎拉与她的姐姐伊丽莎在音乐领域组成了一支卓越的搭档——创作与作曲新歌。姐姐是位造诣深厚的音乐家，妹妹则为圣诗作者。一天，他们的牧师威廉·约翰逊·福克斯（Rev. William Johnson Fox）请这两位杰出的姐妹协助他为会众编纂一本新的圣诗集。她们接受了这项工程，很快便忙于帮助他完成这本歌集。“她们合计贡献了十三首诗文和六十二首新曲调。”

一天，当两位姐妹专心投入手头的工作时，牧师说他希望能有一首圣诗来结束他即将讲的关于雅各与以扫的布道。伊丽莎热切地插话说：“莎拉，这对我们的圣诗集来说是个极好的新诗想法。你为何不为雅各的梦写一首自己的圣诗呢？”

“好极了！”牧师回答。那天晚些时候，莎拉花了大量时间在创作前研读创世纪的记载，吸收其氛围，并感受这段旧约叙事的戏剧性动势，随后开始写作。很快，她将完整的圣经故事作成诗行，成为今天仍在使用的这五段不朽圣诗。

更亲近我上帝，
更亲近你！
即便那是一副十字架
抬举我上去；
我整首歌仍愿是，
更亲近我上帝，
更亲近你！

虽如流浪者般，
夕阳已没，
黑暗围绕我，
我的安息如石；
然而在梦中我仍愿是，
更亲近我上帝，
更亲近你！

愿在那处路显明，
成为通往天的阶梯：
你所差给我的一切
都是恩慈赐予；
使天使向我招手，
更亲近我上帝，
更亲近你！

然后，借着我醒来的思念
以你颂赞光明，
从我坚石般的悲痛中
我要建立伯特利；
如此藉我之苦难能得以
更亲近我上帝，
更亲近你！

或若乘喜乐之翼
劈开苍穹，
忘却日月星辰，
我向上飞腾，
我一切的歌仍必是，
更亲近我上帝，
更亲近你！

这首伟大的圣诗作于1840年，并于次年刊入由牧师福克斯编纂的圣诗集《Hymns and Anthems》中。该诗原始曲调由莎拉的姐姐伊丽莎谱作。1844年，詹姆斯·弗里曼·克拉克（Rev. James Freeman Clarke）将此诗引入美国，但又过了12年才广为人知。那时，这首诗与现今所用的曲调“Bethany”相配，该曲调由洛厄尔·梅森（Lowell Mason）专为此词谱写，他有时被称为美国教会与学校音乐之父。梅森的其他圣诗包括《来自格陵兰的冰山》（"From Greenland's Icy Mountains"）、《当我默想那奇妙十架》（"When I Survey the Wondrous Cross"）、《我有当担要保守》（"A Charge to Keep I Have"）、《普天同庆》（"Joy to the World"）、《我信心仰望主》（"My Faith Looks Up to Thee"）和《安息欢欣日》（"O Day of Rest and Gladness"）。

关于这首圣诗的使用及其对听者或歌者的影响，记载了许多非常有趣的事例。1872年波士顿和平盛典（纪念内战结束）上，五万人合唱了这首《更亲近我上帝》。1871年，著名三位神学教授希区柯克（Hitchcock）、史密斯（Smith）和帕克（Park）在巴勒斯坦旅行时，听到远处传来“Bethany”的微弱旋律。关于此事，我引用自《圣诗故事珍藏》：“他们走近后，惊讶地看见五十名叙利亚学生站在树下围成一圈，用阿拉伯语唱着‘更亲近我上帝’。希区柯克教授事后谈及此事时说，那些叙利亚青年唱这首基督教圣诗令他热泪盈眶，使他比以往听过的任何歌声都更为感动。”

1889年5月31日约翰斯敦市洪水（一次造成两千余人罹难的悲惨灾祸）期间，一列不幸的火车被洪流冲入旋涡之中。一位准备赴远东当传教士的年轻女子，被困于被掀翻的车厢内，无望获救。面对惊愕的人群，她在车厢逐渐沉没于泥水中时从容地对众人说话，以祷告并唱起《更亲近我上帝》，悲痛同情的人群也加入她的歌声。她在唱时离世，确实更亲近她所爱并愿意事奉的上帝。

最后但同样重要的，在1912年4月15日凌晨，关于那艘骄傲而命运多舛的Titanic沉没的故事再次使这首歌浮现在我们记忆中。许多亲历这场大灾难的幸存者作证称，《更亲近我上帝》是沉没前乐队演奏的最后一首曲子——当乐队演奏时，大船沉入深渊，逾一千五百条生命被投入永恒之中。

总之，音乐与歌唱对我们的影响何其深远。从以上一些记述可见，从赞美到危险，从感恩到悲剧，从敬拜到人所能经历的最糟糕的灾难，上帝赐给我们这些古老圣诗作为无价的礼物。愿它们在我们生命中以及我们后代的生命中永不失去光彩，直到那时间将终结的末日。

As sisters in the Lord and born-again believers, I am sure we would all agree that memorizing scripture is important to our spiritual health. I have memorized many, many Scripture verses during my childhood years. Most of the verses that I memorized were taught during a vacation Bible School which I attended each summer.

During the first evening of Bible School, the teachers handed out memory work assignments, often many pages worth. These were not all required but the rewards were appealing. Most years I memorized everything that was assigned. I give these teachers and this Bible School the credit for the wealth of verses I memorized during those years.

Now I am married and have children of my own. The Bible School from my childhood is long past. I realized that if my children were going to memorize Scripture, I would need to make it happen. As moms, many of us know the importance of memorizing God’s Word and hiding it, not only in our hearts, but also in our children’s hearts.

Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments. Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee –Psalm 119:9-11.

We need God’s Word in our hearts to help us with our daily battles with sin. Our children need this as well. Most of our children are not going to memorize scripture without some help from us.

My husband and I did not enter marriage with dreams of memorizing with our children. For our family, it happened almost accidentally. Our oldest children were three and four when my husband suggested that we work with them on memorizing the Christmas story found in Luke 2:1-19. I didn’t think they would be able to do it. I thought young children memorized short verses like, “Be ye kind one to another.” We started reciting it together every evening during our family devotions. I was quite surprised when they memorized this passage quickly and easily.

I was intrigued. Should we try again? Easter was approaching so I started working with them on the crucifixion account found in John 19:1-19. Again, they memorized this without much effort. This encouraged me to continue with other passages.

When it came time to homeschool the children, I wanted memorization to be a part of our daily routine. I bought a binder and inserted the printed passages we had memorized as well as the passages I wanted them to memorize. This started a routine that we still do today.

Every day we recite the current passage as well as one we have previously memorized. We also recite it together as a family during our devotion time. I have found that doing it this way results in the family having the passage memorized in about three to four weeks.

At the beginning of a new passage, I read the scripture out loud. As the days go by the children start chiming in more and more. Eventually, I just get them started and only help as they need help. When I think they know the passage I have them recite it to me one by one. If they know it well, they start reciting it to their dad during our family devotions. If they don’t know it, we keep on practicing till they do know it. Sometimes I will give the struggling child just a few verses to recite. However, most of them would rather recite the whole thing.

We memorize as a family instead of individually. I don’t move on to a new passage until everyone has it memorized or at least memorized to their ability. (Not all children can memorize 19 verses at age three.) Some of our children were barely talking at three years old so verbal Bible memory was hardly possible. Some children will stumble through a passage and need lots of clue words, which is okay if they are doing their best. Sometimes we go over the same passage again in a few years and they learn it better the second time.

This may sound time-consuming and stressful, but it is not so for us. I spend about five minutes a day working on memory work. We have no time constraints on our memorization so there is no pressure to know it by a certain time. The children have been doing this since they were barely talking, so they are used to it and rarely complain. Since we memorize as a family, it also helps the child who can’t memorize as well as another. As a family, we encourage and cheer on the struggling child. He feels a sense of accomplishment even if he struggles through the whole passage.

I give a small reward for each passage memorized. I have a prize box that they can choose from. This does not need to cost much! I often do not spend much more than a dollar. Yard sales and thrift stores are places to purchase items cheaply. Back-to-school sales are nice as well since most children like to have a new pack of crayons or a cute eraser.

As time went by, I found myself becoming discouraged at how quickly the children would forget a memorized passage. I discovered that several years later they often could hardly recite a previously learned passage. I wondered why I was putting in the effort if they were simply going to forget it in a few years. My husband encouraged me to continue. He said that the concepts were still in their hearts even if they could no longer recite the passage. So I continued, but I still hoped for a solution to this problem.

One day I read an article written by another mom who also worked on memorization with her children. In the article she said that it is important to get the memory work out of the short-term memory and into the long-term memory. The solution is actually quite simple. Every day in addition to reciting our new passage, we also recite a previously learned passage. My binder comes in handy for this! All the passages we have learned are in this binder. I use a paper clip to help me remember the passage we just reviewed. Each day the paper clip moves to the next passage. When we reach the end, we start over. This helps to keep the passages fresh in our minds as well as move them to our long-term memory.

I also like to have a theme for each school year. One year my theme was, “Memorize 100 Verses.” The children enjoyed watching the number rise as the year progressed. This year we are working on, “The Sermon on the Mount.” I divided it into 10 sections. The goal is to complete it in a year, but if we don’t reach that goal it doesn’t matter. It is better to go slow and memorize something well than to go fast and not retain what you have learned.

These are the methods I have found helpful for our family. Pray and ask God for ideas that will work well for your family without comparing yourself to other families! Don’t underestimate what your children can do. Don’t assume that because they are young, they can only memorize a verse or two. Children often do only as well as we expect them to, even the younger ones.

After we have God’s Word memorized, we need to use it daily. A blanket that is kept stored away in a closet does no good on a cold, winter night. The writer of Deuteronomy sums this up well—And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up –Deuteronomy 6:5-7.

First, we love God. Then we put His Word into our hearts. Finally, we should teach these truths to our children as we go about our daily activities. This passage encompasses it all—sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up. After a passage is memorized, my husband will explain the verses to us during our devotion time. This helps us to understand what we are memorizing.

We do many things by habit because we realize their importance. We brush our teeth, comb our hair, eat breakfast, and do many other things. We do these things daily. They are a regular part of our lives. Because we value them, we make them happen. This is how it should be with scripture memorization. It is too valuable to skip.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper –Psalm 1:1-3.

When we delight in God’s Word, we will be glad to take time to memorize scripture, and the memorized Word will then bear fruit in its season.

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not –Galatians 6:9.
