Som søstre i Herren og nyfødte troende, er jeg sikker på at vi alle vil være enige om at å memorere Skriften er viktig for vår åndelige helse. Jeg memoriserte mange, mange skriftsteder i barndommen. De fleste av versene jeg lærte utenat ble undervist under et bibelskoleopphold jeg deltok på hver sommer.

Under den første kvelden på bibelskolen delte lærerne ut faste minneoppgaver, ofte mange sider. Ikke alt var obligatorisk, men belønningene var lokkende. De fleste år lærte jeg utenat alt som ble gitt. Jeg tilskriver disse lærerne og bibelskolen rikdommen av vers jeg lærte i de årene.

Nå er jeg gift og har egne barn. Bibelskolen fra min barndom er lenge forbi. Jeg innså at hvis mine barn skulle memorere Skriften, måtte jeg få det til. Som mødre vet mange av oss viktigheten av å memorere Guds Ord og skjule det, ikke bare i våre hjerter, men også i våre barns hjerter.

Hvordan skal en ung mann vasse sin vei ren? Ved å ta vare på den etter ditt ord. Med hele mitt hjerte har jeg søkt deg; la meg ikke vandre fra dine bud. Ditt ord har jeg gjemt i mitt hjerte, for å ikke synde mot deg – Salmenes 119:9-11.

Vi trenger Guds Ord i våre hjerter for å hjelpe oss i våre daglige kamper med synd. Våre barn trenger dette også. De fleste av våre barn kommer ikke til å memorere skriftsteder uten litt hjelp fra oss.

Min mann og jeg gikk ikke inn i ekteskapet med drømmer om å memorere sammen med barna våre. For vår familie skjedde det nesten ved et uhell. Våre eldste barn var tre og fire år da mannen min foreslo at vi skulle arbeide med dem på å lære juleevangeliet i Lukas 2:1-19 utenat. Jeg trodde ikke de ville klare det. Jeg tenkte at små barn lærte korte vers som «Vær gjensidig vennlige». Vi begynte å sitere det sammen hver kveld under våre familietider. Jeg ble ganske overrasket da de lærte denne teksten raskt og lett.

Jeg ble nysgjerrig. Skulle vi prøve igjen? Påsken nærmet seg, så jeg begynte å arbeide med dem på forkynnelsen om korsfestelsen i Johannes 19:1-19. Nok en gang lærte de dette uten mye anstrengelse. Dette oppmuntret meg til å fortsette med andre avsnitt.

Da tiden kom for hjemmeundervisning av barna, ønsket jeg at memorering skulle være en del av vår daglige rutine. Jeg kjøpte en ringperm og puttet inn de utskrevne avsnittene vi hadde lært samt de avsnittene jeg ønsket at de skulle lære. Dette startet en rutine vi fortsatt gjør i dag.

Hver dag siterer vi det aktuelle avsnittet samt ett vi tidligere har lært. Vi siterer det også sammen som familie under vår andaktsstund. Jeg har sett at ved å gjøre det på denne måten får familien avsnittet lærte på omtrent tre til fire uker.

Når vi begynner på et nytt avsnitt, leser jeg skriftstedet høyt. Etter hvert som dagene går, begynner barna å hive seg på mer og mer. Til slutt starter jeg dem bare og hjelper bare når de trenger hjelp. Når jeg synes de kan avsnittet, får de sitere det for meg én og én. Hvis de kan det godt, begynner de å sitere det for faren sin under vår familieandakt. Hvis de ikke kan det, fortsetter vi å øve til de kan det. Noen ganger gir jeg det barnet som strever bare noen få vers å sitere. Men de fleste foretrekker å sitere hele avsnittet.

Vi memoriserer som en familie i stedet for individuelt. Jeg går ikke videre til et nytt avsnitt før alle har det memorisert eller i det minste memorisert etter sin evne. (Ikke alle barn kan memorere 19 vers i en alder av tre.) Noen av våre barn snakket så vidt ved tre år, så muntlig bibelminne var knapt mulig. Noen barn snubler gjennom et avsnitt og trenger mange ledetrådsord, noe som er greit hvis de gjør sitt beste. Noen ganger går vi over samme avsnitt igjen etter noen år, og da lærer de det bedre andre gangen.

Dette kan høres tidkrevende og stressende ut, men det er det ikke for oss. Jeg bruker omtrent fem minutter om dagen på minnearbeid. Vi har ingen tidsbegrensninger for vår memorering, så det er ikke noe press om å kunne det innen en bestemt tid. Barna har gjort dette siden de så vidt kunne snakke, så de er vant til det og klager sjelden. Siden vi memoriserer som familie, hjelper det også det barnet som ikke kan memorere like godt som et annet. Som familie oppmuntrer og heier vi på det barnet som strever. Han føler en følelse av mestring selv om han sliter seg gjennom hele avsnittet.

Jeg gir en liten belønning for hvert avsnitt som blir lært utenat. Jeg har en premieeske som de kan velge fra. Dette trenger ikke koste mye! Jeg bruker ofte ikke mer enn en dollar. Garasjesalg og bruktbutikker er steder å kjøpe ting billig. Tilbake-til-skolen-salg er også fint ettersom de fleste barn liker å få en ny pakke fargeblyanter eller et søtt viskelær.

Etter hvert ble jeg motløs over hvor raskt barna glemte et innlært avsnitt. Jeg oppdaget at flere år senere kunne de ofte knapt sitere et tidligere lært avsnitt. Jeg lurte på hvorfor jeg la inn innsatsen hvis de likevel kom til å glemme det etter noen år. Min mann oppmuntret meg til å fortsette. Han sa at konseptene likevel lå i deres hjerter selv om de ikke lenger kunne sitere avsnittet. Så jeg fortsatte, men jeg håpet fortsatt på en løsning på dette problemet.

En dag leste jeg en artikkel skrevet av en annen mor som også arbeidet med memorering med sine barn. I artikkelen sa hun at det er viktig å få minnearbeidet ut av korttidshukommelsen og inn i langtidsminnet. Løsningen er egentlig ganske enkel. Hver dag, i tillegg til å sitere vårt nye avsnitt, siterer vi også et tidligere lært avsnitt. Min ringperm kommer godt med til dette! Alle avsnittene vi har lært er i denne permen. Jeg bruker en binders for å huske hvilket avsnitt vi nettopp gjennomgikk. Hver dag flytter bindersen seg til neste avsnitt. Når vi når slutten, begynner vi på nytt. Dette hjelper til med å holde avsnittene friske i minnene våre og flytte dem over i langtidsminnet.

Jeg liker også å ha et tema for hvert skoleår. Ett år var temaet mitt «Memorisere 100 vers.» Barna likte å se tallet øke etter hvert som året gikk. I år arbeider vi med «Bergprekenen.» Jeg delte den inn i 10 seksjoner. Målet er å fullføre den på ett år, men hvis vi ikke når det målet spiller det ingen rolle. Det er bedre å gå sakte og memorere noe godt enn å gå fort og ikke huske det man har lært.

Dette er metodene jeg har funnet nyttige for vår familie. Be og spør Gud om ideer som vil fungere godt for din familie uten å sammenligne deg med andre familier! Undervurder ikke hva barna dine kan gjøre. Anta ikke at bare fordi de er små, kan de bare memorere et vers eller to. Barn gjør ofte ikke mer enn vi forventer av dem, selv de yngre.

Etter at vi har Guds Ord memorisert, trenger vi å bruke det daglig. Et teppe som ligger lagret i et skap gjør ingen nytte på en kald vinternatt. Forfatteren av Femte Mosebok oppsummerer dette godt—Og du skal elske HERREN din Gud av hele ditt hjerte og av hele din sjel og av all din kraft. Og disse ord, som jeg i dag påbyr deg, skal være i ditt hjerte; og du skal lære dem grundig til dine barn, og du skal tale om dem når du sitter i ditt hus, når du går på veien, når du legger deg ned og når du står opp – Femte Mosebok 6:5-7.

Først elsker vi Gud. Så legger vi Hans Ord i våre hjerter. Til slutt bør vi lære disse sannhetene til våre barn mens vi går om våre daglige gjøremål. Dette avsnittet omfatter alt—sitting, gåing, legge seg og stå opp. Etter at et avsnitt er lært, forklarer ofte min mann versene for oss i løpet av vår andaktstid. Dette hjelper oss å forstå hva vi memoriserer.

Vi gjør mange ting av vane fordi vi innser deres betydning. Vi pusser tennene, grer håret, spiser frokost og gjør mange andre ting. Vi gjør disse tingene daglig. De er en vanlig del av våre liv. Fordi vi verdsetter dem, får vi dem til å skje. Slik bør det være med skriftmemorering også. Det er for verdifullt til å hoppe over.

Salig er den mann som ikke vandrer i de ugudeliges råd, og ikke står i syndernes vei, og ikke sitter i spotternes sete. Men hans lyst er i Herrens lov, og i hans lov grunner han dag og natt. Og han skal være som et tre plantet ved rennende vann, som bærer sin frukt til sin tid; og hans løv visner ikke; og alt han gjør, lykkes – Salmenes 1:1-3.

Når vi fryder oss over Guds Ord, vil vi gjerne ta oss tid til å memorere skriften, og det memoriserte ord vil da bære frukt til sin tid.

La oss heller ikke bli trette av å gjøre godt; for i rett tid skal vi høste, hvis vi ikke gir opp – Galaterne 6:9.

Greatly desiring to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that I may be filled with joy; When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also. Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:4-7.

“Oh God, give us mothers like Eunice and grandmothers like Lois. Give us women who are women of faith. Give us women who know how to stand for truth against the tide of human rationalization that is destroying the lives of so many well-meaning people. Give us women who are unwavering in their loyalty to Jesus Christ, to their husbands, and to their calling to represent the spirit of Jesus in all of life. Amen”.

History has proven that women are as influential as men in forming the fabric of society and of the Christian community. An argument could be made that they exert an even greater influence if you consider the fact that they have a huge role in shaping the values of little children and, whether or not they dress and conduct themselves according to godly modesty, they can influence the morality of the masses of men around them.

Hence the call for women to be women of faith. Not only does a woman’s faith influence those around her, but every woman has her own personal journey. Her journey is a search for identity, security, and purpose for her life.

Today’s women are inundated with voices that claim to offer the fulfillment that their heart desires. As with their mother Eve, many of these voices appeal to her feminine spirit, but as their mother Eve discovered, unless it is the voice of God, it leads to death and destruction.

The Bible abounds with accounts of women who lived by faith. Consider the harlot Rahab. Bible scholars cannot agree that she was worthy of that title, but it has come down to us as such. She heard the stories of the God of Israel. When she encountered the spies and heard their ominous prediction for her city she chose to believe.

She was a native of Jericho. Jericho was her home. Jericho had high stone walls and brave defenders. She would have had many reasons to place her faith in that which was familiar to her, and which had sustained her in the past.

She chose to place her faith in the God of Israel. The men of Israel told her that if she would hang a scarlet thread from her window on the wall, her house and her life would be spared. A scarlet thread. Not much by way of identity or security, but Rahab hung her faith on a scarlet thread. That scarlet thread represented the power of the God of Israel and, as we know today, it is a beautiful type of the blood of Jesus.

The call to be a woman of faith is a call to turn away from the ideology of the world and to embrace what in the eyes of the world is a futile remedy—a scarlet thread. Rahab’s faith was rooted in her knowledge of the God of Israel and His plan to judge her people. The scarlet thread was her hope of deliverance.

I would like for us to consider how faith in God impacts the primary desires of the feminine heart. Every woman longs for identity, security, and purpose. Jesus has come to meet that heart longing.

Identity –“Who am I?”

This is a question that everyone is compelled to ask at some point in their life—often in adolescence. Young men tend to carve out their identity based in whom they admire and their vocational inclinations. Young women, especially in our Anabaptist communities, are largely at the mercy of the prominent men in their lives to define their identity.

This is not purely cultural. When God said to Eve, …thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee –Genesis 3:16, He was declaring that she and her female descendants would look to the man to define an essential part of their nature.

Fathers play a key role in the early development of a little girl’s identity. Abusive fathers, absent fathers, and indifferent fathers leave in their wake little girls who are uncertain of who they are, or of their value as a person. A father who affirms his daughter’s godly femininity gives her a priceless gift. By that, I mean praising her for qualities of feminine virtue, blessing her for efforts to be chaste and modest, and yes, telling her that she is beautiful.

A woman’s heart will ultimately turn toward a husband. God said, “Thy desire shall be to thy husband”, not to thy father. Most women marry thinking that they have at last found their “savior” and rightly so. Did Paul not say in Ephesians chapter five that the husband is “the savior of the body”? Should a wife not expect to receive from her husband love, affirmation, protection, and provision? This is due to her by divine decree. A godly husband will do everything in his power to provide for her in this way.

“Thy desire shall be to thy husband” is given in the context of the fall. It was one of the consequences of the fall. It is a statement without the promise of fulfillment. This leaves us to believe that, although driven by desire, that desire may go unfulfilled.

What is a woman to do if her husband is unwilling or unable to satisfy her heart’s desire? What if a woman does not have a husband? She must become a woman of faith. Until a woman has found her identity in Jesus, no man will be able to satisfy the deepest longings of her heart.

Many marriages suffer because the wife expects her husband to meet the deep longings of her heart that only Jesus can fulfill. Many men are made to feel inadequate and withdraw when they are expected to be, and to do, for their wives what only Jesus can do.

Calling all women to be women of faith

Women of faith are women who know who they are in Christ Jesus. They have found the deepest longings of their feminine heart met in Him. Because their heart longings are satisfied, they have become a well spring of life to their husband, to their children, and to others.

Security –“Who will protect me?”

Being a woman has always been risky. Women are very vulnerable. In addition to the fact that they are physically more delicate, women are more susceptible to emotional vacillations, and I believe that based on what the Bible has to say about Eve’s deception, that women tend to be more vulnerable to spiritual deception (see 1 Timothy 2:14).

This does not make them inferior to men. Their emotional sensitivity makes them more attune to the many realities of relational problems than many men are. In this, their insight can be a positive thing, helping to balance us men in some of our natural weaknesses. Whatever comparisons we choose to make, I think we can all agree that women need the protection that men offer.

What if the man that is supposed to be protecting you is a coward? We have an example of just such a situation in the Bible. The man’s name is Abraham—yes… the father of faith. Even strong men sometimes make cowardly decisions.

Abraham and Sarah were traveling into Egypt. As they neared Egypt, Abraham became afraid for his life. His wife Sarah was a beautiful woman and Abraham was aware that Egypt was a heathen nation with very loose morals. He was afraid that the Egyptians would kill him so they could have his wife. Abraham said to Sarah, Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee –Genesis 12:13.

Sarah was indeed Abraham’s half-sister. They had the same father, but not the same mother. Abraham’s contingency plan leaves Sarah in a very difficult position. We read nothing of Sarah’s reaction to Abraham’s plan. All we know is that …Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement –1 Peter 3:6.

It would appear that Sarah was not afraid. Her faith was not dependent on Abraham’s protection. She was relying on a higher power. Sarah’s faith gave her a place in the hall of faith in Hebrews chapter 11 and made her Peter’s example of how wives are to relate to their husbands.

The substance of this story is in the outcome. Because of Sarah’s faith, she was delivered from the hand of Pharaoh, the most powerful world ruler of the day. It was Sarah’s faith, not Abraham’s, which protected her.

Women look to men for security, and it is right that they should. Men protect their women as best they can. I believe that when men and women are living within their God-given roles, there is a lot of protection and security available; however, we do live in a fallen world. We do not always honorably fulfill our roles and sometimes God allows evil to befall even the most pious.

Calling all women to be women of faith even as Sarah

Do you have faith to believe that God is bigger than your husband or your father? Are you willing to trust God to overrule where your husband may be weak or even rebellious against God or the church?

A woman of faith is a woman who chooses to trust God in the absence of a reasonable path forward. A woman of faith continues to do what is right, even though it may not be a path of guaranteed security because …The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me –Hebrews 13:6.

Purpose – “Why am I here?”

This is a question that everyone asks at some point in life. We want our lives to have meaning and purpose. The futility of a meaningless living drives men and women into depression and despair. Living purposefully blesses us and others and brings honor to our Creator.

When men think of living purposefully, they envision… a battle to fight, a mountain to conquer, a noble goal to strive for. We men tend to be vision-oriented and goal-focused.

What does it mean for a woman to live purposefully?

Luke gives us some insight into this in the account of Jesus’ visit to the home of Mary and Martha. (See Luke 10:38-42) Jesus would frequently stop by this home when He was passing through Bethany. Here He knew He would find great hospitality and engaging conversation. Today was no exception.

As He relaxed in their sitting room, Mary sat at His feet asking questions and listening intently as He revealed to her the purpose of His life and His future destiny. Mary came to understand things about Jesus that even His disciples had failed to grasp.

Matthew records that when Jesus was dining in the house of Simon a woman, thought to be Mary of Bethany, entered, and knelt and anointed Jesus’ feet with expensive ointment. When the disciples complained about “this waste” Jesus said to them: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial –Matthew 26:12.

Where did Mary get this understanding? Was it not when she was “sitting at Jesus feet?”

Martha on the other hand was “cumbered about much serving”. Now Jesus had to eat. Someone needed to prepare food and I am certain that Jesus enjoyed Martha’s delicious provisions. But Jesus chided her with “Martha, Martha”. Notice the familial tone of his voice.

He was not judging her nor condemning her. He was challenging her to take time for the important things in life. He commended Mary for she …hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her –Luke 10:42.

I would like to suggest that most of our anxiety is of our own making. We set goals for our life that Jesus never required. We place expectations upon ourselves that have no eternal merit. Like Martha, we stress over frivolity, and damage relationships over trivial matters. Yes, supper must be served, and Mary should help, but not to neglect the “better part”.

Calling all women to be women of faith as Mary who loved to linger at Jesus feet

Life for a wife and mother is full of pressing demands. Defuse your life of stress and anxiety by spending time listening for the voice of Jesus—that “still small voice” that Elijah finally heard.

Stress and anxiety will melt away in the presence of Jesus. God speaks to us by His Holy Spirit through His Word. If it is a challenge for you to find time to sit down with your Bible, then you can quiet your spirit with your hands in the dishwater, or while folding the laundry, or as you once again prepare a meal for your family. At times like this you can commune with God. You can pray to your Father in heaven. You can say things like “I love you Lord Jesus, speak to me through Your Word, bring peace to my soul; quiet the wrestlings of my mind; help me to enter into Your rest; give me Your peace.” Then you can listen as His Spirit prompts your spirit with nuggets of truth from the Scriptures that are hidden away in your heart.

Summary –Calling all women to be women of faith

For your own personal wellbeing:

Women today are bombarded by self-help resources in the form of books, podcasts, social media, and seminars. Much of it is good and can be helpful, but nothing will replace a personal relationship and a daily walk with Jesus.

For the wellbeing of your children:

Today, more than ever we need mothers to be women of faith who can project onto their children that walking with God is real and satisfying. Young Timothy was influenced by the unfeigned faith of his mother and of his grandmother. Never underestimate the effect of the influence of your life on the lives of those who follow you.

For the strength of your husband:

Men today need the support of faithful women, especially their wife. A man’s daily walk can be fortified or diminished by the woman in his life. It has been said “Behind every successful man is woman”. A man is tremendously influenced for good or ill by the women in his life.

For the good of the Church:

Woman of faith, the church needs you. Women bring a grace to the church that is desperately needed. Your prayers are needed. Your testimony gives encouragement. Your song moves our hearts. Your smile gives hope. Your peaceful, joyful countenance of a soul that’s at rest in Jesus is an influence that is rivaled by little else in this world.

大大渴望见你，记念你的眼泪，好叫我充满喜乐；又忆起你心里那没有假冒、先在你外祖母罗伊、你母亲以尼基心里的信，且我深信也在你心里。为此我劝你把神所赐你们的恩赐再点燃，那恩赐是藉着我按手给你的。神赐给我们不是胆怯的心，乃是刚强、仁爱、谨守的心──提摩太后书 1:4-7。

“哦 神啊，赐给我们像以尼基那样的母亲，像罗伊那样的外祖母。赐给我们有信心的妇人。赐给我们能在摧毁许多善意之人生命的人类理性化潮流中，为真理坚守立场的妇人。赐给我们在对耶稣基督、对她们的丈夫并对在一切生活中代表耶稣灵的呼召上坚定不移的妇人。阿们”。

历史已证明，妇女在塑造社会结构和基督教团体方面与男子一样有影响力。可以说，如果考虑到她们在塑造幼小孩子价值观方面扮演的重要角色，无论她们是否按照敬虔的端庄来着装和举止，她们能影响周围大批男子的道德，那么她们的影响力甚至更大。

所以，要呼召妇女成为有信心的妇人。妇人的信心不仅影响她周围的人，每个妇女也有她自己的个人旅程。她的旅程是在为她的生命寻求身份、安全和目标。

当今的妇女被号称能带来心灵满足的各种声音淹没。正如她们的母亲夏娃一样，许多这样的声音迎合她们的女性心灵，但正如夏娃所发现的，除非那是来自神的声音，否则它带来的是死与毁灭。

圣经充满了按信心而活的妇女事例。想想妓女喇合。圣经学者对她是否配得那称号未能达成一致，但这称呼传承至今。她听见以色列神的故事。当她遇见探子并听到他们对她城邑的可怕断言时，她选择了信。

她是耶利哥人。耶利哥是她的家。耶利哥有高大的石墙和勇敢的保卫者。她本有许多理由把信心放在她熟悉并过去曾供养她的事物上。

她选择把信心放在以色列的神上。以色列人告诉她，如果她把一条朱红线挂在城墙上的窗户上，她的家和她的性命就必被保全。一条朱红线。作为身份或安全并不多，但喇合把她的信心挂在那条朱红线上。那朱红线代表以色列神的能力，正如我们今天所知道的，它是耶稣血的美好型象。

成为有信心的妇女的呼召，是转离世界意识形态，接受在世人眼中看似徒然的药方──一条朱红线。喇合的信心根植于她对以色列神及祂审判她列民计划的认知。那朱红线是她得救的盼望。

我愿我们来思考信靠神如何影响女性心灵的首要渴望。每个妇人都渴望身份、安全与目的。耶稣已来满足那心灵的渴慕。

身份——“我是谁？”

这是每个人在生命某个阶段都会被迫要问的问题──常在青春期。年轻男子倾向于以他们钦佩的人与职业倾向来刻画自己的身份。年轻女子，尤其在我们的阿拿巴普蒂斯特群体中，往往在很大程度上任由她们生命中显要的男性来定义她们的身份。

这并非纯粹文化现象。当神对夏娃说，…你必恋慕你丈夫，他要管你──创世记 3:16，祂是在宣告她和她的女性后裔会看向男人来定义她们本性的一个要素。

父亲在小女孩早期身份发展中扮演关键角色。虐待的父亲、缺席的父亲与冷漠的父亲会留下不确定自己是谁或作为人的价值如何的小女孩。一个肯定女儿敬虔女性气质的父亲赐给她无价的礼物。我的意思是称赞她的女性美德品质，为她对贞洁与端庄的努力祝福，并且，是的，告诉她她是美丽的。

妇女的心最终会转向丈夫。神说：“你的情欲必归向你的丈夫”，不是归向你的父亲。多数妇女结婚时会认为她们终于找到了她们的“救主”，这想法是有道理的。保罗在以弗所书第五章不也说丈夫是“身体的救主”吗？妻子不应期待从丈夫那里得到爱、肯定、保护与供养吗？这是神圣法令应当赐予她的。一位敬虔的丈夫会尽其所能这样供给她。

“你的情欲必归向你的丈夫”是置于堕落的语境中。它是堕落的后果之一。这是一个没有应许必然成就的陈述。这使我们相信，虽然受欲望驱使，但该欲望可能不得满足。

如果丈夫不愿或不能满足她心灵的渴望，妇人该如何是好？如果一个妇人没有丈夫呢？她必须成为有信心的妇人。除非妇人在耶稣里找着自己的身份，否则没有任何男人能满足她心中最深的渴望。

许多婚姻受苦，是因为妻子期待丈夫去满足只有耶稣能完成的深切渴望。许多男人在被期望为妻子做只有耶稣能做的事时，感到不足而退缩。

呼召众妇成为有信心的妇人

有信心的妇人是那些在基督耶稣里知道自己是谁的妇人。她们已在祂里面找到女性心灵最深的渴望。因为她们的心愿已被满足，她们成了丈夫、子女和他人的生命泉源。

安全——“谁会保护我？”

做为妇女历来充满风险。妇女非常脆弱。除了在体格上更纤弱之外，妇女更易于情绪波动，我也相信根据圣经关于夏娃受骗的记载，妇女倾向于更容易受属灵欺骗的影响（见提摩太前书 2:14）。

这并不使她们比男人差。她们的情绪敏感使她们比许多男人更能察觉人际问题的诸多现实。在这方面，她们的洞见能成为积极的事，帮助平衡我们男人在一些天生软弱上的不足。无论我们选择做何种比较，我想我们都可以同意妇女需要男人所提供的保护。

如果本应保护你的那个人是懦夫怎么办？圣经中就有这样的例子。那人的名字叫亚伯拉罕──是的……信心之父。即使是刚强的人有时也做出懦弱的决定。

亚伯拉罕和撒拉正前往埃及。临近埃及时，亚伯拉罕为自己的性命惧怕。他的妻子撒拉是个美貌的妇人，亚伯拉罕知道埃及是一个道德松散的外邦国度。他怕埃及人要杀他，好夺他的妻子。亚伯拉罕对撒拉说，你既为我有益，我必因此得存性命──创世记 12:13。

撒拉确实是亚伯拉罕的同父异母妹。他们有同一父亲，却不是同一母亲。亚伯拉罕的应急计划把撒拉置于一个非常困难的境地。我们未读到撒拉对亚伯拉罕计划的反应。我们所知道的只是，……撒拉顺服亚伯拉罕，称他为主人：你们若行善、不叫人惧怕什么惊吓的事，就是这样你们的女儿──彼得前书 3:6。

看起来撒拉并不惧怕。她的信心不依靠亚伯拉罕的保护。她信靠更高的权能。撒拉的信心使她在希伯来书第十一章的信心名人堂中有一席之地，并成为彼得论妻子如何对待丈夫的榜样。

这个故事的实质在其结果。因着撒拉的信心，她从法老──当时最有权势的世俗统治者──手中得释放。保护她的乃是撒拉的信心，不是亚伯拉罕的。

妇女向男人寻求安全，本该如此。男人尽其所能保护他们的妇人。我相信当男人与女人在神所赐的角色中生活时，有许多保护与安全可得；然而我们确实生活在一个堕落的世界。我们并非总是光荣地履行职责，有时神允许恶事临到即便是最虔诚的人身上。

呼召众妇如同撒拉般成为有信心的妇人

你有信心相信神比你的丈夫或父亲更大吗？你是否愿意信靠神在你丈夫软弱或甚至悖逆神或教会的地方掌权并超越他们的作为？

有信心的妇人是在缺乏合理出路时仍选择信靠神的妇人。有信心的妇人仍继续行义，尽管这可能不是一条有保证安全的道路，因为……主是我的帮助，我必不惧怕人，谁能把我怎么样呢？──希伯来书 13:6。

目的——“我为何在此？”

这是每个人在生命某个阶段会问的问题。我们希望生命具有意义与目的。毫无意义的生活的虚无驱使男女走向抑郁与绝望。有目的地生活祝福我们和他人，并荣耀我们的造物主。

当男人思考有目的的生活时，他们设想的是……一场要打的仗、一座要征服的山、一项要为之奋斗的崇高目标。我们男人倾向于以远景为导向并专注于目标。

对妇女而言，有目的地生活意味着什么？

路加在记载耶稣造访马大与马利亚家时给了我们一些见解。（见路加福音 10:38-42）耶稣经过伯大尼时常常到他们家里去。在那里祂知道会找到丰盛的款待和引人入胜的对话。今日也不例外。

当祂在客厅里安歇时，马利亚坐在祂脚前，问问题并专心听祂向她启示祂生命的目的和未来的命运。马利亚明白了关于耶稣的一些事，是连祂的门徒都未能领会的。

马太记载，当耶稣在西门家里吃饭时，有一个被认为是伯大尼的马利亚的妇人进来，跪下，把贵重的香膏倒在耶稣的脚上。当门徒因“这浪费”而抱怨时，耶稣对他们说：她把这香膏浇在我的身上，是为我安葬预备的──马太福音 26:12。

马利亚从哪里得着这样的领悟？难道不是当她“坐在耶稣脚前”时吗？

另一方面，马大却“为许多服侍而烦扰”。当时耶稣得吃饭。需要有人预备食物，我确信耶稣享受马大丰盛的供备。但耶稣称她“马大，马大”。注意祂语气中的亲切感。

祂并非在论断她或定她罪。祂是在挑战她为生命中的要事预留时间。祂称赞马利亚，因为她……拣选那上好的福分，是不能夺去的──路加福音 10:42。

我想说大多数焦虑是我们自找的。我们为生活设下耶稣从未要求的目标。我们给自己施加那些没有永恒功效的期望。像马大，我们为琐事烦恼，并为微不足道的事损害人际关系。是的，晚餐必须预备，马利亚应当帮助，但不要忽略那“更好的福分”。

呼召众妇如同喜爱坐在耶稣脚前的马利亚，成为有信心的妇人

妻子与母亲的生活充满紧迫的需求。通过花时间倾听耶稣的声音──那以利亚最终听见的“微小而柔和的声音”，解除你生活中的压力与焦虑。

在耶稣面前，压力与焦虑会消融。神借着祂的圣灵并通过祂的话语与我们说话。如果你难以找到坐下读经的时间，你可以在洗碗时、折衣服时或再次为家人准备饭菜时安静心灵。在这样的时刻你可以与神相交。你可以向天上的父祷告。你可以说像“主耶稣，我爱你，借着你的话向我说话，赐平安给我的心；安静我思虑的争战；帮助我进入你的安息；赐我你的平安。”然后你就可以侧耳聆听，随着祂的灵用藏在你心中的圣经真理的颗粒来提示你的灵。

总结——呼召众妇成为有信心的妇人

为你个人的福祉：

今天的妇女被自助资源轰炸，形式有书籍、播客、社交媒体与研讨会。其许多内容是好的并能有所帮助，但没有什么能取代与耶稣的个人关系和日常同行。

为你孩子的福祉：

如今，我们比以往更需要母亲成为能够向孩子传递与神同行是真实且令人满足的信心妇人。年少的提摩太受他母亲和外祖母那没有假冒的信心所影响。永远不要低估你生命对跟随你之人的影响力。

为你丈夫的力量：

如今的男人需要忠信妇人的支持，尤其是他们的妻子。一个男人的日常行走可以被他生命中的妇人坚固或削弱。常有人说：“每个成功男人背后都有一位女性”。男人在很大程度上受生命中妇人的良善或有害影响。

为教会的益处：

有信心的妇人，教会需要你。妇女给教会带来一种急需的恩典。你的祷告是所需的。你的见证带来鼓励。你的歌声感动我们的心。你的微笑带来盼望。你那在耶稣里安息的灵魂所显示的平安、喜乐的面貌，是这世上少有能与之媲美的影响力。

For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy … For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife? –1 Corinthians 7:14-16.

As we gaze across the thoroughfare of homes surrounding us, we grieve as we behold one Christian tragedy after another. Almost every Christian has some near kin who has experienced divorce, a rebellious child, or strained marital relationships. Perhaps we cry out to God as we wonder why it is so, for it is surely not His plan. Herein we behold the apostle Paul bringing out an amazing principle that is little understood and even less employed—a sanctified home. It is what every sincere believer wants and seeks, but few apprehend. Christianity is not a rubber stamp that automatically clones offspring after the same sort. Still the scripture must be true and there must indeed be a sanctifying effect that a true believer brings into a home. This is no guarantee that the unbelieving spouse or the children of the union will be saved, but when a believing husband or wife acts in accordance with the scripture and the Spirit of God, the effect they have on the home will allow God’s power to be evident and an avenue of grace is poured into the pathway of all who dwell therein.

Our impotency is not caused due to the lack of God’s power, but because our dim understanding is infested and infiltrated with the influences of this present world. Faith in God alone is inevitably a powerful force, while faith injected by human reasoning and impatience will hardly prove any more effective than Abraham and Hagar’s attempts to produce a holy and sanctified child.

What then sanctifies the home? Casual observation will notice that merely being a believer isn’t enough to accomplish it. To sanctify is to make pure and holy. It is a process of filtering and a separation from that which is impure to bring greater purity to the object being sanctified. The Pharisees understood the principle well. They spent many a rigorous hour paying heed to countless miniscule details to make their vessels holy. Still, they were critically unsuccessful.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:25-26.

The Inside Sanctified by Faith and Prayer

What a foolish thing it would be for a man to wash only the outside of a cup, which is to be looked at, and to leave the inside dirty, which is to be used. Yet there are those who avoid only the scandalous sins—those that would spoil their reputation with men—but would still allow themselves pride and moral decay in their heart. It is this which renders them odious to the pure and holy God. Such it is when a man or woman seeks to purify their home by superficial cleansing. Pharisaic attempts to root out and remove the surface details and inconsistencies from the lives of their helpmate and children, in order to sanctify them, are generally fruitless.

However quick-sighted they are in other things; Christ calls them blind. In Christ’s estimation, those who are not acquainted with the wickedness of their own hearts—those who see not, and hate not, the secret sin that is lodged within—are strangers to sanctification. Self-ignorance is the most shameful and hurtful ignorance. The rule is, “Cleanse first that which is within, to get cleansed from the filthiness of the spirit.” Corrupt affections and inclinations, the secret lusts that lurk in the soul, unseen and unobserved, these must first be recognized, mortified, and subdued. If due care is taken concerning that, the outside will, by extension, become clean also. External motives and inducements may keep the outside clean, while the inside remains filthy; but if renewed sanctifying grace makes the inside clean, that will have a lasting and profound influence upon the outside, for the commanding principle is within. If the heart is well kept, all is well, …for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-7.

Here Peter speaks of a wife winning her husband with the due benevolence mentioned in Corinthians. While she has no unconditional guarantee of sanctifying her husband, she certainly will meet with little success without it. Eunice was a Jewess, who, upon embracing faith in Christ, found herself in an unequal yoke with a Greek. We read that unfeigned faith was first wrought in her mother Lois, and that affected Eunice. This, in turn, had a sanctifying effect on young Timothy, who was then prepared for the work of the Lord. We have no record that his father was added to the faith, but one can only imagine the initial turmoil within the breast of this young Jewess as she reverently honored her head and circumcised not her son but rather committed him to prayer. Here brings us to the other vital dimension of home sanctification. While she was not emboldened to teach her husband, she apparently had won his respect enough to allow her to teach her son in the home. This she diligently did… For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness –2 Timothy 3:15-16.

The Outside Sanctified by the Word

When the heart of the believer is dealt with first, the visible dimensions of the home fall into place in succession. Worldly influences have little appeal for the budding child of God. The Word of God must take its full place being administered to the children as well as the adults, for they are profitable for sanctification. A husband is to wash his wife and children (as well as himself) by administering the Word of God so that he may sanctify and cleanse his home.

Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

When the Word of God is given full authority in the home, it becomes the governing principle around which the home operates. It must be allowed to filter out the media of the masses and the influences of all evil communications, which will corrupt good manners.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful –Psalm 1:1.

Individuals within the home may not always appreciate the direction received from it, but submit to it they must, and usually do so heartily. Most of us have received direction from our parents that we did not appreciate at the time but years later have come to grasp the blessedness of their leadership. Leadership that does not lead, is not expressing love, and will leave the home unsanctified and its members disconnected. Though it is rather uncomfortable and inconvenient to ask children to do without what others are partaking in, they are not sanctified by following their peers, but rather by the truth. For us as parents, there is no greater joy than to know that our children walk in truth. Equally so, there is no greater joy for them than to walk in it. Daily family devotions are a cohesive force within the home that is central and integral to home sanctification. We dare not apologize for the authority we give to the Word, nor slack from its use. It is an erroneous Gospel to believe that souls are stifled who are held to the mandates within it.

Here is Christ’s summation of His home.

I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth –John 17:6-17.

Christ, as the head of His home, employed no complicated means to the sanctification of His children. His life manifested a constant keeping Himself in the love of God through faith and prayer, and the administration of God’s Word to those about Him. At times they stumbled at it, wrestled inwardly, and misunderstood Him, but the keeping force rested not on the laurels of convincing words, adamant force, fun activities, nor prudent reasoning.

While a home must employ these resources from time to time, they of themselves do not carry the sanctifying power. For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

Perché il marito non credente è santificato dalla moglie, e la moglie non credente è santificata dal marito: altrimenti i vostri figli sarebbero impuri; ma ora sono santi … Perché ciò che tu sai, o moglie, se salverai tuo marito? o come sai, o uomo, se salverai tua moglie? –1 Corinzi 7:14-16.

Mentre contempliamo la strada di case che ci circonda, ci addolora vedere una tragedia cristiana dopo l’altra. Quasi ogni cristiano ha qualche parente vicino che ha sperimentato il divorzio, un figlio ribelle o rapporti coniugali tesi. Forse gridiamo a Dio chiedendoci perché sia così, poiché sicuramente non è il Suo piano. Qui vediamo l’apostolo Paolo evidenziare un principio sorprendente che è poco compreso e ancora meno applicato: una casa santificata. È ciò che ogni credente sincero desidera e cerca, ma pochi afferrano. Il cristianesimo non è un timbro che clona automaticamente i figli secondo lo stesso modello. Tuttavia la Scrittura deve essere vera e deve esserci davvero un effetto santificante che un vero credente apporta in una casa. Questo non è una garanzia che il coniuge non credente o i figli dell’unione saranno salvati, ma quando un marito o una moglie credente agisce in conformità con la Scrittura e lo Spirito di Dio, l’effetto che hanno sulla famiglia permetterà che la potenza di Dio sia evidente e un canale di grazia venga versato nel cammino di tutti coloro che vi dimorano.

La nostra impotenza non è causata dalla mancanza del potere di Dio, ma perché la nostra scarsa comprensione è infestata e infiltrata dalle influenze di questo mondo presente. La fede in Dio soltanto è inevitabilmente una forza potente, mentre una fede iniettata da ragionamenti umani e impazienza difficilmente si dimostrerà più efficace dei tentativi di Abramo e Agar di produrre un figlio santo e santificato.

Che cosa dunque santifica la casa? L’osservazione casuale noterà che essere semplicemente un credente non è sufficiente per realizzarlo. Santificare significa rendere puro e santo. È un processo di filtrazione e una separazione da ciò che è impuro per portare maggiore purezza all’oggetto che viene santificato. I farisei comprendevano bene il principio. Passavano molte ore rigorose a prestare attenzione a innumerevoli dettagli minimi per rendere i loro vasi santi. Eppure fallivano in modo critico.

Guai a voi, scribi e farisei, ipocriti! perché pulite il fuori del calice e del piatto, ma dentro sono pieni di rapina e intemperanza. Tu fariseo cieco, pulisci prima ciò che è dentro il calice e il piatto, affinché anche il fuori di essi sia pulito –Matteo 23:25-26.

L'interno santificato dalla fede e dalla preghiera

Quanto sarebbe sciocco per un uomo lavare solo l’esterno di un calice, che è quello che si guarda, e lasciare l’interno sporco, che invece si usa. Eppure ci sono coloro che evitano solo i peccati scandalosi—quelli che rovinerebbero la loro reputazione agli occhi degli uomini—ma si permettono comunque orgoglio e decadenza morale nel loro cuore. È questo che li rende odiosi al Dio puro e santo. Così avviene quando un uomo o una donna cerca di purificare la propria casa con una pulizia superficiale. I tentativi farisaici di estirpare e rimuovere i dettagli superficiali e le incoerenze dalle vite del coniuge e dei figli, al fine di santificarli, sono generalmente infruttuosi.

Per quanto rapida possa essere la loro vista in altre cose; Cristo li chiama ciechi. Nella stima di Cristo, coloro che non conoscono la malvagità del proprio cuore—coloro che non vedono, e non odiano, il peccato segreto che è insediato dentro—sono estranei alla santificazione. L’ignoranza di sé è l’ignoranza più vergognosa e dannosa. La regola è: “Pulisci prima ciò che è dentro, per essere purificato dalla sporcizia dello spirito.” Affetti e inclinazioni corrotte, i desideri segreti che si nascondono nell’anima, non visti né osservati, questi devono prima essere riconosciuti, mortificati e sottomessi. Se si presta la dovuta cura a questo, l’esterno, per estensione, diventerà pulito anch’esso. Le motivazioni ed inducimenti esterni possono mantenere l’esterno pulito, mentre l’interno rimane sporco; ma se la grazia santificante rinnovata rende pulito l’interno, ciò avrà un’influenza duratura e profonda sull’esterno, perché il principio dominante è dentro. Se il cuore è ben custodito, tutto va bene, …perché da esso escono le sorgenti della vita –Proverbi 4:23.

Similmente voi mogli, state soggette ai vostri mariti; affinché, se alcuni non ubbidiscono alla parola, siano guadagnati senza parola dalla condotta delle mogli; osservando la vostra castità accompagnata dal timore. Il cui ornamento non sia l’esteriore intrecciarsi dei capelli e l’uso dell’oro, o l’abbigliamento; ma l’uomo nascosto del cuore, che non è corruttibile, cioè l’ornamento di uno spirito mansueto e tranquillo, che è di grande prezzo davanti a Dio. Poiché così in passato anche le sante donne che speravano in Dio si adornavano, essendo soggette ai loro mariti: come Sara obbediva ad Abramo, chiamandolo signore: delle quali voi siete figlie, se fate bene e non vi spaventate di alcuna minaccia. Allo stesso modo voi mariti, convivete con loro secondo conoscenza, dando onore alla moglie, come a vaso più debole, e come coeredi della grazia della vita; affinché le vostre preghiere non siano impedite –1 Pietro 3:1-7.

Qui Pietro parla di una moglie che conquista il marito con la dovuta benevolenza menzionata in Corinzi. Pur non avendo una garanzia incondizionata di santificare il marito, certamente incontrerà pochi successi senza di essa. Euodia era una giudea che, abbracciando la fede in Cristo, si trovò in un giogo disuguale con un greco. Leggiamo che la fede non fingita fu prima operata in sua madre Loide, e che ciò influenzò Euodia. Questo, a sua volta, ebbe un effetto santificante sul giovane Timoteo, che fu allora preparato per l’opera del Signore. Non abbiamo nessun resoconto che suo padre sia stato aggiunto alla fede, ma si può solo immaginare il tumulto iniziale nel petto di questa giovane giudea mentre onorava riverentemente il suo capo e non circoncideva suo figlio ma piuttosto lo affidava alla preghiera. Qui ci conduce all’altra dimensione vitale della santificazione della casa. Pur non essendo incoraggiata a insegnare al marito, apparentemente aveva guadagnato abbastanza suo rispetto da poter insegnare al figlio in casa. Questo lo fece diligentemente… Perché è santificato dalla parola di Dio e dalla preghiera –1 Timoteo 4:5.

E fin da fanciullo hai conosciuto le sacre Scritture, che possono renderti saggio alla salvezza mediante la fede che è in Cristo Gesù. Ogni Scrittura è ispirata da Dio e utile per insegnamento, per riprensione, per correzione, per educazione nella giustizia –2 Timoteo 3:15-16.

L'esterno santificato dalla Parola

Quando il cuore del credente è trattato prima, le dimensioni visibili della casa si sistemano in successione. Le influenze mondane hanno poco fascino per il nascente figlio di Dio. La Parola di Dio deve prendere il suo pieno posto nell’essere amministrata ai bambini così come agli adulti, perché è utile per la santificazione. Un marito deve lavare sua moglie e i figli (così come se stesso) amministrando la Parola di Dio affinché possa santificare e purificare la sua casa.

Mariti, amate le vostre mogli, come anche Cristo ha amato la chiesa e ha dato se stesso per essa; affinché la santificasse, purificandola con il lavacro dell’acqua per mezzo della parola, per presentarla a se stesso una chiesa gloriosa, senza macchia, né ruga, né altro simile; ma che sia santa e irreprensibile –Efesini 5:25-27.

Quando la Parola di Dio è investita della piena autorità in casa, essa diventa il principio governante intorno a cui la famiglia opera. Deve essere permesso che filtri i media delle masse e le influenze di tutte le comunicazioni malvagie, che corrompono i buoni costumi.

Beato l’uomo che non cammina nel consiglio degli empi, né sta nella via dei peccatori, né siede nel banco degli stolti –Salmo 1:1.

Gli individui all’interno della casa potrebbero non apprezzare sempre la direzione ricevuta da essa, ma devono sottomettersi e di solito lo fanno di buon grado. La maggior parte di noi ha ricevuto indicazioni dai propri genitori che non apprezzavamo allora ma anni dopo abbiamo compreso la benedizione della loro guida. Una leadership che non guida, non esprime amore, e lascerà la casa non santificata e i suoi membri disconnessi. Sebbene sia piuttosto scomodo e inconveniente chiedere ai bambini di fare a meno di ciò di cui altri godono, essi non sono santificati seguendo i loro pari, ma piuttosto dalla verità. Per noi genitori non c’è gioia più grande che sapere che i nostri figli camminano nella verità. Allo stesso modo, non c’è gioia più grande per loro che camminare in essa. Le devozioni familiari quotidiane sono una forza coesiva all’interno della casa che è centrale e integrante per la santificazione domestica. Non osiamo scusarci per l’autorità che attribuiamo alla Parola, né allentare il suo uso. È un Vangelo erroneo credere che le anime vengano soffocate quando sono tenute ai suoi comandamenti.

Ecco il riassunto che Cristo fa della Sua casa.

Io ho manifestato il tuo nome agli uomini che tu mi hai dati dal mondo: erano tuoi e tu me li hai dati; ed essi hanno osservato la tua parola. Ora hanno conosciuto che tutte le cose che tu mi hai date sono da te. Perché io ho dato loro le parole che tu mi hai dato; ed essi le hanno ricevute e hanno conosciuto con certezza che io sono venuto da te, e hanno creduto che tu mi hai mandato. Io prego per loro; non prego per il mondo, ma per quelli che tu mi hai dati, perché sono tuoi. E tutte le mie sono tue e le tue sono mie; e io sono stato glorificato in loro. Ora non sono più nel mondo, ma questi sono nel mondo, e io vado a te. Padre santo, custodisci per mezzo del tuo nome coloro che tu mi hai dati, affinché siano uno come noi. Mentre ero con loro nel mondo, io li custodivo nel tuo nome: quelli che tu mi hai dati li ho custoditi e nessuno di loro è andato perduto, eccetto il figlio della perdizione; affinché la Scrittura si adempisse. Ora vado a te; e queste cose dico nel mondo, affinché la loro gioia sia compiuta in sé. Io ho dato loro la tua parola; e il mondo li ha odiati, perché non sono del mondo, come io non sono del mondo. Io non prego che tu li tolga dal mondo, ma che tu li custodisca dal maligno. Essi non sono del mondo, come io non sono del mondo. Santificali per mezzo della verità: la tua parola è verità –Giovanni 17:6-17.

Cristo, come capo della Sua casa, non impiegò mezzi complicati per la santificazione dei Suoi figli. La Sua vita manifestò un costante mantenersi nell’amore di Dio mediante fede e preghiera, e l’amministrazione della Parola di Dio a coloro che gli stavano intorno. Talvolta inciampavano in essa, lottavano interiormente e lo fraintendevano, ma la forza di custodia non riposava sui lauri di parole convincenti, forza adamantina, attività divertenti né ragionamenti prudenti.

Mentre una casa deve impiegare queste risorse di tanto in tanto, esse di per sé non contengono il potere santificante. Perché è santificato dalla parola di Dio e dalla preghiera –1 Timoteo 4:5.

Sigmund Freud, the “father of psychology” and an enemy of the Christian faith, spent much time reflecting on the “problem” of how to overcome the sense of guilt, which he believed to be the negative by-product of religious teaching. He commented that “only through the solidarity of all the participants (of a group) could the sense of guilt be assuaged.”

Being a member of a group with a common focus or goal has the ability to radically change, not only man’s outlook and views, but also his concept of right and wrong, good and evil, etc. It can indeed rid the soul of its normal God-given sense of guilt as the standards of right and wrong are modified. Some parents have discovered this fact when their young people joined a youth group. Some who previously respected their parents’, the church’s, and God’s authority, no longer held the same convictions. If they joined a group whose focus was to have fun and they believed that the “established” rules, facts, and truth were what stood in the way of fulfilling their carnal desires, then the establishment and their rules became the enemy of the group. Right and wrong are determined by the consensus of the group in respect to its goals. If the goal is pleasure, “It isn’t right for (any authority or any rule) to interfere.”

“The child takes on the characteristic behavior of the group in which he is placed … he reflects the behavior patterns which are set by the … leader of the group” (Kurt Lewin, in A Sociology of Education).

Although it seems strange, “it is usually easier to change individuals formed into a group than to change any one of them separately”, according to Kurt Lewin. An individual will naturally resist change to his or her personal beliefs. However, one who is already a member of a group with a common goal (which all groups have), will automatically have that resistance broken down, as far as attitudes of the group are concerned. Example: I am part of this group, so the outlook and opinions of the group are my outlook and opinions. Too often, not one individual of the group will thoroughly examine the group’s beliefs but will take them for granted because they are a part of the group to which he or she belongs.

“One of the most fascinating aspects of group therapy is that everyone is born again, born together in the group”. (Irvin D. Yalom). This can easily be observed among all ages who are part of a group by virtue of common interests.

Adolf Hitler made very effective use of group dynamics with his Hitler Youth groups. Not only was he able to give them a sense of belonging and a cause to support, but he was able to effectively change the moral compass of the youth of his day.

The Bible also records very effective group dynamics and how quickly they can influence people without evidence. In Acts 14:1, we see the group ready to offer sacrifices to Paul as a god, and in the next verse they stoned him. Acts 19 tells of a group yelling “Great is Diana of the Ephesians” for hours. Verse 32 says that most of the people didn’t even know what the fuss was about, but they would have killed for whatever it was. In these examples, possibly not even one individual really stopped to seriously consider what was morally right or wrong. They were taking up the cause of the group. It gave a sense of “rightness” and belonging, just to be a contributing supporter of the cause. But stop and think—the cause, the action, and the consequences should always be carefully considered.

These people were not taking individual responsibility to determine what is morally right and wrong. Too often people don’t, rather they only function as a group. But the Bible tells us that the time will come when we will all be personally held accountable for what we have done in this life. At that time, what the group believed or did will make no difference. When we (each one of us) will stand one day (at the end of time) before God’s judgement throne, we will be judged according to …the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds –Romans 2:5-6.

As we read in the biblical books of the Kings and the Chronicles, Israel, as a nation, functioned with strong group dynamics. When a good king came to power, the nation in general turned to the Lord. When an evil king came to power, the nation in general turned to idol worship. There were a few exceptions—a few people who thought for themselves—whose allegiance to God was greater than their allegiance to the king or nation.

The Christian church itself is a group, influencing and changing the perspectives and morality of individuals for the right or the wrong. Dependent on the convictions of the group and its leaders, the church can be an influence of godly morality, or it can explain away the Bible’s concepts of good and evil.

There should be a major difference between the Christian church and all other groups regarding how their group dynamics work. The Christian church is a group for the express purpose of turning people’s allegiance and faith to Jesus Christ as revealed in His Word, rather than to the group itself. A church whose goal is to gain converts to itself has failed in its mission as detailed in God’s Word. A church that is successful in turning people from all other allegiances to Jesus Christ is a successful church. Allegiance to Jesus includes obedience to His Word which requires obedience to all authorities, including the church. But the Christian’s obedience to the church is secondary and a result of his obedience to Jesus, not the other way around. If a church is successful in turning its members’ faith and focus to Jesus as revealed in His Word, these members will then be unwilling to allow the church to accept unscriptural modern doctrines, and the church will remain sound in …the faith which was once delivered unto the saints –Jude 1:3.

May each one of us, both collectively and individually, focus our faith on Jesus Christ.

মনস্তত্ত্বের “পিতা” এবং খ্রিস্টীয় বিশ্বাসের প্রতিপক্ষ সিগমুন্ড ফ্রয়েড অনেক সময় ব্যয় করতেন ওই “অপরাধবোধ”–কেন তাকে এড়ানো যায় না এবং এটি ধর্মীয় শিক্ষার নেতিবাচক পার্শ্বফল—এই সমস্যাটির উপর চিন্তা করে। তিনি মন্তব্য করেছিলেন, “শুধুমাত্র সকল অংশগ্রহণকারীর ঐক্য (একটি গোষ্ঠীর) মাধ্যমে অপরাধবোধ প্রশমিত করা যায়।”

একটি সাধারণ লক্ষ্য বা উদ্দেশ্যযুক্ত একটি গোষ্ঠীর সদস্য হওয়া কেবল মানুষের দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি ও মতামতকেই নয়, বরং তার ভাল ও মন্দ, সঠিক ও ভুল—এই ধারণাকেও মৌলিকভাবে বদলে দিতে পারে। নীতির মান বদলে গেলে প্রকৃত ঈশ্বর-প্রদত্ত অপরাধবোধও আত্মা থেকে মিটে যেতে পারে। কিছু বাবা-মা এই বিষয়টি আবিষ্কার করেছেন যখন তাদের কিশোরেরা কোনো যুব গোষ্ঠীতে যোগ দিয়েছে। যারা পূর্বে তাদের পিতামাতার, চার্চের, এবং ঈশ্বরের কর্তৃত্বকে সম্মান করতেন, তারা আর একই বিশ্বাস বজায় রাখেননি। যদি তারা এমন একটি গোষ্ঠীতে যোগ দেয় যার লক্ষ্য মজা করা এবং তারা বিশ্বাস করে যে “প্রতিষ্ঠিত” নিয়ম, তথ্য ও সত্যই তাদের কামুক ইচ্ছা পূরণে বাধা দেয়, তখন প্রতিষ্ঠিত প্রতিষ্ঠান এবং তাদের নিয়মই গোষ্ঠীর শত্রু হয়ে ওঠে। সঠিক ও ভুল নির্ধারিত হয় গোষ্ঠীর সম্মতিমতের মাধ্যমে, গোষ্ঠীর লক্ষ্য অনুযায়ী। যদি লক্ষ্য হয় আনন্দ, তখন “কাউকে (কোনো কর্তৃপক্ষ বা নিয়মকে) ব্যাহত করা উচিত নয়” — এমন মনোভাব তৈরি হতে পারে।

“শিশুটি যে গোষ্ঠীতে স্থাপন করা হয় সেখানে গোষ্ঠীর বৈশিষ্ট্যময় আচরণ গ্রহণ করে … সে যে আচরণ প্যাটার্নগুলি প্রতিফলিত করে সেগুলি গোষ্ঠীটিকে নেতৃত্ব দানকারী … নেতার দ্বারা স্থির হয়” (কার্ট লিউইন, A Sociology of Education থেকে)।

যদিও এটা অদ্ভুত শোনায়, “সাধারণত একটি গোষ্ঠীতে গঠিত ব্যক্তিদের বদলানো আলাদা আলাদা প্রতিটি ব্যক্তিকে বদলানোর চেয়ে সহজ”, বলে কার্ট লিউইন। একজন ব্যক্তি স্বভাবতই তার ব্যক্তিগত বিশ্বাস পরিবর্তনে প্রতিরোধ করবে। তথাপি, যে ব্যক্তি ইতিমধ্যে একটি সাধারণ লক্ষ্যযুক্ত গোষ্ঠীর সদস্য (যা সব গোষ্ঠীরই থাকে), সেই ব্যক্তির গোষ্ঠীয় মনোভাবসমূহ সম্পর্কে সেই প্রতিরোধ স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে ভেঙে পড়ে। উদাহরণ: আমি এই গোষ্ঠীর অংশ, সুতরাং গোষ্ঠীর দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি ও মতামতই আমার দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি ও মতামত। প্রায়ই, গোষ্ঠীর কোনো একক ব্যক্তি গোষ্ঠীর বিশ্বাসগুলি গভীরভাবে পর্যালোচনা করে না, বরং সেগুলোকে স্বীকার করে নেয় কারণ সে নিজেই যে গোষ্ঠীর অংশ সে সেটিরই অংশ।

“গোষ্ঠী থেরাপির সবচেয়ে আকর্ষণীয় দিকগুলির মধ্যে একটি হলো যে সবাই গোষ্ঠীর মধ্যে একসাথে নতুন করে জন্ম নেয়” (ইরভিন ডি. ইয়েলম)। সাধারণ স্বার্থের ভিত্তিতে গোষ্ঠীর অংশ যারা তারা তাদের মধ্যে সহজেই এটি দেখা যায়।

অ্যাডলফ হিটলারের হিটলার ইয়ুথ গোষ্ঠীগুলিতে তিনি গোষ্ঠী গতিবিদ্যার খুব কার্যকর ব্যবহার করেছিলেন। তিনি কেবল তাদের মাঝে আত্মসম্মান ও সমর্থনের কারণ দেয়া সীমাবদ্ধ করেননি, বরং তিনি তার যুগের যুবসমাজের নৈতিক দিকচিহ্নও কার্যকরভাবে পরিবর্তন করতে সক্ষম ছিলেন।

বাইবেলেও অত্যন্ত কার্যকরী গোষ্ঠী গতিবিদ্যার কত দ্রুত প্রমাণবিহীনভাবে মানুষকে প্রভাবিত করতে পারে তার নজির রয়েছে। প্রেরিতদের কাজ 14:1-এ আমরা দেখি গোষ্ঠী পলের কাছে দেবতা হিসাবে বলি দেওয়ার সজ্জা করতে প্রস্তুত ছিল, এবং পরের বচনে তাঁরা তাঁকে পাথর মারল। প্রেরিতদের কাজ 19-এ একটি গোষ্ঠীর কয়েক ঘন্টার জন্য “ইফেসিয়দের ডায়ানা মহান” বলে চেঁচানোর কথা বলা হয়েছে। 32 নম্বর বচনে বলা হয়েছে বেশিরভাগ মানুষ জানতেনই না কেন ওই শোরগোল, কিন্তু তারা যা-ই হোক তার জন্য হত্যা করত। এই উদাহরণগুলোয়, সম্ভবত একজন ব্যক্তিও সত্যিই থেমে গুরুতরভাবে বিবেচনা করেনি কী নৈতিকভাবে সঠিক বা ভুল। তারা গোষ্ঠীর কারণকে সমর্থন করছিল। কেবল গোষ্ঠীর জন্য অবদানকারী সমর্থক হওয়াই “সঠিক হওয়ার” এবং অন্তর্ভুক্তির অনুভূতি দিয়েছিল। কিন্তু থামুন ও চিন্তা করুন—উক্ত কারণ, কর্ম এবং পরিণতিগুলো সবসময় সতর্কভাবে বিবেচনা করা উচিত।

এই মানুষগুলো ব্যক্তি হিসেবে দায়িত্ব নিচ্ছিল না নৈতিকভাবে কী সঠিক ও কী ভুল নির্ধারণ করার জন্য। প্রায়ই মানুষগুলো তা করে না; তারা কেবল গোষ্ঠী হিসাবে কাজ করে। কিন্তু বাইবেল আমাদের বলে যে একটি সময় আসবে যখন আমরা সকলেই ব্যক্তিগতভাবে আমাদের জীবনে যা করেছি তার জন্য হিসাব দিতে হবে। তখন গোষ্ঠী কী বিশ্বাস করেছিল বা করেছিল—তার কোনো প্রভাব থাকবে না। যখন আমরা (আমরা প্রত্যেকে) একদিন (সময়ের শেষে) ঈশ্বরের বিচারের সিংহাসনের সামনে দাঁড়াব, তখন আমরা বিচারপ্রাপ্ত হব …ঈশ্বরের ধার্মিক বিচার অনুযায়ী; যিনি প্রত্যেক মানুষের প্রতি তার কর্ম অনুযায়ী প্রতিদান করবেন – রোমীয়দের 2:5-6।

রাজাদের বই এবং ইতিহাসগ্রন্থগুলিতে যেমন আমরা পড়ি, ইস্রায়েল জাতি হিসেবে শক্তিশালী গোষ্ঠী গতিবিধিতে পরিচালিত হত। যখন একটি ভাল রাজা ক্ষমতায় আসত, জাতি সাধারণত প্রভুর দিকে ফিরে যেত। যখন একটি কুফল রাজা ক্ষমতায় আসত, জাতি সাধারণত মূর্তি আরাধনায় ফিরে যেত। কয়েকটি ব্যতিক্রম ছিল—কয়েকজন ব্যক্তি যারা নিজেরাই চিন্তা করত—তাঁদের ঈশ্বরের প্রতি আনুগত্য রাজা বা জাতির প্রতি তাদের আনুগত্যের চেয়ে বড় ছিল।

খ্রিস্টীয় চার্চ নিজেই একটি গোষ্ঠী, যে ব্যক্তিদের দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি ও নৈতিকতাকে ঠিক বা ভুলভাবে প্রভাবিত ও পরিবর্তিত করে। গোষ্ঠীর বিশ্বাস এবং নেতাদের দৃঢ়তার ওপর নির্ভর করে, চার্চ ঈশ্বরীয় নৈতিকতার প্রভাব হতে পারে, অথবা এটি বাইবেলের ভালো ও মন্দের ধারণাগুলো ব্যাখ্যা করে অগ্রাহ্য করে দিতে পারে।

খ্রিস্টীয় চার্চ এবং অন্যান্য সকল গোষ্ঠীর গোষ্ঠী গতিবিধির কাজ করার উপায় সম্পর্কে একটি বড় পার্থক্য থাকা উচিত। খ্রিস্টীয় চার্চ হল বিশেষভাবে এমন একটি গোষ্ঠী যার উদ্দেশ্য মানুষের আনুগত্য ও বিশ্বাসকে গোষ্ঠীর প্রতি নয়, বরং তাঁর বাক্যে প্রকাশিত যীশু খ্রীষ্টের প্রতি ঘুরিয়ে দেওয়া। যে চার্চের লক্ষ্য নিজের প্রতি রূপান্তর লাভ করানো, সে ঈশ্বরের বাক্যে বর্ণিত নিজের মিশনে ব্যর্থ হয়েছে। যে চার্চ অন্যান্য সকল আনুগত্য থেকে মানুষকে যীশু খ্রীষ্টের প্রতি পরিবর্তন করতে সফল, সেই চার্চ সফল। যীশুর প্রতি আনুগত্যের মধ্যে তাঁর বাক্যের প্রতি আনুগত্য অন্তর্ভুক্ত থাকে যা সকল কর্তৃপক্ষের প্রতি আনুগত্য দাবি করে, চার্চ সহ। কিন্তু খ্রিস্টানের চার্চের প্রতি আনুগত্য দ্বিতীয়ক ও তাঁর যীশুর প্রতি আনুগত্যের ফল, বিপরীত নয়। যদি একটি চার্চ তার সদস্যদের বিশ্বাস ও মনোযোগকে তাঁর বাক্যে প্রকাশিত যীশুর প্রতি পরিবর্তিত করতে সফল হয়, তখন এই সদস্যরা চার্চকে অসংগত আধুনিক মতবাদ গ্রহণ করতে দেবে না, এবং চার্চ …যে বিশ্বাস একবার পৌরোহিতদের কাছে সরবরাহ করা হয়েছে সেই বিশ্বাসে টিকে থাকবে – যিহূদা 1:3।

আমরা প্রত্যেকে, সমষ্টিগত ও ব্যক্তিগতভাবে, আমাদের বিশ্বাস যীশু খ্রীষ্টের প্রতি কেন্দ্রীভূত করি—এটাই আমাদের প্রার্থনা।

Sigmund Freud, the “father of psychology” and an enemy of the Christian faith, spent much time reflecting on the “problem” of how to overcome the sense of guilt, which he believed to be the negative by-product of religious teaching. He commented that “only through the solidarity of all the participants (of a group) could the sense of guilt be assuaged.”

Being a member of a group with a common focus or goal has the ability to radically change, not only man’s outlook and views, but also his concept of right and wrong, good and evil, etc. It can indeed rid the soul of its normal God-given sense of guilt as the standards of right and wrong are modified. Some parents have discovered this fact when their young people joined a youth group. Some who previously respected their parents’, the church’s, and God’s authority, no longer held the same convictions. If they joined a group whose focus was to have fun and they believed that the “established” rules, facts, and truth were what stood in the way of fulfilling their carnal desires, then the establishment and their rules became the enemy of the group. Right and wrong are determined by the consensus of the group in respect to its goals. If the goal is pleasure, “It isn’t right for (any authority or any rule) to interfere.”

“The child takes on the characteristic behavior of the group in which he is placed … he reflects the behavior patterns which are set by the … leader of the group” (Kurt Lewin, in A Sociology of Education).

Although it seems strange, “it is usually easier to change individuals formed into a group than to change any one of them separately”, according to Kurt Lewin. An individual will naturally resist change to his or her personal beliefs. However, one who is already a member of a group with a common goal (which all groups have), will automatically have that resistance broken down, as far as attitudes of the group are concerned. Example: I am part of this group, so the outlook and opinions of the group are my outlook and opinions. Too often, not one individual of the group will thoroughly examine the group’s beliefs but will take them for granted because they are a part of the group to which he or she belongs.

“One of the most fascinating aspects of group therapy is that everyone is born again, born together in the group”. (Irvin D. Yalom). This can easily be observed among all ages who are part of a group by virtue of common interests.

Adolf Hitler made very effective use of group dynamics with his Hitler Youth groups. Not only was he able to give them a sense of belonging and a cause to support, but he was able to effectively change the moral compass of the youth of his day.

The Bible also records very effective group dynamics and how quickly they can influence people without evidence. In Acts 14:1, we see the group ready to offer sacrifices to Paul as a god, and in the next verse they stoned him. Acts 19 tells of a group yelling “Great is Diana of the Ephesians” for hours. Verse 32 says that most of the people didn’t even know what the fuss was about, but they would have killed for whatever it was. In these examples, possibly not even one individual really stopped to seriously consider what was morally right or wrong. They were taking up the cause of the group. It gave a sense of “rightness” and belonging, just to be a contributing supporter of the cause. But stop and think—the cause, the action, and the consequences should always be carefully considered.

These people were not taking individual responsibility to determine what is morally right and wrong. Too often people don’t, rather they only function as a group. But the Bible tells us that the time will come when we will all be personally held accountable for what we have done in this life. At that time, what the group believed or did will make no difference. When we (each one of us) will stand one day (at the end of time) before God’s judgement throne, we will be judged according to …the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds –Romans 2:5-6.

As we read in the biblical books of the Kings and the Chronicles, Israel, as a nation, functioned with strong group dynamics. When a good king came to power, the nation in general turned to the Lord. When an evil king came to power, the nation in general turned to idol worship. There were a few exceptions—a few people who thought for themselves—whose allegiance to God was greater than their allegiance to the king or nation.

The Christian church itself is a group, influencing and changing the perspectives and morality of individuals for the right or the wrong. Dependent on the convictions of the group and its leaders, the church can be an influence of godly morality, or it can explain away the Bible’s concepts of good and evil.

There should be a major difference between the Christian church and all other groups regarding how their group dynamics work. The Christian church is a group for the express purpose of turning people’s allegiance and faith to Jesus Christ as revealed in His Word, rather than to the group itself. A church whose goal is to gain converts to itself has failed in its mission as detailed in God’s Word. A church that is successful in turning people from all other allegiances to Jesus Christ is a successful church. Allegiance to Jesus includes obedience to His Word which requires obedience to all authorities, including the church. But the Christian’s obedience to the church is secondary and a result of his obedience to Jesus, not the other way around. If a church is successful in turning its members’ faith and focus to Jesus as revealed in His Word, these members will then be unwilling to allow the church to accept unscriptural modern doctrines, and the church will remain sound in …the faith which was once delivered unto the saints –Jude 1:3.

May each one of us, both collectively and individually, focus our faith on Jesus Christ.

정신분석학의 아버지이자 기독교 신앙의 적수였던 지그문트 프로이트는 종교적 가르침의 부정적 부산물이라고 믿었던 죄책감의 감정을 어떻게 극복할지에 대해 많은 시간을 할애해 성찰했다. 그는 “오직 모든 참가자들의 연대(집단의 연대)를 통해서만 죄책감의 감정을 누그러뜨릴 수 있다”고 논평했다.

공통의 초점이나 목표를 가진 집단의 구성원이 된다는 것은 사람의 관점과 견해뿐 아니라 옳고 그름, 선과 악에 대한 개념까지 근본적으로 바꿀 수 있는 능력이 있다. 집단의 옳고 그름의 기준이 수정되면 정상적으로 하나님께서 주신 죄책감의 감정마저 제거될 수 있다. 어떤 부모들은 자녀들이 청소년 집단에 들어갔을 때 이 사실을 발견했다. 이전에 부모와 교회, 그리고 하나님의 권위를 존중하던 이들이 더 이상 같은 신념을 지니지 않게 된 것이다. 만약 그들이 즐거움을 추구하는 데 초점을 둔 집단에 가입했고, 그 집단이 ‘기성’의 규칙, 사실, 진리가 육욕을 충족하는 데 걸림돌이라고 믿는다면, 기성 체제와 그 규칙들은 집단의 적이 된다. 옳고 그름은 집단의 목표에 관한 합의에 의해 결정된다. 만약 목표가 쾌락이라면 “(어떤 권위나 어떤 규칙이라 할지라도) 간섭하는 것은 옳지 않다”고 여겨진다.

“그 아이는 그가 배치된 집단의 특징적인 행동을 취한다 … 그는 … 집단의 지도자가 정한 행동 양식을 반영한다”(커트 르윈, 『교육의 사회학』에서).

이상하게 들리겠지만, “집단으로 형성된 개인들을 바꾸는 것이 개별적으로 그들 중 어느 한 사람을 바꾸는 것보다 보통 더 쉽다”고 커트 르윈은 말한다. 개인은 본래 자신의 신념 변화에 저항한다. 그러나 이미 공통의 목표를 가진 집단의 일원인 사람은(모든 집단이 가지는) 집단의 태도에 관해서는 그 저항이 자동으로 무너진다. 예: 나는 이 집단의 일원이다. 그러므로 집단의 관점과 의견은 나의 관점과 의견이다. 너무 자주 집단의 어떤 개인도 집단의 신념을 철저히 검토하지 않고 그것들을 당연하게 여기며, 자신이 속한 집단의 일부이기 때문에 그대로 받아들인다.

“집단치료의 가장 매혹적인 측면 중 하나는 모두가 거듭나고, 집단 안에서 함께 거듭난다는 것이다.”(어빈 D. 얄롬). 이는 공통의 관심을 가진 집단의 일원인 모든 연령대에서 쉽게 관찰할 수 있다.

아돌프 히틀러는 히틀러 유겐트 집단을 통해 집단 역학을 매우 효과적으로 이용했다. 그는 그들에게 소속감과 지지할 대의를 제공했을 뿐 아니라, 당대 청소년들의 도덕 나침반을 효과적으로 바꿀 수 있었다.

성경도 집단 역학이 얼마나 효과적이며 증거 없이 사람들에게 얼마나 빠르게 영향을 미칠 수 있는지를 기록하고 있다. 사도행전 14:1에서 우리는 무리가 바울에게 제물로 드리려 하려고 준비된 모습을 보고, 다음 절에서는 그들이 그를 돌로 쳤음을 본다. 사도행전 19장은 한 무리가 몇 시간 동안 “에베소의 대(大)여신 다이아네아”를 외쳤던 일을 전한다. 32절은 대부분의 사람들이 소란이 왜 일어났는지조차 알지 못했지만, 그들이 그것을 위해서라면 누구든 죽일 것이라고 말한다. 이러한 예들에서, 아마도 한 개인이라도 도덕적으로 옳고 그름이 무엇인지 진지하게 숙고한 사람은 거의 없었을 것이다. 그들은 집단의 대의를 옹호하고 있었다. 그것은 단지 대의의 기여자가 되는 것만으로도 ‘옳음’과 소속감을 주었다. 그러나 잠시 멈추어 생각해 보라—대의, 행동, 그리고 결과는 항상 신중히 고려되어야 한다.

이 사람들은 도덕적으로 옳고 그름을 결정하기 위해 개인적 책임을 지지 않았다. 너무 자주 사람들은 그렇게 하지 않고 단지 집단으로서 기능할 뿐이다. 그러나 성경은 우리 모두가 이 생에서 행한 일에 대해 개인적으로 책임을 지게 될 때가 올 것이라고 말한다. 그때에는 집단이 무엇을 믿었는지 또는 무엇을 했는지는 아무런 차이가 없다. 우리가(각각의 우리 모두가) 언젠가(시대의 끝에) 하나님의 심판대 앞에 설 때, 우리는 …하나님의 의로운 심판대로 심판을 받을 것이라. 각 사람에게는 그의 행위들대로 갚으시리라 –로마서 2:5-6.

열왕기와 역대기의 성경서들을 읽어보면, 이스라엘은 국가로서 강한 집단 역학으로 기능했다는 것을 알 수 있다. 선한 왕이 통치할 때에는 나라 전체가 일반적으로 여호와께로 돌이켰다. 악한 왕이 통치할 때에는 나라 전체가 일반적으로 우상 숭배로 돌아갔다. 몇몇 예외가 있었는데—스스로 생각한 소수의 사람들이 있었고—그들의 하나님에 대한 충성은 왕이나 국가에 대한 충성보다 더 컸다.

기독교 교회 자체도 하나의 집단으로서 개인들의 관점과 도덕성을 올바르게든 잘못되었든 영향을 미치고 변화시킨다. 집단과 그 지도자들의 신념에 따라 교회는 경건한 도덕성의 영향력이 될 수도 있고, 성경의 선악 개념을 변명해 버릴 수도 있다.

그들의 집단 역학이 작동하는 방식에 관해 기독교 교회와 모든 다른 집단 사이에는 큰 차이가 있어야 한다. 기독교 교회는 사람들이 집단 자체가 아니라 그들의 신앙과 충성을 그분의 말씀에 계시된 예수 그리스도에게 돌이키도록 하는 분명한 목적을 가진 집단이다. 교회 자신에게 개종자를 얻는 것을 목표로 하는 교회는 하나님의 말씀에 상세히 기록된 그 사명에서 실패한 것이다. 다른 모든 충성심에서 사람들을 끌어내어 예수 그리스도께로 돌이키는 데 성공한 교회는 성공한 교회이다. 예수에 대한 충성은 그의 말씀에 대한 순종을 포함하며, 이는 교회를 포함한 모든 권위에 대한 순종을 요구한다. 그러나 교회에 대한 그리스도인의 순종은 부차적이며 그리스도에 대한 순종의 결과이지, 그 반대가 아니다. 교회가 그 구성원들의 신앙과 초점을 그분의 말씀에 계시된 예수에게로 돌이키는 데 성공한다면, 그 구성원들은 교회가 불성경적인 현대 교리를 수용하도록 결코 허용하지 않을 것이고, 교회는 …성도들에게 한 번 전하여진 믿음을 지킬지니라 –유다서 1:3.라는 데 있어 건전하게 남을 것이다.

우리 각자가, 집단적으로나 개인적으로나, 우리 믿음을 예수 그리스도에게 집중하기를 바란다.

Greetings of Christian love to one and all. In this issue of the magazine (Summer 2023)… The Church History article focuses on Bible prophecy pertaining to the end times and some various ways that over the years certain elements of the church got off track from the Biblical teaching as it pertained to their everyday life. In his article, Donny Brechbill, who together with his wife teaches multiple marriage seminars each year, endeavors to zone in on a challenging subject—some of the root problems that they see with women who are struggling in the church. Lee Rufener takes an unapologetic approach in his effort to share some expository teaching on practical ways to have a sanctified home. We have a new writer for the sisters this time who shares a burden on her heart—instilling God’s Word in the hearts of the next generation.

Plus, more interesting topics. Enjoy.

If you are edified or encouraged by any of the authors’ content, it would be a blessing for you to respond to us by mail or email. We pass this along to our writers for their benefit.

Recently, I was pondering the subject of change. As I have written before, we have gone through a fair bit of change as a family. During the last 1 to 2 years, we moved to another place of residence, I acquired a new job, and finally, praise the Lord, I have mostly recovered from most of the long-term effects of Covid. A special thanks to each one who has prayed for my health.

As I paused in quiet reminiscence, I was surprised by all the things that have changed in the 40-plus years that I can recall from memory. (Even though I am over 50 I really don’t remember much from the earliest years of my life.)

As a boy, I rode around in vehicles that had no seat belts and for sure, no airbags. When both of those “lifesaving” devices were first being introduced I well remember the many discussions whether they were truly lifesaving in their effect or whether the opposite was true. All vehicles used to be rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. How odd it seemed when the first front-wheel drive cars started to appear. Now we have hybrid vehicles with a push towards fully electric vehicles.

Forty-plus years ago, most farmers had gas-powered tractors with a carburetor or a diesel tractor with a manually powered injector pump. Today, most tractors are equipped with a computer and seemingly miles of wires and electronic this and electronic that. Back then, most farmers were able to maintain or repair their own equipment; now there is a need for diagnostic machines and specialized tools which cost a lot of money and take many hours to learn how to operate. This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.

Then there was Covid. That was a stressful time. Have you noticed what has changed during, after, or as a result of Covid? As I interact with others, routinely someone will say that this or that is different since Covid. Is it just me, or since Covid is the general public less friendly and more private with their interactions? Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”. Also, there are help wanted signs everywhere. Why? It seems to me that Covid has encouraged what little work ethic was still flourishing in our society to diminish even further.

Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes. What do these two disconnected products have in common? From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items have done more to change a people and a culture in a more major way than almost anything else has in recent times.

Where does this all leave us? The Hebrew writer says that For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. So, we see that God changed things as He saw fit, thus, if we need to change to become more Biblical, then we should. But the Apostle Paul says That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. So, let us be vigilant in these end times as change happens more and more around us. May we be among those who shall endure until the end.

Χαιρετισμοί χριστιανικής αγάπης σε όλους και όλες. Σε αυτό το τεύχος του περιοδικού (Καλοκαίρι 2023)… Το άρθρο της Εκκλησιαστικής Ιστορίας επικεντρώνεται στις βιβλικές προφητείες που αφορούν τα έσχατα και σε διάφορους τρόπους με τους οποίους με τα χρόνια ορισμένα στοιχεία της εκκλησίας απομακρύνθηκαν από τη Βιβλική διδασκαλία όσον αφορά την καθημερινή τους ζωή. Στο άρθρο του, ο Donny Brechbill, ο οποίος μαζί με τη σύζυγό του διδάσκει πολλά σεμινάρια γάμου κάθε χρόνο, προσπαθεί να εστιάσει σε ένα δύσκολο θέμα—μερικά από τα ριζικά προβλήματα που βλέπουν σε γυναίκες που πασχίζουν στην εκκλησία. Ο Lee Rufener ακολουθεί μια αμετανόητη προσέγγιση στην προσπάθειά του να μοιραστεί εξηγητική διδασκαλία για πρακτικούς τρόπους να έχει κανείς ένα αγιασμένο σπίτι. Αυτή τη φορά έχουμε μια νέα συγγραφέα για τις αδελφές που μοιράζεται ένα βάρος στην καρδιά της—να εμφυσήσει τον Λόγο του Θεού στις καρδιές της επόμενης γενιάς.

Επιπλέον, κι άλλες ενδιαφέρουσες θεματικές. Απολαύστε.

Αν ωφεληθήκατε ή ενθαρρυνθήκατε από το περιεχόμενο κάποιου από τους συγγραφείς, θα ήταν ευλογία για εμάς να απαντήσετε με ταχυδρομείο ή ηλεκτρονικό ταχυδρομείο. Το μεταβιβάζουμε στους συγγραφείς για το όφελός τους.

Πρόσφατα, σκεφτόμουν το θέμα της αλλαγής. Όπως έχω γράψει και πριν, περάσαμε αρκετές αλλαγές ως οικογένεια. Τους τελευταίους 1 έως 2 χρόνους, μετακομίσαμε σε άλλο τόπο κατοικίας, απέκτησα νέα εργασία και τέλος, δοξάζω τον Κύριο, έχω σε μεγάλο βαθμό αναρρώσει από τα περισσότερα μακροχρόνια αποτελέσματα του Covid. Ειδικές ευχαριστίες σε καθέναν που προσευχήθηκε για την υγεία μου.

Καθώς σταμάτησα για ήσυχη αναπόληση, με εξέπληξαν όλα όσα έχουν αλλάξει τα τελευταία πάνω από 40 χρόνια που θυμάμαι με μνήμη. (Ακόμη και αν είμαι πάνω από 50, πραγματικά δεν θυμάμαι πολλά από τα πρώτα χρόνια της ζωής μου.)

Όταν ήμουν αγόρι, κυκλοφορούσα σε οχήματα χωρίς ζώνες ασφαλείας και σίγουρα, χωρίς αερόσακους. Όταν και οι δύο αυτές «συσκευές διάσωσης» εισάγονταν για πρώτη φορά, θυμάμαι καλά τις πολλές συζητήσεις για το αν ήταν πραγματικά διασωστικές στην επίδρασή τους ή αν ίσχυε το αντίθετο. Όλα τα οχήματα είχαν παλαιότερα κίνηση στους πίσω τροχούς ή τετρακίνηση. Πόσο περίεργο φάνηκε όταν άρχισαν να εμφανίζονται τα πρώτα αυτοκίνητα με κίνηση στους εμπρός τροχούς. Τώρα έχουμε υβριδικά οχήματα με ώθηση προς πλήρως ηλεκτρικά οχήματα.

Πριν από πάνω από σαράντα χρόνια, οι περισσότεροι αγρότες είχαν τρακτέρ βενζίνης με καρμπυρατέρ ή ντιζελοκίνητα τρακτέρ με χειροκίνητη αντλία έγχυσης. Σήμερα, τα περισσότερα τρακτέρ είναι εξοπλισμένα με υπολογιστή και φαινομενικά μίλια καλωδίων και ηλεκτρονικά το ένα και το άλλο. Τότε, οι περισσότεροι αγρότες μπορούσαν να συντηρήσουν ή να επισκευάσουν οι ίδιοι τον εξοπλισμό τους· τώρα υπάρχει ανάγκη για διαγνωστικές μηχανές και ειδικά εργαλεία που κοστίζουν πολλά χρήματα και απαιτούν πολλές ώρες για να μάθει κανείς να τα χειρίζεται. Αυτό αναγκάζει τους περισσότερους αγρότες να βασίζονται στην ειδικότητα τεχνικών επισκευών που επίσης κοστίζουν πολλά χρήματα.

Έπειτα ήρθε ο Covid. Ήταν μια στρεσογόνος περίοδος. Έχετε παρατηρήσει τι έχει αλλάξει κατά τη διάρκεια, μετά ή ως αποτέλεσμα του Covid; Καθώς αλληλεπιδρώ με άλλους, συχνά κάποιος θα πει ότι αυτό ή εκείνο είναι διαφορετικό από τότε του Covid. Είμαι μόνο εγώ, ή από τότε του Covid το κοινό είναι λιγότερο φιλικό και πιο ιδιωτικό στις συναναστροφές του; Ας ελέγξουμε τις δικές μας αλληλεπιδράσεις για να εξασφαλίσουμε ότι εξακολουθούμε να είμαστε το «φως» και το «αλάτι» του Θεού σε αυτόν τον σκοτεινό κόσμο, και ότι δεν χάνουμε την «αλμυρότητά» μας. Επίσης, υπάρχουν πινακίδες «ζητείται εργασία» παντού. Γιατί; Μου φαίνεται ότι ο Covid έχει ενθαρρύνει ώστε το λίγο εργασιακό ήθος που ακόμη άνθιζε στην κοινωνία μας να μειωθεί ακόμη περισσότερο.

Έπειτα υπάρχει το θέμα των κινητών τηλεφώνων και των ηλεκτρικών ποδηλάτων. Τι κοινό έχουν αυτά τα δύο ασύνδετα προϊόντα; Από την οπτική γωνία μου, παρατηρώντας τους Αμίσους της κομητείας Χολμς, αυτά τα δύο αντικείμενα έχουν αλλάξει ένα λαό και μια κουλτούρα με πιο σημαντικό τρόπο από σχεδόν οτιδήποτε άλλο τα τελευταία χρόνια.

Πού μας αφήνουν όλα αυτά; Ο συγγραφέας προς Εβραίους λέει ότι Διότι εάν μετατεθεί η ιεροσύνη, χρειάζεται και αλλαγή νόμου – Εβραίους 7:12. Έτσι, βλέπουμε ότι ο Θεός άλλαξε πράγματα όπως Αυτός ευδόκησε· επομένως, αν χρειαζόμαστε αλλαγή για να γίνουμε πιο βιβλικοί, θα πρέπει να την επιφέρουμε. Αλλά ο Απόστολος Παύλος λέει Ώστε να μη είμεθα πλέον νήπιοι, κλυδωνισθήσονται και περιφερώμενοι από παντός ανέμου διδασκαλίας… – Προς Εφεσίους 4:14.

Καί διότι η ανομία πληθυνθήσεται, η δε αγάπη των πολλών θα κρυώσει. Όστις δε αντέξη έως τέλους, ούτος σωθήσεται – Κατά Ματθαίον 24:12-13. Άρα, ας είμαστε εγρήγοροι σε αυτούς τους έσχατους καιρούς καθώς οι αλλαγές συμβαίνουν όλο και περισσότερο γύρω μας. Είθε να είμαστε ανάμεσα σε εκείνους που θα αντέξουν μέχρι το τέλος.
